a-posteriori.kurz: What holds after the data? The a posteriori distribution arises when the prior is combined with the data. It says how plausible each value of a parameter now is. Mean and intervals are read from it.
a-posteriori.beispiel: Prior Beta(2, 2), then 14 successes in 20: Beta(16, 8). The mean of this distribution is 0.67.
a-posteriori.vorsicht: With more data, the influence of the prior shrinks. With little data it remains clearly visible.

a-priori.kurz: What is assumed before the data are in? The a priori distribution states which values of a parameter are considered more or less plausible in advance. It sums up prior knowledge or deliberate restraint.
a-priori.beispiel: For a proportion p, Beta(2, 2) is chosen in advance: mean 0.5, values close to 0 and close to 1 count as less plausible.
a-priori.vorsicht: The prior is an openly stated assumption, not a proof. Comparing results under other priors shows whether they depend on it.

a-priori-power.kurz: How many cases does a test need to find an expected effect? An a priori power analysis calculates, before the study, the required sample size from the significance level, the desired power and the assumed effect size.
a-priori-power.beispiel: t test for two independent groups, d = 0.5, α = 0.05 two-sided, power 0.80: 64 persons per group (63.8 rounded up).
a-priori-power.vorsicht: The assumed effect size is an assumption. If the true effect is smaller, the sample size will not suffice.

a-priori-wendung.kurz: Latin for “from what comes before”. It means fixed in advance, before the data are seen. Hypotheses, sample size and analysis plan should be set a priori. Opposite: post hoc.
a-priori-wendung.beispiel: The sample size of 60 was set a priori, before the first measurement.

abab-design.kurz: A single-case design: one person goes alternately through phases without (A) and with (B) the intervention. If behaviour improves in B and falls back in the next A phase, this supports an effect of the intervention.
abab-design.beispiel: A child disrupts in four phases: no plan, plan, no plan, plan. Disruptions fall in each plan phase and rise again without the plan.
abab-design.vorsicht: It assumes that behaviour goes back after the intervention is withdrawn. With learning, or with interventions whose withdrawal would be unacceptable, this does not work.

abduktiv.kurz: From Latin abducere: “to lead away”. Reasoning to the best explanation: from an observation, the cause that explains it best is suspected. That is a hunch, not evidence; it must be tested on new data.
abduktiv.beispiel: Unusually many absences in winter: a flu wave is suspected. That must be tested on new data.

abhaengigenquote.kurz: The ratio of persons in age groups that are mostly not in work (under 15 and from 65) to persons of working age (15 to 64). It is often stated per 100 persons of working age.
abhaengigenquote.beispiel: 1800 children, 2200 older persons and 6000 persons of working age: (1800 + 2200)/6000 = 0.67, that is 67 per 100.
abhaengigenquote.vorsicht: The age limits are conventions. Not every person aged 15 to 64 works, and not every older person is dependent.

ablehnungsbereich.kurz: From which value of the test statistic on is H₀ rejected? The rejection region (critical region) contains all values that together occur with probability α only if H₀ is true. If the observed value falls inside, H₀ is rejected.
ablehnungsbereich.beispiel: Two-sided t test, 38 degrees of freedom, α = 0.05: the rejection region is t < -2.024 and t > 2.024.
ablehnungsbereich.vorsicht: The rejection region depends on α, the degrees of freedom and the direction of the hypothesis.

ableitung.kurz: The slope of a function at a point. Where the derivative is zero, a maximum or minimum can lie. It is therefore used to determine estimates, such as maximum likelihood and least squares.
ableitung.beispiel: f(x) = -(x - 3)² + 9 has the derivative -2(x - 3). It is zero at x = 3. There lies the maximum, the value 9.
ableitung.vorsicht: A derivative of zero can also mean a minimum or a saddle point. This has to be checked separately.

absolut-relativ.kurz: From Latin absolutus “detached” and relativus “relating to”. Absolute: the count or amount itself. Relative: in relation to something, as a proportion or percent. Both are usually best stated together.

absolute-haeufigkeit.kurz: How many cases are there? The absolute frequency is the counted number of cases with a given value. It depends on the total, so it compares groups of different sizes poorly.
absolute-haeufigkeit.beispiel: 7 of 25 children in class A and 8 of 30 in class B have a pet: 7 and 8 compare badly, 0.28 and 0.27 compare well.

absolutes-risiko.kurz: How often does an event actually occur? Absolute risk is the share of people in whom it occurs within a given period. It is the basis for risk difference, relative risk and NNT.
absolutes-risiko.beispiel: 12 of 400 people experience the event: absolute risk 12 / 400 = 0.03, that is, 3%.
absolutes-risiko.vorsicht: Statements like ‘the risk is halved’ say little without the absolute risk. Going from 2% to 1% is different from going from 40% to 20%.

abweichungsquadrat.kurz: How far is a single value from the mean, ignoring the sign? The squared deviation is (value minus mean) squared. Squaring makes everything positive, and large deviations count disproportionately.
abweichungsquadrat.beispiel: Mean 5: the value 9 has (9 - 5)² = 16, the value 6 has (6 - 5)² = 1.
abweichungsquadrat.vorsicht: Without squaring (or absolute value) the deviations cancel: their sum around the mean is always 0.

access-panel.kurz: A pool of people who have agreed to take part in surveys repeatedly. Participants for single surveys are drawn from it. It is often not a random sample of the population.
access-panel.beispiel: A market research institute has 50 000 panel members and invites 2000 of them to a survey.
access-panel.vorsicht: Panel members differ from non-members, for example through more internet use. Their answers cannot be transferred to the population without further steps.

acf.kurz: How similar are values that lie a given distance apart? The ACF shows the correlation of a series with itself for each distance (lag) 1, 2, 3 and so on. This makes relationships over time visible.
acf.beispiel: Series 2, 4, 3, 5, 6, 8, 7, 9: autocorrelation at lag 1 about 0.48, at lag 2 about 0.39.
acf.vorsicht: With a trend, autocorrelations are high and fall only slowly. The series should be made stationary first.

ad-hoc.kurz: Latin for “to this” (purpose). Introduced for the single case, not planned in advance. An ad hoc decision made after seeing the data can distort results, because it may be tailored to chance patterns.
ad-hoc.beispiel: Excluding values above 100 only after looking at the data would be an ad hoc decision.

adaptives-design.kurz: A study plan that may be changed according to rules fixed in advance, using interim data. Examples are adjusting the sample size or dropping a group. Because the rules are set beforehand, the type I error stays controllable.
adaptives-design.beispiel: Halfway through, the spread is larger than planned. By the rule fixed in advance, the sample size is increased.
adaptives-design.vorsicht: Changes made after an unplanned look at the results invalidate the tests.

adaptives-testen.kurz: The test adapts while it is taken: after each answer the next task is chosen to match the estimated trait level. A few tasks are enough for a precise measurement.
adaptives-testen.beispiel: Someone who solves the first tasks correctly gets harder ones. Someone who does not gets easier ones. The test ends when the measurement error is small enough.
adaptives-testen.vorsicht: A large item pool calibrated in advance is needed. The items must fit a model of item response theory.

additionssatz.kurz: The probability that A or B (or both) occurs is that of A plus that of B minus the probability that both occur. Without the subtraction the overlap would be counted twice.

adjustieren.kurz: From French ajuster: “to fit”. To remove the influence of further variables by calculation. An adjusted value holds at equal values of these variables. Adjustment is a calculation and no substitute for random assignment.
adjustieren.beispiel: The difference between two groups adjusted for age is the difference at equal age.

adjustierter-mittelwert.kurz: What mean would the group have if all groups stood equal on the control variables? The adjusted mean is the model's prediction for this group at the means of all covariates. It makes groups comparable that differ on the covariates.
adjustierter-mittelwert.beispiel: mtcars, fuel use by number of cylinders, controlled for weight and horsepower (at weight 3.22 and 147 hp): adjusted means 22.2 (4 cylinders), 18.9 (6) and 19.0 (8) miles per gallon.
adjustierter-mittelwert.vorsicht: If the slopes of the covariate differ between the groups, there is no single adjusted difference: it then depends on the value of the covariate.
sw: estimated marginal mean at covariate mean
adjustierter-mittelwert.statable: In the analysis of covariance: the table “Adjusted means” with standard error and 95% interval, at the means of all chosen control variables (up to four).

adjustierung.kurz: What remains of a relationship when other quantities are held equal? Adjusting (controlling) means adding further quantities to the model, so that the predictor's coefficient holds for equal values of these quantities.
adjustierung.beispiel: Difference in blood pressure between active and inactive people: crude -6 mmHg, adjusted for age -2 mmHg.
adjustierung.vorsicht: Adjustment covers only what was measured. Adjusting for a collider or a mediator can distort the result.

aequidistant.kurz: From Latin aequus “equal” and distare “to be apart”: at equal distances. An interval scale is equidistant: equal differences mean equal differences in the trait. For response options this is often assumed but not assured.
aequidistant.beispiel: On the Celsius scale the step from 10 to 11 degrees is the same size as from 20 to 21 degrees.

aequivalent.kurz: From Latin aequus “equal” and valere “to be worth”: of equal value. In statistics an equivalence test checks whether a difference lies within limits set in advance. A non-significant difference test does not yet show equivalence.
aequivalent.beispiel: Two measuring devices count as equivalent if their mean difference is at most 1 unit.

aequivalenzeinkommen.kurz: The household income divided by a factor that takes household size into account. By the modified OECD scale the first adult counts 1.0, each further person aged 14 or over 0.5 and each child under 14 counts 0.3.
aequivalenzeinkommen.beispiel: Two adults and two children under 14 have an income of 4200. Weight 1 + 0.5 + 0.3 + 0.3 = 2.1, equivalised income 4200/2.1 = 2000.
aequivalenzeinkommen.vorsicht: The weights are conventions. Other scales lead to other values and can change poverty rates.

aequivalenztest.kurz: Are two groups practically the same? The equivalence test checks whether a difference lies within bounds set in advance. TOST (two one-sided tests) tests twice one-sided: is the difference above the lower bound and below the upper bound?
aequivalenztest.beispiel: Bounds ±2 mmHg, difference 0.5, standard error 0.6, 58 degrees of freedom: p = 0.00005 and p = 0.0076. The larger value is below 0.05, so equivalence is shown.
aequivalenztest.vorsicht: A non-significant ordinary test does not show equality. The bounds must be justified on substantive grounds and set before the analysis.

aetiologie.kurz: From Greek aitia “cause” and logos “study”: the study of causes, mainly of diseases. In statistics the question is which factors contribute to an outcome. An association alone does not yet show a cause.
aetiologie.beispiel: Case-control studies look for clues to the aetiology of rare diseases.

aft.kurz: How does a characteristic change the survival time itself? The AFT model describes by what factor a characteristic stretches or shrinks the time to the event. It is an alternative to Cox regression.
aft.beispiel: Time ratio 1.5: times to the event are 50% longer in the treatment group.
aft.vorsicht: A time ratio is something different from a hazard ratio. The value 1.5 means longer for a time ratio, more frequent for a hazard ratio.

aggregation.kurz: Several rows are combined into one, usually per group or person. A summary is formed, such as mean, sum or count. Many single rows become a smaller table.
aggregation.beispiel: 30 rows with 3 measurements per person (10 people) become 10 rows with the mean per person.
aggregation.vorsicht: Statements about groups cannot simply be carried over to individuals. The spread within the groups is lost.

aggregiert.kurz: From Latin aggregare: “to add, to join together”. Aggregated data summarise single values, for example as sums, means or proportions per group. Relations between groups do not automatically hold for the single people within them.
aggregiert.beispiel: Instead of 300 single grades, only the average per class is available: aggregated data.

aic.kurz: Which model fits best without needing too many parameters? AIC = 2k - 2 ln L with k parameters and the likelihood L. Smaller is better. A single value has no meaning, only comparisons on the same data set.
aic.beispiel: The same 8 people: AIC 43.5 with study hours, 41.9 with practice tasks added. The difference is 1.6.
aic.vorsicht: Only models with the same outcome and the same cases can be compared. The AIC does not say whether the best model is good.

aipe.kurz: A kind of sample size planning that aims not at power but at the width of the confidence interval: how many cases are needed for the interval to be at most a certain width?
aipe.beispiel: A mean with a spread of 10 is to be accurate to ±2 (95 %): n = (1.96 · 10/2)² = 96.04, so 97 people.
aipe.vorsicht: The width is only reached on average, since the spread itself is estimated. For certainty, a margin is added.

akquieszenz.kurz: Yes-saying: the tendency to agree with statements regardless of their content.
akquieszenz.beispiel: A person agrees with the statement 'I like being with people' and equally with the statement 'I prefer being alone'.
akquieszenz.vorsicht: One remedy: word some of the items in reverse and reverse-code them when scoring.

algorithmus.kurz: A clear sequence of steps that solves a task. A computer carries it out exactly as written. Every calculation in a statistics program follows an algorithm.
algorithmus.beispiel: Mean: add up all values, divide the sum by the number of values.
algorithmus.vorsicht: For the same quantity there are sometimes several accepted algorithms. For example, programs give slightly different quantiles for small n.

alpha-kumulierung.kurz: How does the risk of a false alarm grow when many tests are run? Each additional test raises the probability that at least one becomes significant by mistake. This is called alpha accumulation or alpha inflation.
alpha-kumulierung.beispiel: 10 independent tests, each α = 0.05, H₀ true every time: with probability 1 - 0.95¹⁰ = 0.40 at least one test is significant.
alpha-kumulierung.vorsicht: The 0.40 holds for independent tests with all null hypotheses true. With dependent tests the value differs.

alternativhypothese.kurz: What holds if the null hypothesis does not? The alternative hypothesis H₁ (also H_A) states a difference, an association or an effect. It can be directional or non-directional.
alternativhypothese.beispiel: H₁: Mean blood pressure differs between the groups, the difference is not 0 mmHg.
alternativhypothese.vorsicht: Rejecting H₀ does not confirm every conceivable H₁. It only shows that the data fit H₀ poorly.

alternierendes-behandlungsdesign.kurz: A single-case design in which two or more interventions change quickly in random or balanced order, for example from session to session. The courses under the interventions are compared.
alternierendes-behandlungsdesign.beispiel: A person practises words with two methods that change randomly from day to day. The learning curves are compared.
alternierendes-behandlungsdesign.vorsicht: The effects must not influence each other (carry-over). A separate baseline phase is not needed.

analog.kurz: From Greek analogos: “corresponding”. In statistics texts, “calculated analogously” means by the same pattern, with other numbers or groups. In arguments it can also mean “by correspondence”.
analog.beispiel: The test for paired data is calculated analogously to the one-sample test, namely on the differences.

analyseplan.kurz: A document that fixes before the analysis how the data will be analysed: outcomes, methods, handling of missing values, subgroups. It protects against choosing analyses after seeing the results.
analyseplan.beispiel: The plan names the value at 12 weeks as the main outcome and an analysis of covariance with the baseline value as the method.
analyseplan.vorsicht: A plan written after looking at the data does not give this protection.

ancova.kurz: Do groups still differ when a background variable is held constant? Analysis of covariance is an analysis of variance that removes the influence of a numeric background variable (covariate). The adjusted means are then compared.
ancova.beispiel: Suppose: Post-test by group with pre-test as covariate: raw means 61.4 and 68.2 (F(1, 8) = 1.93; p = 0.20), adjusted 62.37 and 67.23 (F(1, 7) = 42.4; p = 0.0003).
ancova.vorsicht: It assumes the covariate relates to the outcome equally strongly in all groups. A covariate cannot replace random assignment.
ancova.statable: At “Do groups differ?” choose the groups, then under “More ways” one to four control variables. The result shows Type III tests, adjusted means and the test of equal slopes.

anderson-darling.kurz: Do the tails of the distribution deviate? Like Kolmogorov-Smirnov, the Anderson-Darling test checks whether data fit a distribution, but gives more weight to the ends of the distribution. It is therefore more sensitive to departures there.
anderson-darling.beispiel: The 11 waiting times 1, 1, 2, 2, 2, 3, 3, 4, 5, 9, 14: A² = 1.08, p = 0.005 against a normal distribution with estimated parameters.
anderson-darling.vorsicht: As with any normality test, the result depends strongly on sample size. It does not replace a plot.

angepasstes-residuum.kurz: Which cell really deviates? The adjusted residual divides observed minus expected by the spread expected for exactly this cell under independence, taking the margins into account. It is roughly standard normal: absolute values above 1.96 stand out.
angepasstes-residuum.beispiel: Hair colour and eye colour in 279 men: black hair with brown eyes occurs 32 times, 19.7 are expected; adjusted residual 3.86.
angepasstes-residuum.vorsicht: With many cells, some exceed 1.96 by chance alone; the Bonferroni limit is stricter. Conspicuous cells show a direction, not a cause.

ankereffekt.kurz: A number named first influences later estimates and judgements, even if it is random. In surveys, examples and given values distort the answers.
ankereffekt.beispiel: Someone first asked “More than 5 hours per day?” then names higher times than someone first asked “More than 1 hour?”.
ankereffekt.vorsicht: The effect is robust and is not avoided even by experts. Open questions without a given number reduce it.

annahmestichprobe.kurz: A method of quality inspection. A sample is checked from a lot. If the number of defective items is at most a fixed acceptance number, the lot is accepted, otherwise rejected.
annahmestichprobe.beispiel: Plan: check 50 items, accept at most 1 defective. At a 2 % defect rate the lot is accepted with probability 0.74, at 10 % with only 0.03.
annahmestichprobe.vorsicht: The acceptance probability depends on the true defect rate. Only the curve over it (OC curve) shows how sharply the plan separates.

anonymisierung.kurz: Anonymisation removes or alters information so that a person can no longer be identified. Pseudonymisation replaces names with codes (pseudonyms), but a linking list still exists and can make the persons recognisable again.
anonymisierung.beispiel: In a dataset, the name is replaced by the number 4711. As long as the list “4711 = Ms Sample” exists, it is only pseudonymised.
anonymisierung.vorsicht: Even without names, combinations of characteristics can identify. Anonymous means that re-identification is not possible with reasonable effort.

anova-messwiederholung.kurz: Do the same people change across several measurements? Repeated-measures analysis of variance compares the means of three or more time points or conditions in the same cases. Differences between the people are removed.
anova-messwiederholung.beispiel: 5 people, 3 time points, means 7, 8.6 and 10.2: F(2, 8) = 96.0; p < 0.001.
anova-messwiederholung.vorsicht: Measurements of the same person are related. Sphericity is therefore checked, and the degrees of freedom are corrected if it is violated.

anova-tabelle.kurz: How do I read the result of an analysis of variance? The table shows, for each source of spread (factor, interaction, error), the sum of squares, the degrees of freedom, the mean square, the F value and the p value.
anova-tabelle.beispiel: Group row: sum of squares 32, degrees of freedom 2, MS 16, F 24, p = 0.00025. Error row: 6, 9, 0.667.
anova-tabelle.vorsicht: The error row (also residual, within) has neither F nor p. It supplies the denominator for the F values of the other rows.

anteil.kurz: What part does something make up? A proportion is a part divided by the whole, a number between 0 and 1. Multiplied by 100 it becomes a percentage.
anteil.vorsicht: Without stating the whole, a proportion cannot be read: 30% of which trips?

anti-image-korrelationsmatrix.kurz: Which question hardly relates to the others? The anti-image correlation matrix holds the negative partial correlations of each two questions with all the others taken out. The diagonal holds the KMO per question (MSA). Large values off the diagonal speak against a factor analysis.
anti-image-korrelationsmatrix.beispiel: Ten bfi questions (A1 to A5, C1 to C5, 2,632 people): overall KMO .78; on the diagonal A1 has .73 and C3 has .83.
anti-image-korrelationsmatrix.vorsicht: A diagonal value below .50 suggests dropping the question, but check the content first. The values off the diagonal should be small; this is a hint, not a test.

antwortstil.kurz: A fixed tendency to choose response options regardless of content. Examples are agreeing, choosing the extremes, or preferring the middle. It distorts means and relations.
antwortstil.beispiel: A person ticks the highest or lowest option for almost every question, whatever the question says.
antwortstil.vorsicht: Response styles differ between persons and groups. A group comparison can therefore partly reflect the response style.

approximation.kurz: From Latin approximare: “to come close”. An approximation is a simpler calculation that only comes close to the exact value. It is usually good when the sample is large.
approximation.beispiel: For large n, the binomial distribution is approximated by the normal distribution.

ar-modell.kurz: A time series model in which each value is predicted from the previous values plus a random remainder. AR(1): y_t = c + φ · y_{t-1} + e_t. It is stationary if |φ| < 1. The autocorrelation falls as φ^k.
ar-modell.beispiel: φ = 0.6 and c = 2: the mean is 2/(1 - 0.6) = 5. The autocorrelation is 0.6 at lag 1 and 0.36 at lag 2.
ar-modell.vorsicht: When φ is close to 1 the series is nearly a random walk. The order is chosen from the partial autocorrelation.

arbitraer.kurz: From Latin arbitrarius: “at will”. Set at will, not grounded in the matter itself. In statistics, class limits or the choice of α = 0.05, a habit, are arbitrary.
arbitraer.beispiel: The age limits 18, 30, 50 are arbitrary: other limits give other bars.

arch.kurz: Models for time series whose spread is not constant but depends on the recent swings. Large swings are often followed by more (volatility clustering). ARCH explains the variance from past squared errors, GARCH also from past variances.
arch.beispiel: σ²_t = 0.1 + 0.5 · ε²_{t-1}. After a swing of ε = 2 the variance is 0.1 + 0.5 · 4 = 2.1, after a swing of 0 only 0.1.
arch.vorsicht: The models describe the spread, not the direction. They are mostly used for financial data.

arima.kurz: How can a series be explained by its own past? ARIMA(p, d, q) combines three parts: p past values (autoregressive), d-fold differencing and q past random deviations (moving average). The model is used for description and forecasting.
arima.beispiel: ARIMA(1, 1, 0): the change from one month to the next depends on the previous month's change.
arima.vorsicht: The model needs a series that is stationary after differencing. A well-fitting model does not necessarily give good forecasts.

arithmetisches-mittel.kurz: What is the average? The arithmetic mean is the sum of all values divided by their number. It is the centre in the sense of a balance point: deviations above and below cancel out.
arithmetisches-mittel.beispiel: Waiting times 3, 4, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9, 10, 40: the sum is 96, divided by 10 gives 9.6.
arithmetisches-mittel.vorsicht: A single extreme value pulls the mean strongly: without the 40 it would be 6.2.

arkussinus.kurz: A conversion for proportions between 0 and 1: arcsin(√p). It stabilises the spread of proportions and stretches the edges near 0 and 1.
arkussinus.vorsicht: For proportions, logistic regression or a binomial model is usually used today, not this transformation.

armutsquote.kurz: What share of people have very low income compared with the others? The poverty rate is the share of people whose income lies below a threshold. A threshold of 60% of the median income is often used.
armutsquote.beispiel: Median 2,000, threshold 60% = 1,200. Of 200 people, 18 lie below it: rate 18 / 200 = 9%.
armutsquote.vorsicht: The rate depends on the threshold and on the income concept, such as income weighted by household size; with a threshold set as a percentage of the median, it stays the same if all incomes rise equally. It says nothing about how far below the threshold those affected are.

artefakt.kurz: An apparent finding that does not lie in the matter itself but arose from the measuring method, the analysis or the study design. From Latin ars (art) and factum (made): something made by humans.
artefakt.beispiel: An instrument shows higher values in one group because it was set differently there. The group difference is an artefact.
artefakt.vorsicht: An artefact can often be recognised only by repeating with a different method. A conspicuous finding does not imply a real effect.

assoziation.kurz: From Latin associare: “to join”. A relation between two variables, without saying which causes which. For categories, “association” is often said instead of “correlation”.
assoziation.beispiel: Smoking and coughing are associated: people who smoke cough more often.

asymptotisch.kurz: Does the approximation hold with little data? An asymptotic method relies on a distribution that the test statistic approaches only as sample size grows. In small samples the p value can be clearly off.
asymptotisch.beispiel: 9 heads in 10 tosses: the normal approximation (without continuity correction) gives z = 2.53 and p = 0.011, the exact value is p = 0.021.
asymptotisch.vorsicht: For χ² tests it is often said that expected counts should be at least 5. There is no fixed minimum n; it depends on the method.

asymptotische-normalitaet.kurz: In large samples many estimators, especially maximum likelihood estimators, are approximately normally distributed around the true value, with a variance given by the Fisher information. Wald intervals and many tests come from it.
asymptotische-normalitaet.beispiel: The proportion p̂ = 0.3 from n = 100 is approximately normally distributed around the true proportion with standard deviation √(0.3 · 0.7/100) = 0.046.
asymptotische-normalitaet.vorsicht: “Large enough” depends on the case. With rare events or proportions near 0 or 1, far more observations are needed.

asymptotischer-standardfehler.kurz: A standard error derived from theory for large samples. It holds approximately and gets better the larger n is. Many programs show it for association measures of cross tables.
asymptotischer-standardfehler.beispiel: Kappa = 0.60 with asymptotic standard error 0.08: the 95 % interval is 0.60 ± 1.96 · 0.08, that is 0.44 to 0.76.
asymptotischer-standardfehler.vorsicht: With small samples or values near the limit (0 or 1) the value can be inexact. Exact methods or the bootstrap are then better.

ate.kurz: The ATE is the mean effect of a treatment over all persons in the population. The ATT applies only to those actually treated. The LATE applies to the group whose treatment can be changed by an instrument (compliers).
ate.beispiel: In a randomised trial the treatment group has a mean of 60, the control group 52. The estimated ATE is 8.
ate.vorsicht: The three effects differ when the effect varies between persons. Which is meant has to be stated.

attenuation.kurz: How strong would the relationship be without measurement error? Measurement error weakens the observed correlation. The correction scales it up using the reliabilities of both measures to the value without error: r / √(rel.x · rel.y).
attenuation.vorsicht: The result can exceed 1 and is only as good as the estimated reliabilities. It is an estimate, not an observed value.

attributables-risiko.kurz: The part of the risk among the exposed that is attributed to the exposure, if the relation is causal. As a difference: risk among the exposed minus risk among the unexposed. As a share: this difference divided by the risk among the exposed.
attributables-risiko.beispiel: Risk among the exposed 0.20, among the unexposed 0.05. Difference 0.15, attributable fraction among the exposed 0.15/0.20 = 75 %.
attributables-risiko.vorsicht: Reading it as a preventable share requires that the relation is causal and not distorted by third variables.

attributkarte.titel: Attribute control chart (p, np, c, u chart)
attributkarte.kurz: A control chart for counted characteristics. The p chart shows the proportion of defective units, the np chart their number. The c chart counts defects per unit, the u chart defects per unit when the size varies. The limits follow the binomial or Poisson distribution.
attributkarte.beispiel: With p = 0.04 and samples of n = 100, the upper limit of the p chart is 0.04 + 3 · √(0.04 · 0.96/100) = 0.099. The lower one would be -0.019 and is set to 0.
attributkarte.vorsicht: With small n the limits are only rough. Very large samples can make the chart too sensitive.

attrition.kurz: Loss of participants during the course of a study (drop-out). If those who left differ from those who remain, the results are distorted.
attrition.beispiel: Of 200 people, 140 remain after one year: 60 dropped out, that is 30%.
attrition.vorsicht: What matters is not only the number but whether the loss is related to a characteristic or to the outcome.

augenscheinvaliditaet.kurz: The impression, on looking at a test or questionnaire, that it measures what it should. It says something about acceptance by participants, not about actual measurement quality.
augenscheinvaliditaet.beispiel: A test of arithmetic skill contains arithmetic tasks. It looks valid.
augenscheinvaliditaet.vorsicht: Face validity is no evidence of validity. A test can look valid and not be, or the other way round.

auspraegung.kurz: Which values can a characteristic take? A value, level or category is one single possible outcome of a characteristic.
auspraegung.beispiel: Characteristic blood group: A, B, AB and O are four values. Characteristic die face: the values 1 to 6.

ausreisser-regel.kurz: When is a value considered unusual? By Tukey's rule a value is unusual if it lies below Q1 minus 1.5 · IQR or above Q3 plus 1.5 · IQR. Box plots draw such values as single points.
ausreisser-regel.vorsicht: The rule only flags values and does not say the value is wrong. The factor 1.5 is a habit; first check whether it is a data entry error.

auswahlbias.kurz: Is taking part made harder for certain persons? Selection bias arises when the way of selecting favours or excludes certain groups. The result then departs systematically from the true value.
auswahlbias.beispiel: A purely online survey about internet use reaches only people with access. The share is estimated too high.
auswahlbias.vorsicht: More cases do not fix this. A huge biased sample only gives a precise wrong result.

auswahlsatz.kurz: The sampling fraction is the sample size n divided by the population size N. When sampling without replacement, the standard error becomes smaller with a large sampling fraction.
auswahlsatz.beispiel: 500 of 2000: sampling fraction 0.25. The standard error shrinks by the factor √0.75 = 0.866.
auswahlsatz.vorsicht: With a small sampling fraction (under 5% is often mentioned) it can usually be ignored. Then n matters, hardly the fraction.

auswaschphase.kurz: A pause between two treatments in a crossover design. The effect of the first is meant to fade before the second begins.
auswaschphase.beispiel: Two weeks without medication lie between two painkillers.
auswaschphase.vorsicht: If the pause is too short, a carry-over effect arises.

autokorrelation.kurz: Is a value related to earlier values of the same series? Autocorrelation is the correlation of a series with itself, shifted by a number of steps (lag). In regression it means residuals that are related to their predecessors.
autokorrelation.beispiel: The values 48, 55, 53, 62, 66, 64, 75, 78 as daily values: the lag-1 autocorrelation is 0.52 by the usual formula.
autokorrelation.vorsicht: Consecutive measurements are not independent. Standard errors and tests that assume independence come out too optimistic with positive autocorrelation.

ave.kurz: The share of the items' variance that the latent variable explains on average. It is computed as the mean of the squared standardised loadings. The rest is measurement error.
ave.beispiel: Loadings 0.8, 0.7, 0.6: (0.64 + 0.49 + 0.36) / 3 = 0.497. About half of the item variance goes back to the latent variable.
ave.vorsicht: From 0.5 the AVE is often named as sufficient, which is a habit. It belongs to convergent validity.

axiom.kurz: A basic assumption laid down without proof, from which everything else is derived. In probability, the Kolmogorov axioms hold: probabilities are never negative, the certain event has probability 1, and mutually exclusive events add up.
axiom.beispiel: From the axiom “probabilities are never negative” it follows that no event can have a negative chance.
axiom.vorsicht: An axiom is set, not proven. It can be sensible or less sensible, but not “wrong” in the sense of a calculation error.

balanced-accuracy.kurz: The mean of sensitivity and specificity. It is the hit rate that weights both groups equally, even if one group is much smaller than the other.
balanced-accuracy.beispiel: Sensitivity 0.80, specificity 0.90: the balanced accuracy is (0.80 + 0.90)/2 = 0.85.
balanced-accuracy.vorsicht: It says nothing about predictive values, and these depend on how common the disease is.

balanciert.kurz: Are all groups the same size? A design is called balanced when every cell (combination of factor levels) has the same number of cases. The effects can then be computed independently of each other.
balanciert.beispiel: 2 × 2 cells with 3 plants each, 12 in all: balanced. With 3, 3, 3 and 5 plants: unbalanced.
balanciert.vorsicht: Missing values can turn a planned balanced design into an unbalanced one. The results then depend on the type of sum of squares.

balkendiagramm.kurz: How many are there per category? A horizontal bar chart shows one lying bar per category, whose length gives the frequency, proportion or mean. Handy when category names are long.
balkendiagramm.beispiel: Favourite fruit of 25 people: four bars of length 10, 8, 4 and 3.
balkendiagramm.vorsicht: The axis should start at 0, otherwise the length ratios deceive. There are gaps between the bars: the categories are separate, unlike in a histogram.

barnard-boschloo.titel: Barnard and Boschloo tests (unconditional exact tests)
barnard-boschloo.kurz: Exact tests for the two-by-two table that, unlike the Fisher test, do not hold both margins fixed but only the group sizes. They use α better and often have more power. The Boschloo test is a more powerful variant of the Fisher test.
barnard-boschloo.beispiel: Two groups of 12 people each, 3 and 9 successes. The Fisher test gives p = 0.039, the Boschloo test p = 0.023.
barnard-boschloo.vorsicht: They need more computation. The Fisher test remains the usual standard, especially when the margins are fixed by the design.

basisjahr.kurz: To which point in time do all values refer? The base year is the point in time whose index value is set to 100. All other values are related to it.
basisjahr.beispiel: Base year 2020 = 100, in 2024 the index is 118: the value is 18% above that of 2020.
basisjahr.vorsicht: If the base year is changed, all index values change, but the rates of change do not. Series with different base years must not be compared directly.

basisrate.kurz: The share of a characteristic in the whole group before extra information such as a test result is added. It determines how much a test result says.
basisrate.beispiel: With a base rate of 1 %, 20 of 2000 people are affected. If the test detects 90 % of those affected and falsely flags 5 % of the others, only 18 of 117 positives are affected.
basisrate.vorsicht: Overlooking the base rate is called the base rate fallacy. The share of true cases among positives depends strongly on it.

baumdiagramm.kurz: A drawing in which each branching shows one step of a random experiment. The branches carry probabilities. Along a path they are multiplied, paths of the same kind are added.
baumdiagramm.beispiel: Urn with 3 red and 2 blue balls, two draws without replacement: path red-red = 3/5 · 2/4 = 0.3.

bayes-faktor.kurz: How much better do the data fit one hypothesis than another? The Bayes factor compares how probable the observed data would be under each of the two hypotheses. BF₁₀ = 6 means: the data are six times as probable under H₁ as under H₀.
bayes-faktor.beispiel: 10 coin tosses, heads 9 times. H₀: the coin is fair. H₁: every heads rate between 0 and 1 is equally plausible. Result: BF₁₀ = 9.31.
bayes-faktor.vorsicht: The Bayes factor is not the probability of a hypothesis; that only follows after multiplying it by the odds before the data. It depends on the prior under H₁, and labels such as ‘moderate’ or ‘strong’ are conventions.

bayes-statistik.kurz: How believable is each value after seeing the data? Bayesian statistics starts with an assumption before the data (the prior), combines it with the data (the likelihood) and arrives at the updated view afterwards (the posterior). Probability here expresses a degree of belief.
bayes-statistik.beispiel: Share of children who solve a task: start with no prior knowledge (Beta(1, 1)), 14 of 20 solve it, afterwards Beta(15, 7) applies with a mean of 0.68.
bayes-statistik.vorsicht: The result also depends on the prior. With little data this can matter a lot, so the prior is always stated openly.

bayessche-aktualisierung.kurz: Combining prior knowledge with new data: posterior odds = prior odds × Bayes factor. The new odds give the new probability. The result serves as the prior next time.
bayessche-aktualisierung.beispiel: The probability of the hypothesis is 0.2 in advance, the odds 1 to 4 (0.25). The Bayes factor is 10. New odds 2.5, probability 2.5/3.5 = 0.71.
bayessche-aktualisierung.vorsicht: The calculation depends on the prior. Someone with a different prior reaches a different result from the same data.

bca.kurz: How does one improve a bootstrap interval for skewed distributions? BCa (bias-corrected and accelerated) shifts the limits of the percentile interval. It corrects for a shift of the bootstrap values relative to the statistic (bias) and allows for skewness through the acceleration.
bca.beispiel: Mean of strongly right-skewed waiting times, 5000 bootstrap samples: the BCa interval may be shifted compared with the percentile interval.
bca.vorsicht: With very small samples BCa is unstable too. The acceleration is usually estimated from jackknife values.

bedingte-verteilung.kurz: The distribution of one variable when the value of another is held fixed. It is obtained by dividing the row or column of the joint distribution by its sum.
bedingte-verteilung.beispiel: Given strong wind (sum 0.3): P(rain | strong) = 0.2 / 0.3 = 0.667, P(no rain | strong) = 0.333.

bedingte-wahrscheinlichkeit.kurz: How likely is A if it is already known that B has occurred? Divide the probability that both occur by that of B. The bar | is read “given”.
bedingte-wahrscheinlichkeit.beispiel: Two dice: P(sum at least 10) = 6/36 = 0.167. Knowing that the first die shows a 6, it is 3/6 = 0.5.
bedingte-wahrscheinlichkeit.vorsicht: P(A | B) and P(B | A) are different quantities and are often confused.

benjamini-hochberg.kurz: How is the false discovery rate controlled with many tests? The Benjamini-Hochberg procedure sorts the p values and multiplies the one with rank i by m / i. Adjusted values may not decrease with rank. Everything below the chosen FDR is rejected.
benjamini-hochberg.beispiel: Five p values 0.004, 0.012, 0.024, 0.200, 0.600 give adjusted 0.02, 0.03, 0.04, 0.25, 0.60. At an FDR of 0.05, three are rejected, with Bonferroni only one.
benjamini-hochberg.vorsicht: The procedure is meant for independent or positively dependent tests. An adjusted value is not an ordinary p value.

beobachterverzerrung.kurz: The person who measures or rates is influenced by knowledge or expectation. Or the groups are examined with unequal thoroughness. Blinding is the remedy.
beobachterverzerrung.beispiel: Someone who knows which children took part in the programme rates their essays more kindly.
beobachterverzerrung.vorsicht: Even a good instrument does not help if the person reading it knows the group and the reading leaves room for judgement.

beobachtete-haeufigkeit.kurz: What was actually counted? The observed frequency is the number counted in a cell. It stands against the expected frequency, which would be expected under independence: row total times column total divided by the grand total.
beobachtete-haeufigkeit.beispiel: Inner district and car: observed 30, expected 100 · 90 / 200 = 45.

beobachtungsstudie.kurz: Things are only observed, nothing is interfered with. The researchers record what happens anyway and compare.
beobachtungsstudie.beispiel: The number of cups of coffee employees drink and how long they sleep are recorded, without changing anything.
beobachtungsstudie.vorsicht: An association does not prove a cause. Unmeasured confounders can explain it.

bernoulli.kurz: A single trial with exactly two outcomes, for example success (1) or no success (0). The Bernoulli distribution has one parameter: the probability of success p. Several such trials together give the binomial distribution.
bernoulli.beispiel: A customer buys with p = 0.3. Expected value 0.3, variance 0.3 · 0.7 = 0.21.

berufs-und-bildungsklassifikation.kurz: International code systems that assign occupations (ISCO), levels of education (ISCED), diseases (ICD) or industries (NACE, ÖNACE in Austria) to categories. They make data from different sources and countries comparable.
berufs-und-bildungsklassifikation.beispiel: A survey records the occupation as text. It is assigned a four-digit code by ISCO. Occupational groups can then be compared across countries.
berufs-und-bildungsklassifikation.vorsicht: The assignment is not always unambiguous, and the code systems are revised from time to time. For comparisons across years the version has to be noted.

besd.kurz: A display that shows a correlation r as the difference between two success rates: 50 % + r/2 versus 50 % - r/2. A small correlation thus becomes vivid.
besd.beispiel: r = 0.30: success rate 65 % in one group, 35 % in the other.
besd.vorsicht: The display assumes an artificial split of 50 %. It does not reproduce the actual rates.

bessel-korrektur.kurz: Why does the variance of a sample divide by n - 1? Deviations are measured from the sample mean, which lies closer to the data than the true mean does. Dividing by n - 1 makes up for that.
bessel-korrektur.beispiel: Values 2, 4, 6: mean 4, sum of squared deviations 8. Dividing by n = 3 gives 2.67, by n - 1 = 2 gives 4 (s = 2).
bessel-korrektur.vorsicht: The correction makes s² unbiased. For a fully observed group with no intent to estimate, one divides by N.

bestaetigungsfehler.kurz: The tendency to seek, interpret and remember information in a way that fits one's own expectation. In analysis it shows when paths are tried until the expectation seems confirmed.
bestaetigungsfehler.beispiel: Someone who expects an effect runs three more analyses after an unclear result and reports the one that fits the expectation.
bestaetigungsfehler.vorsicht: Remedies are an analysis fixed in advance and blinding.

bestimmungsgrenze.kurz: The smallest amount that can not only be detected but also stated numerically with acceptable precision. It lies above the limit of detection. A common rule is ten times the standard deviation of the noise, divided by the slope of the calibration line.
bestimmungsgrenze.vorsicht: The rules differ between fields. Values between the limit of detection and the limit of quantification are detectable but imprecise.

beta-verteilung.kurz: A distribution for values between 0 and 1, such as proportions or probabilities. Two shape parameters decide whether it is bell-shaped, skewed or U-shaped. In Bayesian statistics it often describes the uncertainty about a proportion.
beta-verteilung.beispiel: Beta(2, 8): mean 2 / (2 + 8) = 0.2, median 0.180. The curve is stretched to the right.
beta-verteilung.vorsicht: Not to be confused with the regression weight β or the type II error β. It is only the same name.
beta-verteilung.statable: In the learning lab, tab “Bayes with prior knowledge”: for a proportion the prior is a beta distribution Beta(a, b), the posterior Beta(a + k, b + n − k).

between-subjects.kurz: Different people, different conditions: each person experiences only one condition, and groups are compared.
between-subjects.beispiel: 30 people learn with method A, another 30 with method B. The means of the two groups are compared.
between-subjects.vorsicht: The groups can already differ before the treatment. Random assignment evens this out on average.

bevoelkerungspyramide.kurz: A chart of the age distribution of a population, usually with horizontal bars: men on the left, women on the right, age from bottom to top. It shows birth strength, ageing and breaks such as wars.
bevoelkerungspyramide.beispiel: A wide bottom shows many children, a wide top an ageing population. A mushroom or urn shape is typical of countries with a low birth rate.
bevoelkerungspyramide.vorsicht: The shape is a picture of the present, not a forecast. Migration changes it as well.

bias.kurz: A systematic distortion is a deviation that always goes in the same direction. It does not arise by chance and remains even with very many data.
bias.beispiel: A scale always shows 2 kg too much. The mean of 100 weighings stays 2 kg too high.
bias.vorsicht: Random errors even out in large samples, systematic errors do not.

bias-varianz.kurz: Is a slightly shifted but steady estimator better than an accurate but erratic one? Often yes. An estimator can trade bias (systematic error) against variance (spread). The MSE shows which is better overall.
bias-varianz.beispiel: A: no bias, variance 9, MSE 9. B: bias 1, variance 4, MSE 5. B lies closer to the true value on average.
bias-varianz.vorsicht: Less bias is not automatically better. And smaller variance around a wrong value does not help.

bic.kurz: Like the AIC, but with a stricter penalty in larger samples. BIC = k · ln(n) - 2 ln L. The penalty per parameter is ln(n), so from n = 8 it is larger than 2. Smaller is better, compared on the same data set.
bic.beispiel: The same 8 people: BIC 43.8 with study hours, 42.3 with practice tasks added.
bic.vorsicht: AIC and BIC can prefer different models. Neither proves that a model is true.

bifaktor.kurz: A measurement model with one general factor on which all items load and several specific factors for groups of items. The general and specific factors are uncorrelated.
bifaktor.beispiel: A test has arithmetic, word and figure tasks. All load on a general ability factor, plus one specific factor per task type.
bifaktor.vorsicht: The model fits very easily. A good fit does not show that the general factor has a meaning of its own.

bimodal.kurz: Does the distribution have two peaks? Bimodal means two-peaked: two regions occur clearly more often than their surroundings. Often two groups are hidden in the data.
bimodal.beispiel: Customers of a café by time of day: one peak around 8 a.m., one around 1 p.m.
bimodal.vorsicht: The mean then often lies between the peaks, where there are hardly any cases. In small samples random bumps arise easily and do not mean two groups.

bindung.kurz: Several cases have the same value and so no unique rank. The usual way is to give all of them the mean of the positions they occupy. Many ties change how rank tests are computed, especially exact p-values.
bindung.beispiel: Values 7, 9, 9, 9, 12: the three 9s occupy places 2, 3, 4. They receive rank 3. All ranks: 1, 3, 3, 3, 5.
bindung.vorsicht: With ties, exact p-values often are no longer strictly valid. The approximation then needs a correction for ties.

binomialkoeffizient.kurz: It gives the number of ways to select k things out of n when order does not matter. It is read “n choose k” and equals n! divided by the product of k! and (n - k)!.
binomialkoeffizient.beispiel: Choosing 2 people out of 5: 5 choose 2 = 10. Six numbers out of 49: 13983816.

binomialtest.kurz: Does a proportion differ from an expected proportion? For yes/no outcomes, the binomial test checks whether the hit rate fits an assumed proportion p₀. It computes exactly with the binomial distribution.
binomialtest.beispiel: 15 of 20 people choose variant A. Test against p₀ = 0.5: p = 0.041 (two-sided).
binomialtest.vorsicht: Observations must be independent, and p₀ must be justified in advance. p = 0.041 does not mean the true proportion is 0.5 with 4.1% probability.

binomialverteilung.kurz: How many successes occur in n independent trials if each trial succeeds with the same probability p? The binomial distribution gives the probability of every possible number of successes. The expected value is n · p.
binomialverteilung.beispiel: 20 parts, each with a 10% defect rate: exactly 2 defective parts has probability 0.285. The expected number is 2.
binomialverteilung.vorsicht: It only holds if p stays the same in every trial and trials do not influence each other. For drawing without replacement from small sets, the hypergeometric distribution fits better.

binomische-formel.kurz: Rules for the square of a sum or difference: (a + b)² = a² + 2ab + b² and (a - b)² = a² - 2ab + b². They appear in statistics in the variance of a sum and in rearranging the variance formula.
binomische-formel.vorsicht: The square of a sum is not the sum of the squares: (3 + 2)² = 25, but 3² + 2² = 13.

bivariat.kurz: Exactly two variables are looked at together, usually to describe a relationship or a difference. Typical tools are a scatter plot, a cross table and a correlation.
bivariat.beispiel: For 40 people, sleep duration and a concentration test are shown together in one scatter plot.

blasendiagramm.kurz: A scatterplot in which the size of each point shows a third variable. Two variables are on the axes, the third is in the area of the bubble.
blasendiagramm.beispiel: Each country is a bubble: the x axis shows life expectancy, the y axis income, the bubble area the population.
blasendiagramm.vorsicht: The area, not the diameter, should be proportional to the value. Otherwise large values look exaggerated.

block-hierarchisch.kurz: In what order do predictors enter the model? A block is a group of predictors that is added together. Block 1 often holds control variables. Each further block shows what it adds beyond the previous ones (ΔR², for yes/no the block χ²).
block-hierarchisch.beispiel: Block 1: age and weight of the mother, block 2: smoking and hypertension. Block χ²(2) = 11.44, p = .003: the second block improves the model.
block-hierarchisch.vorsicht: The order of the blocks is a decision made before the calculation, not a search for the best result. The contribution of a block depends on what is already in the model.

blockrandomisierung.kurz: How do the groups keep equal numbers throughout? In block randomisation, assignment is made in small blocks, for example 4 persons. Each block holds each group equally often, with the order inside drawn at random.
blockrandomisierung.beispiel: Block of length 4, two groups: there are 6 possible orders with 2 A and 2 B each, and one is drawn.
blockrandomisierung.vorsicht: With a fixed small block, the last place in a block can become guessable. Varying block lengths and blinding help.

bodeneffekt.kurz: The test is too hard: many reach the lowest possible score, so differences at the bottom can no longer be seen.
bodeneffekt.beispiel: A scale runs from 0 to 20, and 35% of the people score 0. Differences among these people are lost.
bodeneffekt.vorsicht: The spread is cut off, and associations tend to come out too small.

bonferroni.kurz: How does the error rate stay under control with many tests? The Bonferroni correction divides α by the number of tests, or multiplies each p value by it (capped at 1). The chance of at least one type I error then stays below α.
bonferroni.beispiel: 10 tests, α = 0.05: each test must reach p < 0.005. A p of 0.012 becomes 0.12 and is no longer significant.
bonferroni.vorsicht: The method is strict and loses much power with many or dependent tests. Holm is never worse.

boosting.kurz: A machine learning method: many simple models, usually small trees, are built one after another, and each corrects the errors of the previous ones. Together they form a strong model.
boosting.beispiel: A first small tree predicts prices roughly. The second is trained on the errors of the first, the third on what remains. After 500 trees the prediction is much more accurate.
boosting.vorsicht: Too many steps lead to overfitting. Learning rate and number of steps are chosen by cross-validation.

bowker.kurz: The extension of the McNemar test to tables with more than two categories. It tests whether the table of two measurements of the same cases is symmetric, that is whether changes in both directions are equally frequent.
bowker.beispiel: The same people are placed in three levels before and after a course. The test checks whether changes from low to high are as frequent as from high to low.
bowker.vorsicht: It tests symmetry, not agreement. With many small cells the approximation is uncertain.

box-cox.kurz: A family of power transformations, y(λ) = (y^λ - 1)/λ, with λ = 0 as the logarithm. The parameter λ is chosen so that the data become as normal as possible or the errors as equally spread as possible. It needs positive values.
box-cox.beispiel: λ = 0.5 corresponds roughly to the square root: for y = 9, (9^0.5 - 1)/0.5 = 4. λ = -1 corresponds to the reciprocal, λ = 1 to no change.
box-cox.vorsicht: The chosen λ is itself estimated and its uncertainty is not considered. Back-transforming results requires care.

box-m.kurz: Do the groups have the same covariance matrices? Box's M test checks this assumption of MANOVA, that is equal spreads and equal relationships among the measures in all groups.
box-m.beispiel: Two groups with two measures: the two 2 × 2 covariance matrices are compared, each holding two variances and one covariance.
box-m.vorsicht: The test reacts strongly to departures from normality and becomes significant easily in large samples. It is therefore often judged only at a strict level, such as 0.001.
box-m.statable: Under the MANOVA result: “Checking the assumptions”. Statable shows Box's M with the F and χ² approximation and says whether Pillai's trace is too cautious or too liberal with unequal groups.

box-tidwell.titel: Box-Tidwell test (checking the linearity of the logit)
box-tidwell.kurz: Does a number act evenly on the logit? The Box-Tidwell test adds the term x · ln(x) of this number to the model. If it is significant, the relation with the logit is not straight. The number must be greater than 0 everywhere.
box-tidwell.beispiel: Age in the model for low birth weight: term age · ln(age) z = −0.80, p = .42. No sign of a curve.
box-tidwell.vorsicht: Not significant is no proof of linearity. With several numbers test more strictly, for example .05 divided by the number of tests. A chart shows the shape more precisely.

boxplot.kurz: What do centre, spread and outliers look like at a glance? A box plot draws a box from Q1 to Q3 with a line at the median. Lines (whiskers) reach to the outermost values within 1.5 IQR. Further values appear as single points.
boxplot.beispiel: Waiting times 3, 4, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9, 10, 40: box from 4.25 to 8.75, line at 6.5, whiskers from 3 to 10, the 40 as a single point.
boxplot.vorsicht: A box plot hides whether the distribution has one or two peaks, and does not show the number of cases. The whisker length follows a chosen rule.

brant.kurz: A test of whether the assumption of the proportional odds model (parallel lines) in an ordinal regression holds: the effect of a predictor should be the same at every threshold of the ordered response. It tests each predictor and the whole model.
brant.beispiel: A predictor acts strongly on the threshold “low versus medium/high” but hardly on “low/medium versus high”. The Brant test becomes significant.
brant.vorsicht: With large samples the test becomes significant even for small departures. Ways out are models with non-parallel lines or multinomial models.

breitformat.kurz: One row per person. Repeated measurements stand side by side in columns of their own. This is the familiar kind of table. Some methods for repeated measures expect this format.
breitformat.beispiel: 4 people with 3 time points each give 4 rows and the columns t1, t2, t3.

brennan-prediger.kurz: An agreement measure for categories that corrects for chance like kappa. The chance agreement is taken as 1/q, where q is the number of categories. It therefore does not depend on the frequencies.
brennan-prediger.beispiel: Two raters agree in 80 % of cases, and there are q = 4 categories. The coefficient is (0.80 - 0.25)/(1 - 0.25) = 0.73.
brennan-prediger.vorsicht: The assumption of equally likely categories does not fit if some categories hardly occur. The value depends on the number of categories.

breslow-day.kurz: A test of whether the odds ratio is the same in all strata of a stratified two-by-two table. Only if it is similar does a common odds ratio (Mantel-Haenszel) make sense. The Tarone correction improves the test.
breslow-day.beispiel: The odds ratio is 2.0, 2.2 and 6.5 in three age groups. A significant Breslow-Day test speaks against a common odds ratio.
breslow-day.vorsicht: With small strata the test lacks power. A non-significant result does not prove equality.
sw: test of homogeneity of odds ratios

breusch-godfrey.kurz: A test for autocorrelation of the errors up to a chosen lag. Unlike Durbin-Watson it can also be used with lagged dependent variables as predictors. The statistic rests on an auxiliary regression of the residuals.
breusch-godfrey.beispiel: A regression of monthly data is checked for autocorrelation up to lag 12. The test thus also reveals seasonal patterns.
breusch-godfrey.vorsicht: The choice of lag is a decision. A significant result argues for using time series models or robust errors.

breusch-pagan.kurz: Do the residuals spread equally everywhere? The Breusch-Pagan test checks whether the spread of the residuals depends on the predictors. A small p value speaks against constant spread (homoscedasticity).
breusch-pagan.beispiel: n = 100, auxiliary regression of the squared residuals with R² = 0.08: statistic n · R² = 8, df = 1, p = 0.005.
breusch-pagan.vorsicht: In large samples even an unimportant difference in spread stands out, in small ones it is easily missed. The residual plot belongs with it.

brier-score.kurz: A measure of the quality of predicted probabilities: the mean squared distance between the prediction (0 to 1) and the actual outcome (0 or 1). Smaller is better. It checks discrimination and calibration together.
brier-score.vorsicht: The value can be read only in comparison, for example with the value obtained by always predicting the frequency of the event.

brown-forsythe.kurz: A test for equal spread in groups, a variant of the Levene test using distances to the median instead of the mean. It is more robust with skewed distributions. Another Brown-Forsythe test is an analysis of variance for unequal spreads.
brown-forsythe.beispiel: Three groups with skewed value distributions: the Brown-Forsythe test for equal spread is more stable than the Levene test with means.
brown-forsythe.vorsicht: Both procedures carry the name. The output has to be checked for which is meant.

brunner-munzel.kurz: A rank test for two independent groups that tests the probability that a value from one group is larger than one from the other (superiority). Unlike the Mann-Whitney test it tolerates unequal spreads.
brunner-munzel.beispiel: Two groups with very different spread: the Mann-Whitney test can give too many false alarms here, the Brunner-Munzel test keeps the level better.
brunner-munzel.vorsicht: It tests that the probability of superiority equals 0.5, not equality of the medians.

burn-in-warmup.kurz: Why are the first draws of an MCMC chain discarded? At the start the chain is not yet where the posterior distribution has its mass. This run-in phase (warmup, formerly burn-in) is not analysed.
burn-in-warmup.beispiel: Of 3000 draws per chain, the first 1000 are discarded as warmup. 2000 remain.
burn-in-warmup.vorsicht: The length of the warmup is not a fixed value. Measures such as R-hat and trace plots show whether it was enough.

cauchy.kurz: A bell-shaped distribution with tails so wide that it has no mean and no variance. The ratio of two independent standard normal quantities is Cauchy distributed. Its centre is the median.
cauchy.beispiel: Standard Cauchy: half of the values lie between -1 and 1. The mean of many observations is still no more stable than a single one.
cauchy.vorsicht: Mean and standard deviation are meaningless here. The median is usable.

ceteris-paribus.kurz: Latin for “other things being equal”. The influence of one quantity is looked at while all others are held fixed. This is how a regression coefficient in multiple regression is read. In observational data, holding fixed is done only by calculation.
ceteris-paribus.beispiel: Per year of work experience, pay in the model is higher, ceteris paribus: at the same education and age.

cfi.kurz: A fit index that compares the model with a null model in which all variables are independent. It lies between 0 and 1. The closer to 1, the better the model fits compared with the null model.
cfi.beispiel: Model: χ² = 48 with 24 degrees of freedom. Null model: χ² = 600 with 36. CFI = 1 - 24 / 564 = 0.957.
cfi.vorsicht: Values from 0.95 are often named as good fit, which is a habit and not proof. A high CFI says nothing about the reliability of the items.

chi-quadrat-homogenitaet.kurz: Do several groups spread over the categories of a characteristic in the same way? The calculation is exactly the same as for the test of independence. The difference lies in the design: the group sizes are fixed in advance, and each group is sampled separately.
chi-quadrat-homogenitaet.beispiel: 100 respondents from each of two districts: bike, bus, car inner 30, 40, 30; outer 20, 20, 60. χ² = 18.67, df = 2, p = 0.00009.
chi-quadrat-homogenitaet.vorsicht: A significant result only shows that the distributions are not the same in all groups, not in which category.

chi-quadrat-unabhaengigkeit.kurz: Are two categorical characteristics related in a sample? The test compares the observed frequencies with those expected under independence. The larger the deviations, the larger χ².
chi-quadrat-unabhaengigkeit.beispiel: Expected per row: 25, 30 and 45. χ² = 18.67 with (2 - 1)(3 - 1) = 2 degrees of freedom, p = 0.00009.
chi-quadrat-unabhaengigkeit.vorsicht: The test shows whether an association can be detected, not how strong it is; a measure such as Cramér's V does that. If many expected frequencies are small (below 5 is often cited), the approximation is inaccurate.

chi-quadrat-verteilung.kurz: How large are deviations when only chance is at work? The χ² distribution (chi-square) describes sums of squared standardized deviations. It only has values from 0 upward and is stretched to the right. Its mean equals its degrees of freedom.
chi-quadrat-verteilung.beispiel: With 3 degrees of freedom the mean is 3. Only 5% of values are larger than 7.815.
chi-quadrat-verteilung.vorsicht: With more degrees of freedom the curve becomes more symmetric. A large χ² value speaks against the assumption that only chance is at work, but does not say how large an effect is.

choroplethenkarte.kurz: A map in which areas such as countries or districts are coloured according to a value. It shows spatial patterns, for example the distribution of a rate.
choroplethenkarte.beispiel: Each district is coloured in five steps by its unemployment rate: light for low, dark for high.
choroplethenkarte.vorsicht: Large, thinly populated areas stand out strongly, small areas with many people hardly. Rates should be shown rather than absolute numbers, and the class limits change the picture.

chow-test.kurz: A test of whether a regression has the same coefficients in two parts of the data (for example before and after a point in time, or in two groups). The pooled model is compared with the two separate models.
chow-test.beispiel: n = 60, two coefficients per model. SSE pooled 500, separate 180 + 200 = 380: F = ((500 - 380)/2)/(380/56) = 8.84, p < 0.001. The relations differ.
chow-test.vorsicht: The time point or grouping must be fixed beforehand. The test assumes equal error spread in both parts.

ci-ueberlappung.kurz: Two 95 % intervals that overlap do not mean that the difference is not significant. Intervals may overlap somewhat and the difference is still significant. What matters is the interval of the difference.
ci-ueberlappung.beispiel: Means 10 and 14, each with standard error 1.4: the intervals 7.3 to 12.7 and 11.3 to 16.7 overlap. The difference 4 has a standard error of 1.98, z = 2.02, p = 0.043.
ci-ueberlappung.vorsicht: The reverse holds: if they do not overlap, the difference is significant. The rule of thumb “overlap means not significant” is wrong.

cliffs-delta.kurz: An effect size for two groups based on ranks: the probability that a value from the first group is larger than one from the second, minus the reverse probability. It lies between -1 and 1.
cliffs-delta.beispiel: P(X > Y) = 0.65 and P(X < Y) = 0.30: δ = 0.35. With the probability of superiority A = 0.675, δ = 2A - 1.
cliffs-delta.vorsicht: There are no generally valid limits for “small” or “large”. Commonly named values are conventions.

cloglog.kurz: A link function for yes-no data: log(-log(1 - p)). Unlike logit and probit it is asymmetric. It fits events observed in discrete time, where the risk per period is proportional.
cloglog.beispiel: At p = 0.5 cloglog gives log(-log 0.5) = -0.37, not 0 as the logit does.
cloglog.vorsicht: The coefficients are not odds ratios. They are log hazard ratios, read as hazard ratios.

clopper-pearson.kurz: Which range is safely plausible for a proportion? The Clopper-Pearson interval is an exact confidence interval for a proportion, calculated from the binomial distribution. Its true level is at least as high as stated.
clopper-pearson.beispiel: 18 of 40: 0.293 to 0.615, somewhat wider than Wilson with 0.307 to 0.602. 0 of 20: 0 to 0.168.
clopper-pearson.vorsicht: It is often too cautious, that is wider than needed. "Exact" refers to the calculation, not to a more accurate statement.

cluster-randomisierte-studie.kurz: Not single persons but whole groups (classes, practices, wards) are randomly assigned to the conditions. People in the same group resemble each other, and the analysis must allow for this (design effect, multilevel model).
cluster-randomisierte-studie.beispiel: 20 classes are randomly assigned to the new or the existing curriculum, not the individual children.
cluster-randomisierte-studie.vorsicht: If analysed as if every person had been assigned individually, the p-values are too small.

clusteranalyse.kurz: A method that sorts cases into groups (clusters) by similarity, without the groups being known beforehand. Within a cluster the cases should be alike, and between clusters they should differ.
clusteranalyse.beispiel: Customers are sorted into three groups by purchase frequency and basket value.
clusteranalyse.vorsicht: There is no single correct solution. The result depends on the distance measure, the method and the number of clusters, and a program will find clusters even in random data.

clusterrobuste.kurz: Standard errors that take into account that observations within groups (clusters) are related, without modelling the relation. They are reliable when the number of clusters is large enough.
clusterrobuste.beispiel: Pupils are grouped in classes. With class-robust standard errors the regression stays the same, but the errors and p values allow for the grouping.
clusterrobuste.vorsicht: With few clusters (say under 30) they are often too small. Corrections or a multilevel model then help.

cochran-armitage.kurz: A test of whether a proportion rises or falls steadily across ordered groups. It uses the order of the groups and therefore has more power than a general chi-square test.
cochran-armitage.beispiel: The share of smokers across four age groups falls: 42 %, 35 %, 30 %, 22 %. The trend test checks whether this steady decline exceeds chance.
cochran-armitage.vorsicht: The test checks a linear trend. It does not detect a U-shaped relation.

cochran-q.kurz: Do three or more yes-no conditions differ in the same people? Cochran's Q test extends the McNemar test to more than two measurements. The statistic Q is judged with the χ² distribution.
cochran-q.beispiel: 8 people attempt 3 tasks; 6, 6 and 2 people solved them: Q = 4.57, df = 2, p = 0.10.
cochran-q.vorsicht: With few people the χ² approximation is inaccurate. People who always or never solve a task contribute nothing.

cochrane-orcutt.kurz: A method for regressions with autocorrelated errors: the data are transformed with the estimated autocorrelation coefficient ρ (y_t - ρ·y_{t-1}), then estimated in the usual way. This is repeated until ρ no longer changes.
cochrane-orcutt.beispiel: The residuals of a time series regression have an autocorrelation of 0.6. After transforming with ρ = 0.6, the residuals are nearly uncorrelated.
cochrane-orcutt.vorsicht: The first observation is lost (Prais-Winsten keeps it). Today robust standard errors or time series models are often preferred.

codierung.kurz: Assigning numbers or short labels to answers. Coding makes answers storable and analysable in data. Which code stands for what is recorded in the codebook.
codierung.beispiel: Smoking status: 0 = never, 1 = former, 2 = current. The file contains only 0, 1 or 2.
codierung.vorsicht: Codes are names, not measurements. A mean of the codes 0, 1, 2 says nothing for a nominal variable.

cohen-konventionen.kurz: The benchmarks for effect sizes proposed by Jacob Cohen, such as d = 0.2 small, 0.5 medium and 0.8 large; r = 0.1, 0.3 and 0.5; η² = 0.01, 0.06 and 0.14. They were meant as a stopgap when nothing else is known.
cohen-konventionen.beispiel: A difference of d = 0.5 is often called “medium” without checking what that means in the field.
cohen-konventionen.vorsicht: The values are habits, not laws of nature, and what is large in one field is small in another. Benchmarks from the field are better.

cohens-d.kurz: How far apart are two means, measured in standard deviations? Cohen's d is the difference of means divided by the common (pooled) standard deviation. It does not depend on the unit of measurement.
cohens-d.beispiel: Means 52 and 48, both standard deviations 8: d = (52 - 48) / 8 = 0.5.
cohens-d.vorsicht: Often quoted are 0.2 as small, 0.5 as medium and 0.8 as large, but these are habits, not a yardstick for usefulness. In small groups d is slightly overestimated.

cohens-f.kurz: How strongly do several group means differ, relative to the spread within groups? Cohen's f is the standard deviation of the group means (divisor k, the number of groups) divided by the within-group standard deviation. It serves sample size planning for ANOVA.
cohens-f.beispiel: Three equal-sized groups with means 10, 12, 14 and within-group SD 4: the spread of the means is √(8 / 3) = 1.633, so f = 1.633 / 4 = 0.41. This corresponds to η² = 0.14.
cohens-f.vorsicht: Often quoted are 0.10 as small, 0.25 as medium, 0.40 as large. These are habits that must be fitted to the field.

cohens-h.kurz: An effect size for the difference between two proportions. The proportions are transformed by the arcsine so that equal distances mean the same everywhere: h = 2·arcsin(√p₁) - 2·arcsin(√p₂).
cohens-h.vorsicht: Values of 0.2, 0.5 and 0.8 are often named as benchmarks, which are habits. A difference of 10 percentage points gives different h depending on where it lies.

cohens-q.kurz: An effect size for the difference between two correlations: the difference of their Fisher z values, q = z(r₁) - z(r₂). The Fisher transformation makes the scale even.
cohens-q.vorsicht: Benchmarks such as 0.1, 0.3 and 0.5 are habits. The difference between 0.60 and 0.40 is not the same size as that between 0.90 and 0.70.

cohens-u3.kurz: The share of the group with the lower mean that lies below the mean of the other group, for normally distributed values with equal spread. It translates Cohen's d into a share: U3 = Φ(d).
cohens-u3.beispiel: d = 0.5: U3 = 0.69. 69 % of the persons in the comparison group have a value below the mean of the group with the higher mean.
cohens-u3.vorsicht: The conversion holds only for normally distributed values with equal spread. For other distributions it is inexact.

collider.kurz: What happens when selection or control is based on a common consequence of two quantities? A collider is a quantity influenced by two others. If it is held constant or used for selection, a spurious relationship or a distortion appears between the two.
collider.beispiel: Admission to a programme depends on grades and sports performance. Among those admitted, someone with a weak grade must be good at sports: an inverse relationship appears.
collider.vorsicht: Unlike with a confounder, taking it into account does harm here. Whether a quantity is a confounder or a collider depends on the structure, not on the data alone.

compliance.kurz: The extent to which participants follow the study plan or treatment as intended. Poor adherence weakens the observed effect and is a reason for differences between intention-to-treat and per-protocol analysis.
compliance.beispiel: Of 100 people assigned, 80 take the tablets as intended. Compliance is 80 %.
compliance.vorsicht: Those who do not follow the treatment often differ from those who do. Compliance is therefore not random itself.

composite-reliabilitaet.kurz: A measure of the dependability of a scale, computed from the loadings of a measurement model. It states what share of the variance of the scale sum goes back to the latent variable. Unlike Cronbach's alpha, it allows loadings of different size.
composite-reliabilitaet.beispiel: Loadings 0.8, 0.7, 0.6: sum 2.1, square 4.41. Error parts 0.36 + 0.51 + 0.64 = 1.51. Composite reliability = 4.41 / (4.41 + 1.51) = 0.745.
composite-reliabilitaet.vorsicht: As with alpha, 0.7 is often named as sufficient, which is a habit. The measure assumes a fitting measurement model.

cooks-distanz.kurz: How strongly does a single case change the whole model? Cook's distance measures, for each case, how much the predicted values would change if that case were left out. It combines the distance from the line (residual) with the leverage.
cooks-distanz.beispiel: A person with 9 hours and 30 points is added to the 8 people: Cook's distance 2.06, the others at most 0.28. The slope falls from 4.13 to 0.72.
cooks-distanz.vorsicht: Commonly quoted cut-offs such as 1 or 4/n are rules of thumb. A conspicuous case is examined, not removed automatically.

copula.kurz: A function that separates the dependence between variables from their individual distributions. It allows the single distributions to be chosen freely and the dependence structure to be set separately.
copula.beispiel: Two claim amounts each follow a Pareto distribution. The copula determines how strongly large claims occur together.
copula.vorsicht: The same correlation can belong to very different joint distributions. The choice of copula is a model assumption.

cox-regression.kurz: How do characteristics affect the event rate? Cox regression estimates a hazard ratio for each predictor without fixing the time course of the baseline rate. Censored cases are included.
cox-regression.beispiel: Hazard ratio 0.5 for a treatment: at any time the event rate is half as large as without treatment.
cox-regression.vorsicht: The model assumes that the ratio of the rates stays the same over time. This assumption has to be checked.

cox-residuen.titel: Residuals of Cox regression (Schoenfeld, martingale, Cox-Snell)
cox-residuen.kurz: Diagnostics for a Cox model. Schoenfeld residuals test the proportional hazards assumption (a trend over time points to a violation). Martingale residuals show whether a predictor enters in the right form. Cox-Snell residuals check the overall fit.
cox-residuen.beispiel: A plot of Schoenfeld residuals against time shows a rising course for one predictor. The effect therefore changes over time.
cox-residuen.vorsicht: The residuals do not have the simple form of linear regression and are read differently.

cramer-rao.kurz: A lower bound for the variance of every unbiased estimator: it is the reciprocal of the Fisher information. An estimator that reaches it is called efficient.
cramer-rao.beispiel: For a proportion p from n = 100 observations the bound is p(1 - p)/n = 0.3 · 0.7/100 = 0.0021. The sample proportion reaches it.
cramer-rao.vorsicht: The bound holds for unbiased estimators and under regularity conditions. Biased estimators can have a smaller variance.

cramer-von-mises.kurz: A test of whether data fit a specified distribution that compares the whole distribution function. It measures the sum of squared distances between the observed and expected distribution function.
cramer-von-mises.beispiel: Waiting times are checked for fit to an exponential distribution. The test compares across the entire range.
cramer-von-mises.vorsicht: As with other goodness-of-fit tests, the result is no proof of fit. With small samples power is lacking.
