cramers-v.kurz: How strongly are two categorical variables related? Cramér's V turns the result of the χ² test into a number from 0 to 1. 0 means no association, 1 a complete one. It fits cross tables of any size.
cramers-v.vorsicht: V shows only the strength, not the direction. Rules of thumb for small or large depend on the table size.

cronbach-alpha.kurz: Do the items of a scale fit together in measuring the same thing? Cronbach's alpha (α) summarises how strongly the items are related. It usually lies between 0 and 1. A higher value means the items are more strongly related.
cronbach-alpha.beispiel: 4 items with a mean inter-item correlation of 0.5: standardised alpha = 4 x 0.5 / (1 + 3 x 0.5) = 0.80.
cronbach-alpha.vorsicht: Alpha rises with the number of items, and a high value proves neither unidimensionality nor validity. Rules of thumb such as 0.7 are habits.

cross-lagged.kurz: A longitudinal model for two variables measured at several time points. It estimates whether X at one time predicts later Y and vice versa, after allowing for stability over time.
cross-lagged.beispiel: School enjoyment and achievement are measured over three years. The model tests whether enjoyment in year one predicts achievement in year two and achievement the later enjoyment.
cross-lagged.vorsicht: A predictive path is not a cause. Stable differences between persons bias the paths, so extended models with person-level random intercepts exist.

crossover-design.kurz: Each person receives all conditions one after the other, and the order is distributed at random. Each person thus serves as their own comparison.
crossover-design.beispiel: 20 people: one half gets condition A first and then B, the other half B first and then A, with a break in between.
crossover-design.vorsicht: The effect of the first condition can carry over into the second (carry-over effect). A break in between is necessary.

csv.kurz: A text file in which each line is a case and the values are separated by a delimiter. CSV stands for comma-separated values. Almost every program can read and write it.
csv.vorsicht: The delimiter (comma or semicolon), the decimal sign and the character set differ with the language setting. Variable labels, value labels and level of measurement are not stored in the file.

cut-off.kurz: A value at or above which a result counts as abnormal or positive. If it is chosen from the same data, the result looks better than it will be. A different value shifts sensitivity and specificity.
cut-off.beispiel: From a test score of 12 upwards someone counts as flagged: 12 is the cut-off.

dagostino.kurz: A test for normality that combines skewness and kurtosis into one statistic K². Both are first transformed so that they are approximately normally distributed.
dagostino.beispiel: A sample of 80 values is tested for normality. The omnibus test combines skewness and kurtosis into one p value.
dagostino.vorsicht: It is regarded as usable only from about 20 values. A non-significant test does not prove normality.

datenbereinigung.kurz: Checking data for errors and correcting them before analysis. One looks for typing errors, impossible values, duplicate cases and wrong codes. Everything that is changed should be recorded so that it can be traced.
datenbereinigung.beispiel: An age of 199 years is impossible. It is looked up in the original or set to missing.
datenbereinigung.vorsicht: A conspicuous value is not automatically wrong. Genuine extreme values are not deleted just because they are inconvenient.

datenmanagementplan.kurz: A document that describes how data are handled in a project: collection, format, storage, backup, access, protection and retention. Many funders require it.
datenmanagementplan.beispiel: The plan states where the data are kept, who has access, how often backups are made and how long they are retained after the project ends.
datenmanagementplan.vorsicht: The plan is a living document and is adapted over the course of the project. It does not replace data protection.

datenmatrix.kurz: A table in which every row holds one case and every column one variable. Each cell is the value of one variable for one case.
datenmatrix.beispiel: Case 1: 31 years, 172 cm. Case 2: 45 years, 168 cm. Case 3: 27 years, 181 cm. This is a matrix with 3 rows and 2 columns.

datenpunkt.kurz: A single value or case. A data point is a single observation: a value in a cell or, depending on context, a whole case with all its values. In a scatter plot it is one dot.
datenpunkt.beispiel: Person no. 7 with 171 cm and 66 kg is one dot at (171 | 66) in a scatter plot.
datenpunkt.vorsicht: Several measurements of the same person are several data points, but they are not independent of each other.

datensatz.kurz: All data collected in a study, put together as one table: rows are cases, columns are variables.
datensatz.beispiel: 40 people with 6 variables each make a dataset with 40 rows and 6 columns, so 240 cells.

datentyp.kurz: The way a value is stored: as a number, as text or as a date. The type determines what you can calculate with it. A mean cannot be formed from text, while a date allows a distance in days.
datentyp.beispiel: The ID 007 stored as a number becomes 7. Stored as text it stays 007.
datentyp.vorsicht: The data type is not the level of measurement. A code for a category is stored as a number and is still nominal.

dbscan.kurz: A clustering method that recognises groups as dense regions of cases separated by thinly populated regions. Cases in thin regions count as noise. The number of clusters need not be specified.
dbscan.beispiel: On a map of locations, DBSCAN finds two dense clusters and marks single, isolated places as noise.
dbscan.vorsicht: Two settings (neighbourhood radius and minimum number of neighbours) determine the result. With clusters of very different density the method fails easily.
sw: density-based spatial clustering of applications with noise

de-facto.kurz: Latin for “from the fact”. It means in reality, as opposed to planned or official (de jure). For samples: the number actually reached, not the planned one.
de-facto.beispiel: The plan was 200 people; de facto, 164 took part.

deckeneffekt.kurz: The test is too easy: many reach the highest possible score, so differences at the top can no longer be seen.
deckeneffekt.beispiel: A test has at most 20 points, and 40% of the people reach 20. Differences among these people are lost.
deckeneffekt.vorsicht: The spread is cut off, and associations tend to come out too small.

deduktiv.kurz: From Latin deducere: “to derive”. Reasoning from the general to the particular: a testable hypothesis is derived from a theory. The counterpart is inductive.
deduktiv.beispiel: From the theory “practice shortens the time” follows: after training, times are shorter.

deflator.kurz: Nominal values are measured in current prices, real values in prices of a base year. Converting from nominal to real is called deflating: the value is divided by a price index (times 100).
deflator.beispiel: Turnover is 1200 nominal. The price index stands at 120 (base year 100). Real turnover is 1200/120 · 100 = 1000.
deflator.vorsicht: The deflator depends on the price index chosen. Real values are comparable only for the chosen base year.

delphi.kurz: A method of obtaining the judgement of a group of experts in several rounds. After each round everyone receives a summary of the answers and may adjust their judgement. The aim is a consensus or a stable picture.
delphi.beispiel: In three rounds, 25 experts rate each measure on a scale from 1 to 9. Consensus is defined as an interquartile range of at most 2.
delphi.vorsicht: The definition of consensus is a habit. The result is an expert judgement, not evidence.

delta-methode.kurz: An approximation method for calculating the spread of a function of an estimated quantity. With a first-order Taylor expansion, Var(g(X)) ≈ g′(μ)² · Var(X). This gives the standard error of, for example, a logarithm, a quotient or an odds ratio.
delta-methode.beispiel: An estimate of 10 has the standard error 0.5. For the logarithm g′(x) = 1/x, so the standard error is about 0.5/10 = 0.05.
delta-methode.vorsicht: The approximation is inexact for small samples and strongly curved functions. A bootstrap is then more reliable.

delta-r2.kurz: How much does an additional predictor or block of predictors bring? ΔR² (delta R²) is the increase in R² from one model to the next, which contains additional predictors. An F test checks whether the increase goes beyond chance.
delta-r2.beispiel: Practice tasks are added to study hours (R² = 0.933): R² = 0.958, ΔR² = 0.024.
delta-r2.vorsicht: If the predictors are related, ΔR² depends on the order in which they enter the model.

deming.kurz: How does one compare when both measurement methods have error? Ordinary regression assumes x is error-free and then distorts the slope. Deming regression allows for error in x and y through the ratio of the two error variances.
deming.beispiel: Two blood glucose meters, equally precise: the ratio of error variances is 1. If one meter is half as precise, the ratio changes.
deming.vorsicht: The ratio of error variances must be known or estimated from repeated measurements. A wrongly set ratio distorts the line.

dendrogramm.kurz: A tree diagram that shows in which order and at which distance hierarchical clustering merges groups. The height of a join is the distance at which the groups were merged.
dendrogramm.beispiel: A join at height 0.5 means: these two cases are very similar. A horizontal cut at height 4 splits the tree into the groups below it.
dendrogramm.vorsicht: The left-to-right order of the leaves is partly arbitrary. Only the heights of the joins count.

design.kurz: From Latin designare: “to mark out”. The set-up of a study: who is examined, when, how often and in which groups. The design determines which questions the data can answer.
design.beispiel: Two groups, each measured once before and once after training: a pre-post design.

designbasiert.kurz: A way of inferring in which the random selection of the sample is the basis of the statement, not a model of the data. The uncertainty arises from which units were drawn. The counterpart is model-based inference.
designbasiert.beispiel: The mean of a school sample is computed with weights and standard errors from the sampling design. No model for the distribution of grades is needed.
designbasiert.vorsicht: The statements hold for the finite population of the survey. For relations of a general kind, additional assumptions are needed.

designeffekt.kurz: How much less precise is a sampling plan than simple drawing by lot? The design effect is the variance of the estimator under the plan divided by the variance under simple random sampling of the same size. Above 1 means less information per case.
designeffekt.beispiel: 50 clusters of 20 respondents, similarity within clusters ρ = 0.05: deff = 1 + 19 · 0.05 = 1.95. Of 1000 cases about 513 remain effective.
designeffekt.vorsicht: The formula holds approximately for equal-sized clusters. Stratification can push the value below 1.

designmatrix.kurz: The table of predictors in regression in which each row is a case and each column a predictor, with a column of ones for the intercept. Everything is calculated from it: b = (XᵀX)⁻¹Xᵀy.
designmatrix.beispiel: Three persons with one predictor x = 2, 3, 5: rows [1, 2], [1, 3], [1, 5]. The first column stands for the intercept.
designmatrix.vorsicht: Groups are represented in it by dummy columns. The choice of coding changes the meaning of the coefficients.

deskriptive-statistik.kurz: What do the data look like? Descriptive statistics summarise data through measures, tables and charts. They say something only about the data at hand.
deskriptive-statistik.beispiel: The mean and spread of sleep duration in 50 people describe these 50 people, not everyone else.

determinante-korrelationsmatrix.kurz: Do some questions almost fully overlap? The determinant is a single number from the correlation matrix: 1 if all questions are uncorrelated, close to 0 if some are almost copies of each other. Below .00001 counts as a warning sign; at 0 the matrix cannot be inverted.
determinante-korrelationsmatrix.beispiel: bfi A1 to A5 and C1 to C5: determinant .125, so no sign of almost duplicate questions.
determinante-korrelationsmatrix.vorsicht: The limit .00001 is a rule of thumb. A small value does not say which question is the problem; for that look at the correlations and the KMO per question.

determinationskoeffizient.kurz: How much of the differences in the outcome does the model account for? The coefficient of determination is the share of the outcome's variation that the model accounts for. It lies between 0 and 1. In a simple regression R² equals r².
determinationskoeffizient.beispiel: r = 0.966 between study hours and scores gives R² = 0.933: the line accounts for 93.3% of the variation in scores.
determinationskoeffizient.vorsicht: ‘Explained’ here means variation split up by calculation, not a cause. Adding predictors never lowers R², even useless ones.

deterministisch.kurz: Fixed by the starting conditions, without chance. The same conditions always give the same result. The opposite is stochastic.
deterministisch.beispiel: Price = 4 € · quantity: for 5 items it is always 20 €. A measurement of this quantity with error, in contrast, is stochastic.
deterministisch.vorsicht: A model is often deterministic plus random error: the pattern is deterministic, the deviation stochastic.

devianz.kurz: How far is a model from the best possible one for these data? The deviance is -2 times the logarithm of the likelihood ratio against the saturated model. Smaller is better. The difference between two nested models approximately follows a χ² distribution.
devianz.beispiel: Null model 138.63, model 110.00: difference 28.63 with 1 degree of freedom, p < 0.001.
devianz.vorsicht: With individual data (yes/no per person) the deviance alone does not work as a measure of fit. Only differences are usable.

devianzresiduum.kurz: How badly does the model fit a single case? The deviance residual measures the contribution of the case to the deviance, with a sign. Standardised, it is divided by the square root of 1 minus leverage. Values above 2 in size stand out.
devianzresiduum.beispiel: A case with predicted probability 0.12 where the event did occur: deviance residual about 2.1.
devianzresiduum.vorsicht: With yes/no data the residuals are not normally distributed; charts look different from linear regression. Check unusual cases, do not delete them.

dezil.kurz: Where are the tenth boundaries? Nine deciles split the sorted values into ten equal parts. D1 is the 0.1 quantile, D5 the median, D9 the 0.9 quantile.
dezil.beispiel: Waiting times 3, 4, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9, 10, 40: D1 = 3.9 and D9 = 13 minutes.
dezil.vorsicht: “Top decile” usually means the upper 10% of the cases. The boundary for it is D9.

dezilverhaeltnis.titel: Quintile share ratio (S80/S20) and decile ratio
dezilverhaeltnis.kurz: A measure of income inequality: the ratio between the income share of the top 20 % and that of the bottom 20 % (S80/S20). The decile ratio compares the top and bottom 10 % (shares, S90/S10) or the decile cut-offs (P90/P10).
dezilverhaeltnis.beispiel: The top 20 % have 40 % of total income, the bottom 20 % have 8 %. S80/S20 = 40/8 = 5.
dezilverhaeltnis.vorsicht: The ratio ignores the middle of the distribution. Two different distributions can have the same value.

dfbetas-dffits.kurz: Influence measures for single cases in regression. DFBETAS shows by how many standard errors a coefficient changes when the case is left out. DFFITS shows the same for the predicted value.
dfbetas-dffits.beispiel: With n = 100, 2/√n = 0.2 is often named for DFBETAS, and 2√(p/n) for DFFITS; with p = 3 coefficients that is 0.35.
dfbetas-dffits.vorsicht: The limits are habits. A conspicuous case is looked at, not removed automatically.

dichotom.kurz: A variable with exactly two values. Dichotomous means “split in two”. It is usually stored as 0 and 1. The mean of the 0/1 values is then the proportion of 1s.
dichotom.beispiel: Smoking: no = 0, yes = 1. With 8 yes answers among 20 people the mean is 0.4, a proportion of 40%.
dichotom.vorsicht: If a variable with many levels is split into two groups at a cut-off, information is lost. Two groups are not the same as a measured quantity.

dichte-beschreibung.kurz: A detailed account of actions in context that also supplies intentions, circumstances and meanings, not just the outward events. Readers can then judge whether the findings transfer to their own situation.
dichte-beschreibung.beispiel: Instead of “The teacher smiled”, it is described in what situation, to whom and with what effect on the class the smile occurred.
dichte-beschreibung.vorsicht: Thick description is not a quantity of data but precision in context. It supports transferability without guaranteeing it.

dichtefunktion.kurz: It describes a continuous random variable. The probability for a range is the area under the curve over that range. The total area is 1.
dichtefunktion.beispiel: Uniform from 0 to 10: height 0.1. Between 2 and 5 the area is 3 · 0.1 = 0.3.
dichtefunktion.vorsicht: The function value is not a probability and can exceed 1. For a uniform from 0 to 0.5 the height is 2.

dichtekurve.kurz: Where do the values lie close together? A density curve is a smooth curve over the values. The area under it between two values is the share of cases in that range. The total area is 1.
dichtekurve.beispiel: If the area between 4 and 8 minutes is 0.40, about 40% of the waiting times fall in that range.
dichtekurve.vorsicht: The height of the curve is not a proportion and can exceed 1. Only the area is a proportion.

dickey-fuller.kurz: Does the series have a unit root, so that it is not stationary? The (augmented) Dickey-Fuller test (ADF) tests the null hypothesis that the series has a unit root. A small p value speaks against this null hypothesis.
dickey-fuller.beispiel: A random walk (each value is the previous one plus chance) has a unit root. Here the test should usually give a large p value.
dickey-fuller.vorsicht: A large p value does not prove non-stationarity. With short series the test often has little power.

dif.kurz: An item works differently in two groups although the people are equally able. The task then favours one group for reasons unrelated to the ability being measured.
dif.beispiel: Two groups with the same arithmetic ability. One group solves a word problem far less often, for example because of a word unknown to it.
dif.vorsicht: A difference in means between groups is not yet DIF. Only at equal ability does it show whether the item is biased.

differential-privacy.kurz: A protection concept for analyses: enough random noise is added to the published result that it hardly changes if one single person is missing from the dataset. The strength is measured by the parameter ε; smaller means more protection.
differential-privacy.beispiel: A count (changed by at most 1 by one person) is published with ε = 0.5. The noise follows a Laplace distribution with scale 1/0.5 = 2.
differential-privacy.vorsicht: More protection means greater inaccuracy. With small numbers the noise can be larger than the result itself.

differenz-in-differenzen.kurz: Did the treatment group change more than the comparison group? Difference-in-differences subtracts the change of the comparison group from the change of the treatment group.
differenz-in-differenzen.beispiel: Treatment group 50 to 58 (+8), comparison group 48 to 52 (+4): effect 8 - 4 = 4.
differenz-in-differenzen.vorsicht: It holds only if both groups would have moved in parallel without the measure (parallel trends assumption). Before the measure the courses of the two groups can be compared, afterwards it remains an assumption.

differenzieren.kurz: How does the value change from one time point to the next? Differencing replaces each value by its change from the previous one. This can remove a trend.
differenzieren.vorsicht: Differencing too often creates artificial patterns. Once or twice is usually enough.

dimension.kurz: From Latin dimensio: “measuring out”. In statistics usually the number of axes or quantities. A data matrix has the dimension rows times columns. A scale can have several dimensions, parts that measure different things.
dimension.beispiel: A table with 120 rows and 8 columns has the dimension 120 by 8.

dimensionsreduktion.kurz: The collective term for methods that condense many variables into a few dimensions while keeping as much information as possible. Examples are principal component analysis, factor analysis and multidimensional scaling.
dimensionsreduktion.beispiel: From 30 questions on satisfaction, 4 principal components are formed that together capture most of the variance.
dimensionsreduktion.vorsicht: The condensed dimensions are harder to interpret than the original variables. What information is lost has to be checked.

disjunkt.kurz: From Latin disiungere: “to separate”. Without overlap. Disjoint events cannot happen at the same time. The categories of a variable should be disjoint. Disjoint is not the same as independent.
disjunkt.beispiel: In a single roll of a die, “even number” and “the number 3” are disjoint.

diskrepanz.kurz: From Latin discrepare: “to differ”. A deviation or contradiction between two values, for example between target and actual value, or between two measurements of the same quantity.
diskrepanz.beispiel: Between self-rating and test there is, on average, a discrepancy of 3 points.

diskret.kurz: A variable that takes only separate, single values. Discrete values can be counted off, for example 0, 1, 2, 3. Nothing lies between two neighbouring values.
diskret.beispiel: Number of siblings: 0, 1, 2 or 3. A person does not have 1.5 siblings.
diskret.vorsicht: Discrete says something about the possible values, not about the level of measurement. A count is discrete and on a ratio scale.

diskriminante-validitaet.kurz: Is the construct distinct from unrelated ones? Discriminant validity means: measures of different constructs are only weakly related, as the theory expects.
diskriminante-validitaet.beispiel: An anxiety scale and a spelling test hardly correlate (r = 0.05).

diskriminanzanalyse.kurz: A method for groups that are already known. It looks for combinations of variables that separate the groups as well as possible, and uses them to assign new cases to a group. Unlike cluster analysis, the groups are given.
diskriminanzanalyse.beispiel: From measurements, it is determined which combination of body length and wing length best separates two bird species.
diskriminanzanalyse.vorsicht: The hit rate on the same data is too optimistic. A check on new cases or by cross-validation is more telling.

diskursanalyse.kurz: A group of methods that study how meanings, positions and power are produced in texts and conversations. The question is not only what is said but how it is spoken about and which statements are possible.
diskursanalyse.beispiel: Newspaper articles on migration are examined: which words and images are used, who gets a say?
diskursanalyse.vorsicht: There are many schools that differ strongly. The results are interpretations, not measurements.

distanzmass.kurz: A rule that computes, for two cases, a number saying how different they are. The larger, the less alike. Clustering and scaling methods need a distance measure. Euclidean and Manhattan distance are common, and other measures exist for categories.
distanzmass.beispiel: Two people with values (1, 2) and (4, 6) have a Euclidean distance of 5 and a Manhattan distance of 7.
distanzmass.vorsicht: The chosen measure influences the result of a clustering method. Categories and metric variables call for different measures.

divergente-uebergaenge.kurz: A warning in Hamiltonian Monte Carlo: the sampler could not follow a narrow part of the target distribution and aborted the step. The results can be biased there.
divergente-uebergaenge.beispiel: In a hierarchical model with very small group spreads, 40 of 4000 draws report divergence. This is a sign to reformulate the model.
divergente-uebergaenge.vorsicht: A few warnings must not be ignored. Usually a different parametrisation or a more informative prior helps.

divergenz.kurz: From Latin divergere: “to tend apart”. The opposite of convergence. A calculation procedure diverges when the estimates do not settle down. Divergence also names a measure of distance between two distributions.
divergenz.beispiel: The estimation procedure diverged: after 100 steps the values still swung widely.

dixon.kurz: An outlier test for small samples (about 3 to 30 values). The statistic Q is the distance of the suspect value from its neighbour, divided by the range.
dixon.beispiel: Values 10, 11, 11, 12, 12, 13, 25: Q = (25 - 13)/(25 - 10) = 0.80. This is compared with a tabulated critical value.
dixon.vorsicht: It tests only one outlier and assumes approximately normal data. Several outliers disturb it.

dominanzregel.kurz: A rule of statistical disclosure control: a cell is suppressed if one or a few contributors make up too large a share of the cell value. The cell sum would otherwise allow conclusions about their individual values.
dominanzregel.beispiel: Under a (1, 75) rule a turnover cell is suppressed if the largest firm contributes more than 75 % of the cell value. If it has 80 %, the cell is suppressed.
dominanzregel.vorsicht: The thresholds are set by the agency concerned. A suppressed cell can be recovered through margins, so secondary suppressions are needed.

dosis-wirkung.kurz: The relation between the strength of an exposure and the strength of the effect. A rise of the effect with the dose is taken as a hint of a causal relation, but is no proof.
dosis-wirkung.beispiel: With a rising number of cigarettes smoked per day, the rate of lung cancer rises steadily. This is a dose-response gradient.
dosis-wirkung.vorsicht: Confounders can also produce a gradient. It can also show thresholds or saturation instead of a straight rise.

dreiecksverteilung.kurz: A simple distribution with minimum a, maximum b and most frequent value c, whose density forms a triangle. It is used for estimates when there are no data. The mean is (a + b + c)/3.
dreiecksverteilung.beispiel: Effort for a project: at least 2 days, at most 10, most often 3. Expected (2 + 10 + 3)/3 = 5 days.
dreiecksverteilung.vorsicht: It is a model for estimates, not a finding from data.

drittvariable.kurz: Is there another quantity that influences two others at the same time? A third variable lies outside the pair under study. It can create, strengthen or weaken their relationship. If it influences both, it is called a confounder.
drittvariable.beispiel: The more firefighters at a fire, the greater the damage. The third variable is the size of the fire.
drittvariable.vorsicht: A third variable that was not measured cannot be calculated away.

dropout.kurz: People who leave before the end of a study. If the reasons are linked to the outcome, the picture is distorted. This is why the number and reasons of dropouts are reported.
dropout.beispiel: Of 100 people, only 78 finish the study: 22 dropouts.

dublette.kurz: A case that appears more than once in the file. The cause is usually an error in entering, merging or exporting. Duplicates count one case several times and make n too large.
dublette.beispiel: The same ID appears twice in the dataset because a questionnaire was entered twice. Of 150 rows, 149 are different cases.
dublette.vorsicht: Identical answers alone do not prove a duplicate, because two people can have the same values. The ID is decisive.

duncan.kurz: Two older stepwise post hoc procedures that compare ordered group means pairwise and adjust the critical value for the number of steps in between. They are more liberal than Tukey and do not keep the familywise error rate strictly.
duncan.beispiel: Five group means are ordered by size. Neighbouring means are tested against a smaller critical value, more distant ones against a larger one.
duncan.vorsicht: Because of the higher risk of false findings, the Duncan test is hardly recommended today. Tukey is the rule.

dunn.kurz: Which groups differ after a Kruskal-Wallis test? The Dunn test compares each pair of groups using their mean ranks. Because several comparisons arise, it needs an adjustment, for example Bonferroni or Holm.
dunn.beispiel: Mean ranks 2.75 and 10.5 for 12 values in 3 groups of 4: z = -3.04, p = 0.0024; after Bonferroni (3 comparisons) 0.0071.
dunn.vorsicht: Without adjustment, the number of false-positive findings grows with every further comparison.

dunnett.kurz: Which groups differ from a reference group? The Dunnett test compares each group only with one chosen control group and not with each other. With fewer comparisons it is sharper than a test of all pairs.
dunnett.beispiel: Control A (mean 5) against B (7) and C (9), 4 values each: a difference of 1.51 or more counts as important. Both differences, 2 and 4, are above it.
dunnett.vorsicht: The control group must be fixed beforehand. Comparisons among the other groups are not covered.
dunnett.statable: Under the result of the analysis of variance at “Which groups differ?” choose the Dunnett test and set the control group below it.

durbin-watson.kurz: Are consecutive residuals related? The Durbin-Watson test checks for first-order autocorrelation. The statistic d lies between 0 and 4. Values around 2 point to no autocorrelation, values near 0 to positive, values near 4 to negative.
durbin-watson.beispiel: Residuals of 10 consecutive days: 1.2, 0.9, 0.6, -0.1, -0.7, -1.0, -0.8, 0.4, 0.9, -0.4. This gives d = 0.77.
durbin-watson.vorsicht: Meaningful only if the cases have a natural order, such as time. The test checks only a distance of one step.

ebenen.kurz: At which level was it measured? In multilevel models, level 1 is the smallest unit and level 2 is the group it belongs to. Variables can sit on either level, for instance age on level 1 and class size on level 2.
ebenen.beispiel: Students (level 1) in classes (level 2): sex belongs to level 1, class size to level 2.
ebenen.vorsicht: A level-2 value is the same for every member of the group. The number of groups, not of persons, then determines how much it can tell.

ebenenuebergreifende-wechselwirkung.kurz: Does the effect of a characteristic of the person depend on which group they are in? The cross-level interaction is the product of a characteristic within the group and a characteristic of the group. It explains why slopes differ from group to group.
ebenenuebergreifende-wechselwirkung.beispiel: Social status of the pupil times school type: b = −1.35 (p < .001). In Catholic schools the relationship between status and achievement is weaker than in public schools.
ebenenuebergreifende-wechselwirkung.vorsicht: The characteristic within the group should be centred at the group mean, otherwise the levels mix. The main effect of each variable holds where the other is 0.

effektcodierung.kurz: Two ways to turn a group characteristic into numbers for a regression. Reference coding (dummy coding): each group gets 0 or 1, one group is the comparison base. Effect coding: the reference group gets -1, and the coefficients show deviations from the grand mean.
effektcodierung.beispiel: Three groups A, B, C. With reference coding with A as the base, the coefficient of B is the difference B minus A. With effect coding it is the difference of B from the mean of the three groups.
effektcodierung.vorsicht: The coefficients mean something different in each coding. The intercept changes too.

effektive-kategorienzahl.kurz: The number of equally frequent categories that would have the same diversity as the observed distribution. Usual are exp(H) with the Shannon index H or 1/Σp².
effektive-kategorienzahl.beispiel: Shares of 0.5, 0.3 and 0.2: exp(1.03) = 2.8. The three categories are about as diverse as 2.8 equally frequent ones.
effektive-kategorienzahl.vorsicht: Different formulas give different numbers; with 1/Σp² it would be 1/0.38 = 2.6. The formula has to be stated.

effektmodifikation.kurz: The strength of an effect differs depending on the level of a third characteristic. This is an interaction, but in epidemiology it is named this way. Whether it is present depends on the scale, additive (difference) or multiplicative (ratio).
effektmodifikation.beispiel: The relative risk of a treatment is 2 in both age groups. The baseline risk is 0.1 and 0.3. The risk difference is 0.1 and 0.3. No modification on the ratio scale, but modification on the difference scale.
effektmodifikation.vorsicht: The finding of modification depends on the scale. It needs enough cases in the groups and a test planned in advance.

effizienz.kurz: Which of two estimators varies less? Of two unbiased estimators, the more efficient one has the smaller variance. Its values lie closer together from sample to sample.
effizienz.beispiel: For normally distributed data and large n, the median as an estimator of the centre has about 1.57 times (π/2) the variance of the mean.
effizienz.vorsicht: This holds for this distribution. With very heavy tails or outliers the median can be more efficient.

efron-breslow.kurz: When several events occur at the same time, their order is unknown (a tie). Breslow and Efron are two approximations for how these ties are handled in the partial likelihood. Efron is more accurate, Breslow simpler.
efron-breslow.beispiel: Two people die on the same day with 20 at risk. Breslow keeps both in the risk set of the first death; Efron weights this more exactly.
efron-breslow.vorsicht: With few ties the results hardly differ. With many, Breslow can underestimate the effects.

egger-test.kurz: Do small studies differ conspicuously from large ones? The Egger test checks whether the funnel plot is lopsided. It regresses effect / standard error on 1 / standard error. An intercept far from 0 points to asymmetry.
egger-test.beispiel: An intercept of 2.1 with p = 0.03 across 15 studies would be a sign of asymmetry in the funnel plot.
egger-test.vorsicht: Asymmetry has causes other than publication bias. With fewer than about 10 studies the test is often not recommended.

eigenvektor.kurz: A direction that a matrix only stretches or shrinks but does not turn. The stretching factor is the matching eigenvalue. In factor analysis and principal component analysis, eigenvectors give the directions of the factors or components.
eigenvektor.beispiel: The matrix with rows (2, 1) and (1, 2) has the direction (1, 1) as an eigenvector. There it acts with factor 3, and in the direction (-1, 1) with factor 1.
eigenvektor.vorsicht: The sign of an eigenvector is arbitrary. A program may flip it without changing anything.

einfache-regression.kurz: Predicting an outcome from exactly one predictor. Simple linear regression has the equation y = b₀ + b₁ · x with an intercept b₀ and a slope b₁.
einfache-regression.beispiel: For 8 people: intercept 44.04, slope 4.13 points per study hour, R² = 0.933.
einfache-regression.vorsicht: The slope holds on average for the group, not for every single person.

einfache-zufallsstichprobe.kurz: How does one draw purely by lot? In a simple random sample every possible selection of n elements has the same chance. So every single element also has the same chance of being drawn.
einfache-zufallsstichprobe.beispiel: 2 of 5 persons: there are 10 possible pairs, each with chance 0.1. Each person has chance 0.4.
einfache-zufallsstichprobe.vorsicht: The basic formulas for standard errors and intervals mostly assume this case. For other sampling plans they do not fit without adjustment.

einfacher-haupteffekt.kurz: How does one factor act when the other stays at a fixed level? A simple main effect compares the levels of one factor separately at each level of the other. It is often computed after an important interaction.
einfacher-haupteffekt.beispiel: Light without fertiliser: 10 against 14 cm, F(1, 8) = 24, p = 0.0012. Light with fertiliser: 12 against 20 cm, F(1, 8) = 96, p < 0.0001. Error term from the whole model.
einfacher-haupteffekt.vorsicht: Each simple main effect is a test of its own. With several of them the significance level is often adjusted.
einfacher-haupteffekt.statable: Under the two-way analysis of variance as “Simple effects” (error term of the whole model). With two repeated-measures factors under “Simple main effects”: a separate analysis of variance per level, adjusted by Holm.

einfachstruktur.kurz: The ideal picture of a loading matrix: each item loads high on exactly one factor and near zero on the others. Rotations such as varimax or oblimin seek an approximation to it.
einfachstruktur.beispiel: Of eight items, four load high on factor 1 and hardly on factor 2, the other four the other way round. This is a clear simple structure.
einfachstruktur.vorsicht: Real data rarely achieve it. Simple structure is a goal of rotation, not proof that the factors are correct.

einfaktorielle-anova.kurz: Does a measured value depend on which group someone belongs to? One-way analysis of variance compares the means of two or more groups that differ in exactly one factor. With two groups it gives the same result as the t test assuming equal spreads.
einfaktorielle-anova.beispiel: Means 5, 7 and 9 with 4 values each: F(2, 9) = 24.0; p = 0.00025.
einfaktorielle-anova.vorsicht: It assumes independent observations, roughly normally distributed deviations and similar spreads. When the spreads differ a lot, Welch's ANOVA is the alternative.

einflussreiche-werte.kurz: Which cases determine the result out of proportion? Influential observations are cases whose removal clearly changes the coefficients or predictions. This usually takes both an unusual predictor value (leverage) and a large distance from the line.
einflussreiche-werte.beispiel: One person with 9 hours and 30 points added to 8 people with a slope of 4.13: the slope falls to 0.72.
einflussreiche-werte.vorsicht: An outlier is not automatically influential, and an influential case is not automatically an error. What changes with and without it should be reported.

einstichproben-t-test.kurz: Does the mean of one group fit a given value? The one-sample t test compares the mean of a sample with a fixed target value. Its degrees of freedom are n - 1.
einstichproben-t-test.beispiel: 8 measurements, mean 5.30, SD 0.35, target 5.0: t = 2.42 with 7 degrees of freedom, p = 0.046.
einstichproben-t-test.vorsicht: The target must be fixed beforehand. The result concerns the means, not single measurements.

elastic-net.kurz: How can selection and stability be combined? The elastic net mixes the penalties of lasso and ridge. It can set coefficients to 0 and tends to keep related predictors together.
elastic-net.beispiel: Mixing value 0.5: half lasso, half ridge.
elastic-net.vorsicht: Besides the strength of the penalty the mixture must be chosen too, usually by cross-validation.

elementarereignis.kurz: A single outcome of a random experiment that cannot be split further. Every event consists of one or more such outcomes.
elementarereignis.beispiel: Rolling a die twice: (3, 5) is an elementary event. “Sum 8” consists of 5 of them: (2,6), (3,5), (4,4), (5,3), (6,2).

em-algorithmus.kurz: An iterative method for estimating parameters when part of the information is missing, such as group membership or missing values. In the E step the missing part is expected under the current parameters, in the M step the parameters are re-estimated.
em-algorithmus.beispiel: In a mixture of two normal distributions, the E step estimates the probability that each case belongs to group 1. The M step uses it to compute new means.
em-algorithmus.vorsicht: The method increases the likelihood at every step but can end in a local maximum. Several starting values are needed.

empirical-bayes.kurz: A method in which the prior distribution is estimated from the data themselves instead of fixed in advance. Single estimates are pulled towards the overall mean.
empirical-bayes.beispiel: The batting averages of many players are considered together. The prior distribution is estimated from them, and each average is combined with it.
empirical-bayes.vorsicht: The data are used twice, for the prior and for the estimate. The uncertainty of the prior is usually underestimated.

empirie.kurz: Is a statement based on observation or measurement? Then it is empirical (grounded in experience and data). Empirical work collects and analyses such observations, as opposed to reasoning alone.
empirie.beispiel: Whether sleep duration and memory are related is tested empirically: a memory test in 40 people, together with their measured sleep time.

empirische-regel.kurz: In a normal distribution about 68% of values lie within one standard deviation of the mean, about 95% within two and about 99.7% within three. It gives a quick overview of the spread.
empirische-regel.beispiel: Mean 170, standard deviation 10: about 68% lie between 160 and 180, about 95% between 150 and 190.
empirische-regel.vorsicht: It holds only for roughly normally distributed data. More exactly the shares are 68.27%, 95.45% and 99.73%; for exactly 95% it is 1.96 standard deviations.

endlichkeitskorrektur.kurz: If a large part of a small population is studied, the estimate is more precise than the usual formula assumes. The standard error is reduced by the factor √((N - n) / (N - 1)). This is the finite population correction.
endlichkeitskorrektur.beispiel: N = 500 people, n = 100 surveyed: factor √(400 / 499) = 0.895. The standard error drops by a good 10%.
endlichkeitskorrektur.vorsicht: It is often said to matter only from about 5% of the population on. It applies only to sampling without replacement.

endogenitaet.kurz: An explanatory variable is endogenous if it is related to the error term, for example through omitted variables, measurement error or reciprocal effects. The estimate is then biased. Exogenous means it is not related to the error term.
endogenitaet.beispiel: People who take more tutoring have worse grades, because worse grades lead to more tutoring. Tutoring is endogenous.
endogenitaet.vorsicht: Endogeneity cannot be seen from the residuals, because by construction residuals are uncorrelated with the predictors. It follows from the design of the study.

entscheidungsbaum.kurz: A method that splits cases into groups through a series of yes-no questions. Each branching uses the variable and threshold that separate the groups best. At the end of each branch is a prediction. The tree is easy to read.
entscheidungsbaum.beispiel: Question 1: age over 40? Question 2: smoker? At the end of a branch is the share of people with the illness in that group.
entscheidungsbaum.vorsicht: A deep tree adapts to chance quirks of the data (overfitting). Small changes in the data can produce a very different tree.

entscheidungskurve.titel: Decision curve (decision curve analysis, net benefit)
entscheidungskurve.kurz: A method for judging the practical value of a prediction model. The net benefit is the share of true positives minus the share of false positives, weighted by the odds of the threshold. It is shown for all reasonable thresholds.
entscheidungskurve.beispiel: 200 people, 40 true positive, 20 false positive, threshold 20 %: net benefit = 40/200 - 20/200 · (0.2/0.8) = 0.175.
entscheidungskurve.vorsicht: The threshold reflects how heavily a false alarm weighs against a missed case. It is a decision, not a property of the model.

epidemie-pandemie.kurz: Epidemic: a disease occurs in a region temporarily much more often than expected. Pandemic: an epidemic that affects many countries or continents. Endemic: a disease is present in a region permanently at about constant frequency.
epidemie-pandemie.beispiel: A flu wave in a city is an epidemic. If it spreads worldwide, it is a pandemic. Malaria in some areas is endemic.
epidemie-pandemie.vorsicht: The words describe spread, not severity. Where the line to an epidemic lies is a decision.

epsilon-quadrat.kurz: What share of the total variation is due to the groups? Like ω², ε² is a less biased estimate than η². It subtracts from the group share what chance alone would be expected to give.
epsilon-quadrat.beispiel: Same numbers as for ω²: sum of squares between 40, within 160, total 200, 3 groups, 63 people. η² = 0.20, ε² = 0.17.
epsilon-quadrat.vorsicht: The name is also used for a measure after the Kruskal-Wallis test, where ε² = H / (n - 1). The formula should therefore always be stated.

epv.kurz: A rule of thumb for sample size in logistic and Cox regression: for each predictor at least about 10 cases with the rarer outcome should be available. The smaller of the two groups is decisive.
epv.beispiel: 80 people with the event allow by the rule at most 80/10 = 8 predictors, no matter how many people are in the study overall.
epv.vorsicht: The number 10 is a habit. Newer work recommends calculating the sample size from the desired precision of the prediction.

ereignis.kurz: A statement about the outcome of a random experiment that can be true or not. It is described as a subset of the sample space. Its probability can be stated.
ereignis.beispiel: Rolling a die twice, event “sum 8”: 5 of 36 outcomes, so 5/36 = 0.139.

ergebnisraum.kurz: The set of all outcomes a random experiment can have. Each outcome appears exactly once. The usual symbol is the capital Greek letter omega (Ω).
ergebnisraum.beispiel: Three coin tosses: Ω has 8 outcomes, from HHH through HHT to TTT (H = heads, T = tails).

erinnerungsverzerrung.kurz: People remember past events incompletely or differently depending on their situation. This is a problem especially in case-control studies, because the ill search for causes harder than the healthy.
erinnerungsverzerrung.beispiel: Parents of ill children recall earlier exposures more often than parents of healthy children.
erinnerungsverzerrung.vorsicht: The bias does not come from deliberate false statements but from unequal remembering.

erwartungstreue.kurz: Does an estimator hit the true value on average? An estimator is unbiased if its average over all possible samples equals the unknown value exactly. It is not systematically too high or too low.
erwartungstreue.beispiel: Population 2, 4, 6, all 9 samples with n = 2 (with replacement): the sample means average 4, exactly the population mean.
erwartungstreue.vorsicht: Unbiased does not mean that one single sample is right. The variance s² is unbiased, the standard deviation s is not quite.

erwartungswert.kurz: The value around which a random variable fluctuates on average. It is formed by weighting each possible value by its probability and adding up. It is the counterpart of a sample mean.
erwartungswert.vorsicht: The expected value need not be a possible value. A die never shows 3.5.

esd-test.kurz: An outlier test that checks for up to a pre-set number r of outliers at once. It removes the most extreme value step by step and compares each step with a critical value.
esd-test.beispiel: With 50 values, the check is for at most 3 outliers. The test finds how many of them are actually conspicuous.
esd-test.vorsicht: The upper limit r has to be chosen in advance. Like Grubbs it assumes approximately normal data.

et-al.kurz: Abbreviation of the Latin “et alii”: “and others”. In references, “et al.” follows the first name when there are several authors. From how many names onward the list is shortened depends on the citation style.
et-al.beispiel: Kramer et al. (2021) describe the method.

ethnografie.kurz: A way of researching in which the researchers take part in and observe a field over a long time in order to understand ways of life, rules and meanings from within. It uses observation, conversation and documents.
ethnografie.beispiel: A researcher accompanies the daily life of a hospital ward for three months and notes observations and conversations.
ethnografie.vorsicht: The presence of the researchers can change the field. The results hold for the field studied and cannot be transferred without further steps.

euklidisch.kurz: The ordinary straight-line distance, extended to several variables. It is the square root of the sum of the squared differences on each variable. It is the most widely used distance measure.
euklidisch.beispiel: Two cases (1, 2) and (4, 6): square root of 3² + 4² = square root of 25 = 5.
euklidisch.vorsicht: Variables with a large range count for more, so standardising first is usual. If the variables are strongly related, the Mahalanobis distance is better suited.

evaluation.kurz: The systematic assessment of a measure, programme or procedure against fixed criteria using data. Questions concern implementation, effect, benefit and cost. Formative evaluation accompanies and improves, summative draws a conclusion.
evaluation.beispiel: A reading support programme is evaluated after one year: was it implemented as planned, and did the participants' reading scores improve compared with a comparison group?
evaluation.vorsicht: An evaluation shows an effect only if it contains a comparison. A before-after finding without a comparison group is not sufficient.

evidenz.kurz: From Latin evidentia: “clearness”. In technical use, the strength of the support the data give for a statement. It does not mean “obvious” and not “proof”. Evidence comes in degrees.
evidenz.beispiel: The data give weak evidence for a difference between the groups.

evidenzpyramide.kurz: A picture that ranks study types by the strength of their evidence for the effect of a measure. At the top are systematic reviews and randomised trials, below them cohort and case-control studies, at the bottom case reports and expert opinions.
evidenzpyramide.beispiel: On the question of whether a therapy works, pooled randomised trials count for more than a single case series.
evidenzpyramide.vorsicht: The pyramid holds for questions of effect; other questions fit other orders. A poorly done randomised trial can be worth less than a good observational study.

ex-ante-ex-post.kurz: Latin for “from before” and “from after”. Ex ante: before the event, as a plan or forecast. Ex post: in hindsight. A power analysis ex ante plans the sample size; computed ex post from the observed effect, it says little.
ex-ante-ex-post.beispiel: Ex ante the sample size is calculated; ex post, what actually occurred is analysed.

exakter-test.kurz: Is the p value computed exactly or only approximated? An exact test uses the exact distribution of the test statistic, without approximating it by a smooth curve. This matters especially for small samples or rare events.
exakter-test.beispiel: 10 coin tosses give heads 9 times. The exact binomial test against 0.5 gives p = 0.021 (two-sided).
exakter-test.vorsicht: Exact refers to how the p value is computed, not to the truth of the result. An exact test still rests on its assumptions.

exogen-endogen.titel: Exogenous and endogenous variables (in a structural model)
exogen-endogen.kurz: Exogenous means not explained by the model; it acts from outside. Endogenous means explained in the model by other variables. In a path diagram an exogenous variable has only outgoing arrows, an endogenous one at least one incoming arrow.
exogen-endogen.beispiel: Education is exogenous. Income is explained by education and is endogenous. Satisfaction is explained by income, also endogenous.
exogen-endogen.vorsicht: What is exogenous is set by the model, not by the nature of the variable. A variable can be exogenous in one model and endogenous in another.

experiment.kurz: What happens when something is changed on purpose? In an experiment the researchers decide who gets which condition, usually at random (randomisation), and then compare the outcome.
experiment.beispiel: 60 people are randomly assigned to two learning methods, then all take the same test.
experiment.vorsicht: A cause can be inferred only if assignment was random and the study was run cleanly. Without random assignment it is a quasi-experiment.

experimentalgruppe.kurz: The group that receives the condition or treatment under study.
experimentalgruppe.beispiel: 20 people practise with the new app for ten minutes a day (experimental group), 20 practise without it (control group).

explizit-implizit.kurz: From Latin explicare “to unfold” and implicare “to enfold”. Explicit: stated outright. Implicit: tacitly meant. Methods contain implicit assumptions that need checking.
explizit-implizit.beispiel: The pooled t test implicitly assumes equal variances; the Welch test does not.

explorativ.kurz: Is something striking being looked for? Exploratory means: data are searched without a fixed prediction, to find patterns and ideas. The results are leads, not confirmation.
explorativ.beispiel: With 15 variables, all 105 pairs are correlated to see what stands out.
explorativ.vorsicht: With many comparisons, a few striking results are to be expected by chance alone. They have to be confirmed on new data.

exponentialfamilie.kurz: A group of distributions with a common mathematical form, including the normal, binomial, Poisson, gamma and exponential distributions. Generalised linear models rest on this form.
exponentialfamilie.beispiel: The Poisson distribution belongs to it. Poisson regression can therefore be treated in the same framework as linear and logistic regression.
exponentialfamilie.vorsicht: The name has nothing to do with the exponential distribution alone, which is only one member.

exponentialverteilung.kurz: How long does it take until the next event if events happen at random at a steady rate? The exponential distribution describes this waiting time. It has no memory: someone who has already waited does not wait less.
exponentialverteilung.beispiel: On average a customer arrives every 2 minutes (rate 0.5 per minute). It takes longer than 3 minutes with probability 0.223.
exponentialverteilung.vorsicht: It only fits a steady rate. If failures become more likely with age, the Weibull distribution fits better.

exponentiell.kurz: From Latin exponere: “to set out”. An exponent is a power. Exponential growth: in each period the value grows by the same factor; the increase is proportional to the current value. With the logarithm it becomes a straight line.
exponentiell.beispiel: If a value doubles every 3 days, it goes 1, 2, 4, 8, 16: exponential.

exponentielle-glaettung.kurz: How can a series be smoothed so that recent values count more? In exponential smoothing, each new value is a weighted mean of the new observation and the previous smoothed value. The weight is called α.
exponentielle-glaettung.vorsicht: This α is not the significance level. A large α follows the series closely, a small one smooths strongly.

extern.kurz: From Latin externus “outside” and internus “inside”. Internal: valid within the study. External: transferable beyond the study, or lying outside the data, like an external criterion. These are different questions.
extern.beispiel: A lab experiment can be very informative internally yet hardly transferable to everyday life externally.

externe-validitaet.kurz: Does the result hold elsewhere? External validity describes how far results carry over to other people, places and times.
externe-validitaet.beispiel: A learning training works for students in a lab. Whether it also works for working adults in daily life is not settled by that.

extremwertverteilung.kurz: A distribution for maxima or minima of many values, such as the highest flood level of a year. The Gumbel, Fréchet and Weibull distributions belong to the extreme value distributions.
extremwertverteilung.beispiel: The highest water level is taken from each week. The distribution of these weekly maxima follows an extreme value distribution rather than a normal distribution.
extremwertverteilung.vorsicht: Maxima behave differently from means, and the normal distribution usually does not fit them. Extrapolating far beyond the data stays uncertain.

f-ff.kurz: “f.” stands for “and the following page”, “ff.” for “and the following pages”. Today page ranges like pp. 12-15 are more exact. The Latin forms are sq. and sqq.

f-test-varianzen.kurz: Do two groups spread differently? The F test for two variances divides the larger variance by the smaller. Under H₀ of equal variances, the quotient follows the F distribution with the two degrees of freedom.
f-test-varianzen.beispiel: Two groups of 21 people each, SD 6 and 3: F = 36 / 9 = 4, degrees of freedom 20 and 20, p = 0.003 (two-sided).
f-test-varianzen.vorsicht: The test reacts strongly to departures from the normal distribution. As a pre-check before a t test it is mostly not recommended; the Welch test is better right away.

f-verteilung.kurz: How large is the ratio of two variances when there is no difference? The F distribution describes this ratio. It has two degrees of freedom (numerator and denominator), only values from 0 upward, and is stretched to the right.
f-verteilung.beispiel: With 2 and 27 degrees of freedom, F is larger than 3.354 in only 5% of cases when three groups do not differ.
f-verteilung.vorsicht: The order of the two degrees of freedom matters. Swapping numerator and denominator gives a different distribution.

f1-score.kurz: The harmonic mean of sensitivity (recall) and positive predictive value (precision). It is high only if both are high. It equals 2TP/(2TP + FP + FN).
f1-score.beispiel: 40 true positive, 10 false negative, 20 false positive: sensitivity 0.80, predictive value 0.67, F1 = 80/110 = 0.73.
f1-score.vorsicht: True negatives do not enter. The F1 score has to be read differently for rare events than for common ones.

fagan.kurz: A calculation aid that gives the posttest probability from the pretest probability and the likelihood ratio of a test. Behind it: posttest odds = pretest odds × likelihood ratio.
fagan.beispiel: Pretest probability 10 % (odds 1 to 9), positive likelihood ratio 9: posttest odds 1, probability 50 %.
fagan.vorsicht: The calculation holds only if the pretest probability fits the person. The likelihood ratio is an assumption about the test.

fail-safe.kurz: The number of unfound studies with an effect of zero that would be needed to make the combined result of a meta-analysis no longer significant. It is meant to quantify the danger of publication bias.
fail-safe.beispiel: 10 studies with the sum of z values 25: N = 25²/2.706 - 10 = 221 further studies with zero effect would be needed.
fail-safe.vorsicht: The method is hardly recommended today because it rests on p values instead of effects and has no realistic yardstick. Better are the funnel plot, trim-and-fill and selection models.

fair-open-data.kurz: FAIR stands for findable, accessible, interoperable and reusable. It describes how research data should be designed. Open data are freely accessible, but FAIR does not necessarily mean open.
fair-open-data.beispiel: A dataset has a persistent identifier, a description, an open file format and a clear licence. It is FAIR even if access is regulated.
fair-open-data.vorsicht: Open and FAIR are different things. Personal data may often be accessible only in a restricted way.

faking.kurz: A person answers a test deliberately differently from the truth, usually to look better or worse. It occurs mainly in selection situations.
faking.beispiel: Applicants tick the highest option for “I am reliable”, even if this is only partly true.
faking.vorsicht: Faking is not the same as social desirability, which can also work unconsciously.

faktor.kurz: Which grouping is being studied? A factor is the independent variable of an analysis of variance. Its values are called levels and form the groups or conditions that are compared.
faktor.beispiel: The factor “fertiliser” has the levels “none” and “with”.
faktor.vorsicht: The factor of an analysis of variance is not the same as a factor in factor analysis. There it is a summarising quantity that is not measured directly.

faktor-hoeherer-ordnung.kurz: A factor that explains the relations between first-order factors. The first-order factors are thus related through a common factor behind them.
faktor-hoeherer-ordnung.beispiel: Three factors (arithmetic, reading, writing) are correlated. A second-order factor “school achievement” explains these correlations.
faktor-hoeherer-ordnung.vorsicht: With exactly three first-order factors the model is just identified and always fits as well as a model with correlated factors. With two factors it is not identified.

faktorielles-design.kurz: Several influencing quantities at once: all combinations of the levels of several factors are studied. This shows whether the effect of one factor depends on the level of another.
faktorielles-design.beispiel: 2 study times and 3 methods give 2 x 3 = 6 conditions, each with its own group.

faktorstufe.kurz: Which values can the grouping take? A factor level is one of the groups or conditions of a factor. Two levels give two groups, three levels give three groups.
faktorstufe.beispiel: The factor “dose” with the three levels 0, 10 and 20 mg.
faktorstufe.vorsicht: With more than two levels, the F test only shows that a difference exists somewhere, not between which levels.

faktorwert.kurz: An estimated position of a person on a factor. From the answers to all items, one value per factor is computed, weighted by the loadings. The factor itself is not measured, so the value is an estimate.
faktorwert.beispiel: A person with high answers on all items of the factor “curiosity” gets a standardised factor score of 1.2. That is 1.2 standard deviations above average.
faktorwert.vorsicht: There are several estimation methods, for example regression and Bartlett, giving slightly different values. A simple sum of the items is often used instead.

faktorwert-methoden.titel: Methods for computing factor scores (regression, Bartlett, Anderson-Rubin)
faktorwert-methoden.kurz: Different ways to estimate a person's value on a factor from the items. The regression method (Thomson) gives the best prediction but correlated scores. Bartlett gives unbiased scores. Anderson-Rubin gives uncorrelated, standardised scores.
faktorwert-methoden.beispiel: With two orthogonal factors, the regression scores are slightly correlated with each other, the Anderson-Rubin scores are not.
faktorwert-methoden.vorsicht: Factor scores are estimates and not unique. The method has to be stated.

fakultaet.kurz: n! is the product of all whole numbers from 1 to n. It gives the number of ways n different things can be put in a row. By definition 0! = 1.

fall-kohorten-studie.kurz: A random sample (subcohort) is drawn from the cohort, and all cases are added. The same subcohort can serve as the comparison for several diseases.
fall-kohorten-studie.beispiel: 500 of 10 000 people are drawn at random. All 200 people who fall ill are added, even if they were not in the random sample.
fall-kohorten-studie.vorsicht: The analysis has to allow for the way people were selected, with special weighting.

fall-kontroll-studie.kurz: Working backwards from the outcome: people with a disease (cases) are compared with similar people without it (controls). The question is who was exposed to a factor earlier.
fall-kontroll-studie.beispiel: 150 people with a rare disease and 300 without are asked about earlier contact with a substance.
fall-kontroll-studie.vorsicht: Because the number of cases is fixed, disease rates cannot be calculated. The suitable measure is the odds ratio.

fallauswahl.titel: Purposive case selection (extreme, typical, deviant, maximum variation)
fallauswahl.kurz: Strategies for choosing cases for a study deliberately. Extreme cases show the special, typical ones the usual, deviant cases contradict an expectation. Maximum variation chooses cases as different as possible to show the range.
fallauswahl.beispiel: For a case study of schools, a particularly successful, a particularly weak and an average school are chosen.
fallauswahl.vorsicht: Purposive choice does not allow scaling up to the population. The selection criteria must be disclosed.

fallzahlplanung.kurz: How many cases does a study need? Sample size planning fixes the sample size before data collection, to match the desired precision or the desired power.
fallzahlplanung.beispiel: Share accurate to ±0.05, 95%, worst case p = 0.5: n = 1.96² · 0.25 / 0.05² = 384.2, so at least 385.
fallzahlplanung.vorsicht: Losses come on top: with an expected 30% nonresponse, more persons must be approached. The assumptions of the plan are estimates.

falsifikation.kurz: From Latin falsus “false” and facere “to make”: refutation. According to Popper a statement is scientific if observations could contradict it. Statements about probabilities cannot be refuted strictly; tests give only indications.
falsifikation.beispiel: “All children make at most two errors” is refuted by a single child with three errors.

fang-wiederfang.kurz: A method for estimating the size of a population that cannot be counted completely. M animals are caught and marked. In a second catch of C animals, R are marked. The estimate is N = M · C / R.
fang-wiederfang.beispiel: 200 animals are marked. In the second catch of 150, 30 are marked. N = 200 · 150 / 30 = 1000.
fang-wiederfang.vorsicht: It assumes that each animal has the same chance of being caught, the population is closed and marks are not lost.

fdr.kurz: How many of the reported hits are likely to be false? The false discovery rate (FDR) is the expected proportion of false rejections among all rejections. It is used with very many tests and is less strict than protecting against every single error.
fdr.beispiel: If 50 findings are reported as significant at an FDR of 10%, at most about 5 of them are false on average.
fdr.vorsicht: The FDR holds on average over many analyses. It does not say which findings are false, and it is not the same as α.

fehlendcode.kurz: A number or label that means “no answer” in the file, such as 99 or -9. The file treats it as missing only once it is declared so. Otherwise it is calculated with like a real value.
fehlendcode.beispiel: Ages 20, 30 and 99 (= unknown): the mean would be 49.7. Without the missing-value code it is 25.
fehlendcode.vorsicht: The code must lie outside all possible real values. The codebook should describe it in a line.

fehlende-werte.kurz: Information that is not available for a case and a variable. Reasons include refused answers, measurement failures or oversights. How much is missing and why decides which approach fits.
fehlende-werte.beispiel: Among 200 people, income is missing for 14: 14 of 200 is 7%.
fehlende-werte.vorsicht: Missing values are not entered as 0. A code such as 99 counts as missing only if the file declares it so.

fehler-1-art.kurz: How often is an effect reported that does not exist? A type I error occurs when H₀ is rejected although it is true. Its probability is at most the significance level α.
fehler-1-art.beispiel: If H₀ is true in each of 100 independent tests, about 5 of them are wrongly rejected on average at α = 0.05.
fehler-1-art.vorsicht: Whether a single study contains a type I error stays unknown. α describes only the long-run rate.

fehler-2-art.kurz: How often is an existing effect missed? A type II error occurs when H₀ is not rejected although H₁ is true. Its probability is called β and equals 1 minus power.
fehler-2-art.beispiel: With a true effect of d = 0.5 and 20 people per group, power is 0.34. The effect is missed with probability about 0.66.
fehler-2-art.vorsicht: β holds only for an assumed effect. For a smaller effect, β is larger.

fehlerkorrekturmodell.kurz: A model for cointegrated series. It describes short-run changes and the return to the long-run equilibrium: the further the series are from equilibrium, the stronger the correction in the next step.
fehlerkorrekturmodell.beispiel: If the price at place A departs by 4 from the price at place B and the correction coefficient is -0.25, about 1 unit of the gap is closed in the next step.
fehlerkorrekturmodell.vorsicht: The model assumes that the series are cointegrated. The correction coefficient must be negative, otherwise there is no return.

fehlerrate-pro-vergleich.kurz: The probability of a type I error in a single test, that is the usual α. It is distinct from the familywise error rate, which refers to at least one error in the whole group of tests.
fehlerrate-pro-vergleich.beispiel: Each of 20 tests has α = 0.05. The per-comparison error rate is 0.05, the familywise rate without correction 1 - 0.95²⁰ = 0.64.
fehlerrate-pro-vergleich.vorsicht: Anyone who controls only the per-comparison error rate accepts one or more false alarms when there are many tests.

fehlerterm.kurz: What does the model leave open? The error term ε collects in the model equation everything besides the predictors that acts on the outcome, including measurement error and chance. It belongs to the population model and cannot be observed.
fehlerterm.beispiel: y = 44 + 4.1 · x + ε: two people with 5 study hours each score differently. The difference sits in ε.
fehlerterm.vorsicht: The error term (model, not observable) and the residual (sample, calculated) are different things. The usual tests assume ε to be independent, equally spread and mostly normal.

fehlklassifikation.kurz: A person or observation is put into the wrong category, for example ill instead of healthy or exposed instead of unexposed. Non-differential means equally frequent in all comparison groups. Differential means unequally frequent.
fehlklassifikation.beispiel: A test with a sensitivity of 0.8 wrongly classifies 20 of 100 ill people as healthy.
fehlklassifikation.vorsicht: Non-differential errors usually weaken a relation towards zero when there are two categories. Differential errors bias in any direction.

fester-effekt.kurz: Does an effect apply equally to everyone? A fixed effect is a coefficient estimated as one single value for the whole population. In mixed models it sits next to the random effects.
fester-effekt.beispiel: With each dose step, blood pressure falls by 3 mmHg on average. This one value applies to all practices in the model.
fester-effekt.vorsicht: A fixed effect does not mean that the effect is really the same for everyone. It only means the model estimates one common average.

fester-faktor.kurz: Are exactly these levels of interest? A fixed factor has levels that were chosen on purpose and stand for themselves. The conclusions apply to exactly these levels.
fester-faktor.beispiel: Dose 0, 10 and 20 mg: the question is about these three doses, not about a sample of all possible ones.
fester-faktor.vorsicht: A two-level factor such as sex, or a treatment arm, is also a fixed factor. Generalising to other levels is not covered.

filterfrage.kurz: A question after which only part of the respondents are routed on. Those who meet the condition of the filter question get the follow-up questions; the others skip them. Only questions that fit the person are asked.
filterfrage.beispiel: “Is there a car in the household?” is the filter question. Only those who say “yes” get the questions on use.
filterfrage.vorsicht: For analysis: for the follow-up questions the base is smaller. Skipping is not the same as a missing answer.

fiml.kurz: A method that uses all available information from each person when values are missing, without dropping cases or replacing values. The likelihood is built from the variables observed for each person.
fiml.beispiel: Of 300 people, 40 have single answers missing. FIML uses all 300 cases and their available information.
fiml.vorsicht: It holds under the MAR assumption and approximately normal data. Under MNAR the estimate stays biased.

fisher-ansatz.kurz: How strongly do the data speak against H₀? In the Fisher approach, the p value is taken as a measure of how well or badly the data fit H₀. There is no fixed threshold, no H₁ and no decision rule with fixed error rates.
fisher-ansatz.beispiel: With p = 0.03, exactly this value is reported: a clear hint that the data fit H₀ poorly, nothing more.
fisher-ansatz.vorsicht: p is not the probability that H₀ is true. It is the probability of such or more extreme data if H₀ holds.

fisher-exakt.kurz: Are two characteristics related when the table is too small for the chi-square test? Fisher's exact test computes the p value without approximation from all tables with the same marginal totals. It is mainly used for 2x2 tables.
fisher-exakt.beispiel: 5 of 6 improved in group A, 2 of 8 in group B: two-sided p value 0.103. The smallest expected frequency is 3.
fisher-exakt.vorsicht: Exact means no approximation. The test can still be cautious because it treats the marginal totals as given.

fisher-index.kurz: The geometric mean of the Laspeyres and Paasche price indices: √(L · P). It balances the biases of both indices and passes the time reversal test (swapping the periods gives the reciprocal).
fisher-index.vorsicht: Like the Paasche index it needs quantities of each period and is therefore more laborious. It cannot be calculated from one period alone.
sw: geometric mean of Laspeyres and Paasche

fisher-information.kurz: A measure of how much the data reveal about a parameter. The steeper and narrower the likelihood curve around its maximum, the greater the information. The reciprocal of the information gives the smallest possible variance of an unbiased estimator.
fisher-information.beispiel: For a proportion p from n observations the information is n/(p(1 - p)). With n = 100 and p = 0.3 that is 476. The standard error is 1/√476 = 0.046.
fisher-information.vorsicht: The information depends on the true parameter and is evaluated at the estimate.

fisher-lsd.kurz: A post hoc procedure that compares all pairs with ordinary t tests based on the pooled spread, without adjusting the error. It is called protected if used only after a significant F test of the analysis of variance.
fisher-lsd.beispiel: With three groups, after a significant F test each pair is tested at α = 0.05.
fisher-lsd.vorsicht: With more than three groups the familywise type I error rises above α, so a correction such as Tukey or Holm is used.

fixed-effect-modell.kurz: Is there a single true effect for all studies? The fixed-effect model assumes so. Differences between studies are then pure chance. Each study is weighted by 1 / variance.
fixed-effect-modell.beispiel: Three studies with weights 100, 25 and 44.4: overall effect 0.277, standard error 0.077.
fixed-effect-modell.vorsicht: The overall effect is a common effect only if all studies measure the same thing. With visible heterogeneity the interval is too narrow, and the random-effects model usually fits better.

flaechendiagramm.kurz: A line chart in which the area under the line is filled. It shows how a quantity changes over time. Stacked, it also shows the parts of a whole.
flaechendiagramm.beispiel: Energy use per year is shown as an area, split into oil, gas and electricity. The total height is the total use.
flaechendiagramm.vorsicht: In stacked areas, only the bottom layer can be compared well. The baseline should start at 0.

fleiss-kappa.kurz: An agreement measure for more than two raters sorting cases into nominal categories. Like Cohen's kappa it corrects for chance agreement. It does not require the same persons to rate all cases.
fleiss-kappa.beispiel: 4 cases, 3 raters, 2 categories. Per case (3/0), (2/1), (0/3), (1/2). Mean agreement 0.67, expected by chance 0.50: κ = (0.67 - 0.50)/(1 - 0.50) = 0.33.
fleiss-kappa.vorsicht: The categories must be nominal. For ordered categories, Krippendorff's alpha or weighted kappa suits better.

fligner-killeen.kurz: A test for equal spread in several groups that works with ranks. It is very robust against departures from normality.
fligner-killeen.beispiel: Four groups with values containing outliers: the Fligner-Killeen test keeps the check for equal spread stable where the Bartlett test and the F test would fail.
fligner-killeen.vorsicht: It tests spread but assumes a similar distribution shape in the groups.

fokusgruppe.kurz: A guided discussion of a small group on a topic, usually with 6 to 10 people. It shows how opinions arise and change in conversation. The data are the statements of the group.
fokusgruppe.beispiel: Eight parents discuss school routes for an hour, led by a moderator.
fokusgruppe.vorsicht: Dominant persons can shape the group, and the opinions are not independent of each other. Shares cannot be estimated from it.

follow-up.kurz: The later observation or re-collection after a first measurement, for example after six months. The longer the follow-up, the more people are often lost.
follow-up.beispiel: After the intervention, a follow-up takes place after six months.

forced-choice.kurz: Instead of rating each statement alone, the person must choose between options that seem equally desirable. This is meant to make faking harder. The points are shared between scales, and their sum is the same for everyone (ipsative).
forced-choice.beispiel: From “tidy”, “outgoing”, “creative”, the person picks the trait that fits best.
forced-choice.vorsicht: Ipsative scores show only the rank order of traits within a person. Comparisons between persons and the usual correlations between scales are limited; the scales are artificially negatively related.

forschungsdesign.kurz: How is the study set up? The research design (study design) fixes who is measured when, how often and under which conditions, and how groups are formed.
forschungsdesign.beispiel: Two groups, randomly assigned, each measured before and after the intervention: a randomised pre-post design with two groups.

forschungsfrage.kurz: What is the study meant to clarify? The research question names which quantities are looked at, in whom, and for what purpose. Hypotheses, measurement and analysis are derived from it.
forschungsfrage.beispiel: Do adults with and without a pet differ in the number of steps they take per day?

fragebogen.kurz: A set of questions, put in writing or electronically, used to record information, attitudes or behaviour.
fragebogen.beispiel: Twelve questions on sleep quality with five answer steps each, plus age and sex.
fragebogen.vorsicht: The answers are self-reports. They depend on how the question is understood, how good the memory is and how people choose to answer.

fragenreihenfolge.kurz: The answer to a question depends on which questions came before or in which order the response options stand. Earlier questions set a frame; later options are read differently.
fragenreihenfolge.beispiel: Someone first asked about problems at work rates overall satisfaction lower afterwards.
fragenreihenfolge.vorsicht: Remedies are rotated order of questions and options and testing in a pretest. Primacy and recency effects (what is named first or last is favoured) belong here too.

fragility-index.kurz: The smallest number of people whose outcome (such as event yes or no) would have to change for a significant result to become non-significant. It shows how narrow a result was.
fragility-index.beispiel: 100 against 100 people, 10 against 25 events, Fisher test p = 0.0085. Only with 4 additional events in the first group is p = 0.073. The fragility index is 4.
fragility-index.vorsicht: The index depends on sample size and number of events and is not a stand-alone statement about the quality of the study.
