frailty.kurz: Are there unobserved differences in susceptibility? Frailty is a random factor that changes the event rate of a person or group without having been measured. The model allows groups to be more or less at risk by themselves.
frailty.beispiel: Patients from 25 clinics: clinics can differ in event rate even if all measured characteristics are the same.
frailty.vorsicht: The word here does not mean frailty in the everyday sense. It is a statistical quantity for what was not recorded.

fraktionelles-design.kurz: Only a deliberately chosen part of all possible combinations of factor levels is run. This saves runs. In return, some effects can no longer be told apart, because they are mixed up with each other.
fraktionelles-design.beispiel: With 5 factors at 2 levels each there are 2⁵ = 32 combinations. A half fraction uses 16 of them.
fraktionelles-design.vorsicht: Sensible only if higher-order interactions can be regarded as negligible.

freeman-halton.kurz: The extension of Fisher's exact test to tables with more than two rows or columns. It tests independence exactly, without the chi-square approximation.
freeman-halton.beispiel: A 3 × 3 table with many small expected frequencies is tested exactly because chi-square is not reliable here.
freeman-halton.vorsicht: For large tables and samples the computation is heavy. Then testing is done approximately by simulation.
sw: exact test for r x c tables

frequentistisch.kurz: A view in which a probability is the share that the relative frequency approaches over very many repetitions. It belongs to processes that can be repeated.
frequentistisch.beispiel: Suppose a drawing pin tossed 1000 times lands point up 412 times: the share 0.412 estimates the probability of “point up”.
frequentistisch.vorsicht: A frequentist probability belongs to a process, not to a hypothesis. A p value is therefore not the probability that the hypothesis is true.

friedman.kurz: Do three or more conditions differ in the same people when only ranks count? Within each person the conditions are ranked. The test compares the rank sums of the conditions.
friedman.beispiel: 6 people rank 3 methods; rank sums 17, 12 and 7: χ² = 8.33 with 2 degrees of freedom, p = 0.016.
friedman.vorsicht: A person with a missing value usually drops out of the test altogether. A significant result does not show which conditions differ.

fuenf-punkte.kurz: What summarises the data briefly? The five-number summary gives the smallest value, Q1, median, Q3 and the largest value. It is the basis of the box plot.
fuenf-punkte.vorsicht: The R function fivenum() calculates the hinges differently (4 and 9 instead of 4.25 and 8.75). The quartiles can differ slightly by program.

funktion.kurz: From Latin functio: “performance”. A rule that assigns to each input value exactly one output value. In statistics: density function, distribution function, regression function.
funktion.beispiel: The equation y = 2 + 3x assigns exactly one y to each x: at x = 2 the result is 8.

g-studie.kurz: The G study splits the variation in scores into parts: persons, items, raters and their interplay. The D study uses this to calculate how reliable a planned measurement design would be, for example with more raters.
g-studie.beispiel: Essays are rated by several people. The G study shows that a large part of the variation comes from the severity of the raters. The D study calculates how many raters are needed.
g-studie.vorsicht: The results hold for the sources studied. New sources that were not included are missing from the result.

gam.kurz: A regression model in which each predictor acts through a smooth curve estimated from the data, rather than a straight line. The curves are added. It extends the generalised linear model.
gam.beispiel: Blood pressure depends on age through one curve and on weight through another. The shapes of the curves come from the data.
gam.vorsicht: The curves are best read graphically. Overly flexible curves lead to overfitting.

games-howell.kurz: Which groups differ when the spreads are different? The Games-Howell test compares all pairs without assuming equal spreads. It is the usual follow-up to Welch's ANOVA.
games-howell.beispiel: Two groups with variances 0.8 and 4.4 (6 values each), means 11 and 14: standard error 0.93, Welch degrees of freedom 6.76.
games-howell.vorsicht: With very small groups the test can be too liberal. The degrees of freedom here are not whole numbers.

gamma-mass.kurz: How strong is the association between two ordered categorical characteristics? Gamma compares concordant and discordant pairs: γ = (C - D)/(C + D). Ties are left out. Values from -1 to 1.
gamma-mass.beispiel: Training (rarely, sometimes, often) by fitness (low, medium, high), 100 people, rows 20, 10, 4 / 8, 16, 10 / 2, 10, 20: 1980 concordant, 396 discordant pairs. γ = 1584/2376 = 0.667.
gamma-mass.vorsicht: Because ties are ignored, gamma is often larger than tau-b or Somers' d when there are many ties.

gamma-verteilung.kurz: A distribution for values above 0 that is stretched to the right, such as waiting times until the k-th event or costs. It has two parameters, shape and rate. The exponential and χ² distributions are special cases.
gamma-verteilung.beispiel: Shape 2, rate 0.5 per minute: waiting time until the second customer. Mean 4 minutes, variance 8.
gamma-verteilung.vorsicht: The gamma distribution is given with a rate or with a scale (1 / rate). Programs use different conventions.

geburtenrate.kurz: The crude birth rate counts births per 1000 inhabitants and year. The total fertility rate (TFR) is the number of children a woman would have over her life if the rates of the individual ages of the year considered applied.
geburtenrate.beispiel: A TFR of 1.5 means: at today's age-specific rates a woman would have 1.5 children on average. Replacement of the parent generation lies at about 2.1.
geburtenrate.vorsicht: The TFR describes a year, not an actual woman's life. The crude rate depends on the age distribution.

gee.kurz: How can the average association be estimated when observations within groups or series are related? GEE estimates coefficients for the whole population. The dependence is handled through an assumed correlation structure, and the standard errors are robust.
gee.beispiel: Repeated yes/no measurements on 200 people: GEE estimates one average odds ratio across all people.
gee.vorsicht: GEE describes the average over the population, not the course of one single person. With missing values, stricter assumptions apply than in mixed models.

gegenereignis.kurz: The complement of A occurs exactly when A does not occur. Its probability is 1 minus that of A. This often helps when “at least once” is asked.

geheimhaltung.kurz: Measures that prevent conclusions about single persons or firms from published results. Typical are suppressing or merging cells with very few cases, rounding and altering values.
geheimhaltung.beispiel: A table shows cases by municipality and occupation. Cells with fewer than 3 cases are replaced by a dot so that no single person can be recognised.
geheimhaltung.vorsicht: A value “under 3” is not zero. When recalculating from totals, suppressed values can reappear.

gelegenheitsstichprobe.kurz: What if only those who are at hand can be reached? A convenience sample consists of the persons who are easy to reach. Who is selected is not random by design.
gelegenheitsstichprobe.beispiel: A study asks the students who eat in the canteen on one day.
gelegenheitsstichprobe.vorsicht: Intervals and p-values can be computed formally, but they assume random selection. A conclusion about a larger group is not supported.

gemeinsame-verteilung.kurz: It gives how likely each combination of values of two (or more) random variables is. From it, marginal distributions, conditional distributions and the association can be read.
gemeinsame-verteilung.beispiel: Rain and wind: rain+strong wind 0.2; rain+light wind 0.1; no rain+strong 0.1; no rain+light 0.6. Sum 1.

gemischte-anova.kurz: Do groups develop differently over time? Mixed analysis of variance combines a between-groups factor (different people) with a repeated-measures factor (the same people measured several times). The interaction of the two is usually the point.
gemischte-anova.beispiel: Suppose: Control and training, 4 people each, before and after. Means: control 11.5 and 12.5, training 11.5 and 17. Interaction F(1, 6) = 243; p < 0.001.
gemischte-anova.vorsicht: The interaction shows that the development differs. Whether the training caused it depends on the study design, above all on how people were assigned to the groups.

generalisierbarkeit.kurz: From Latin generalis: “general”. The question whether a result holds beyond the cases studied: for the population, for other places and times. It depends strongly on how the sample was chosen.
generalisierbarkeit.beispiel: A survey of students in one city says little about all adults.

generalisiertes-eta.kurz: How large is an effect so that it can be compared across designs? Generalised eta squared also puts the variation due to measured quantities, above all the people, in the denominator. The value then stays comparable whether or not repeated measures were used.
generalisiertes-eta.beispiel: Repeated measures with 5 people: time effect 25.6, error 1.07, people 36.93. Partial 25.6 / (25.6 + 1.07) = 0.96; generalised 25.6 / (25.6 + 1.07 + 36.93) = 0.403.
generalisiertes-eta.vorsicht: In purely between-groups designs with only experimentally set factors, ηG² equals the partial value. The difference shows up with repeated measures, measured factors (such as sex) and covariates.
generalisiertes-eta.statable: In the repeated-measures table ηG² stands next to the partial η², also with two repeated-measures factors and in the mixed design. The word for the size in the sentence (small, medium-sized, large) follows from ηG².

geometrische-verteilung.kurz: How many trials are needed until the first success if each trial succeeds independently with probability p? The geometric distribution gives the probability of each number of trials. On average it takes 1 / p trials.
geometrische-verteilung.beispiel: Rolling a die until the first six: the first six exactly on the third roll has probability (5/6)² · (1/6) = 0.116. On average it takes 6 rolls.
geometrische-verteilung.vorsicht: There are two conventions: trials up to and including the success (starting at 1), or failures before it (starting at 0). The formulas and the mean differ by 1.

geometrisches-mittel.kurz: What was the average growth factor? The geometric mean multiplies all n values and takes the n-th root of the product. It suits factors that multiply one after another.
geometrisches-mittel.beispiel: Sales: year 1 plus 10% (factor 1.10), year 2 plus 20% (1.20), year 3 minus 10% (0.90). Product 1.188, cube root 1.059: on average plus 5.9% per year.
geometrisches-mittel.vorsicht: The plain mean of the percentages (6.7%) would give 1.214 after three years instead of 1.188. All values must be greater than 0.

gepaarter-t-test.kurz: Has the same group changed between two measurements? The paired samples t test forms, for each person, the difference between the two values and tests whether their mean differs from 0. It is a one-sample t test on the differences.
gepaarter-t-test.beispiel: 6 people, before 70, 82, 65, 90, 76, 84, after 68, 79, 66, 85, 73, 80: mean difference 2.67, t = 3.16 with 5 degrees of freedom, p = 0.025.
gepaarter-t-test.vorsicht: Without a comparison group it shows only a change, not its cause. It needs pairs that truly belong together.

geplanter-kontrast.kurz: Which questions were fixed before the analysis? A planned comparison (a priori contrast) is set up from the research question before looking at the data. A few such comparisons are often regarded as acceptable without adjusting the level.
geplanter-kontrast.beispiel: Fixed in advance: new method against the average of two old methods. This is a comparison with one degree of freedom.
geplanter-kontrast.vorsicht: A comparison that arises only after looking at the data is not planned, even if it looks the same. Post hoc rules then apply.
geplanter-kontrast.statable: Under the result of the analysis of variance with three or more groups: “Planned comparisons”. Enter your own weights for each group or insert a template (Helmert, simple, repeated, deviation).

gerichtete-hypothese.kurz: Is the group larger, or just different? A directional hypothesis fixes the direction of the effect, for example μ₁ < μ₂. It is tested one-sided. The critical value moves closer to the centre.
gerichtete-hypothese.beispiel: Hypothesis: the new training shortens the time. With 38 degrees of freedom and α = 0.05, the one-sided cut-off is t > 1.686, the two-sided |t| > 2.024.
gerichtete-hypothese.vorsicht: The direction must be fixed before looking at the data. Choosing it afterwards effectively doubles α.

gesamtfehler.kurz: The sum of all sources of error in a survey, not just the sampling error: coverage, sampling, non-response, measurement and processing. It shows that a small sampling error alone does not make an accurate survey.
gesamtfehler.beispiel: A survey with 10 000 respondents has a very small sampling error. But if only 10 % of those invited were willing to take part, the bias can be far larger.
gesamtfehler.vorsicht: The sampling error can be calculated; the other sources of error usually cannot.

gesamtmittelwertzentrierung.kurz: The mean of all cases is subtracted from each value, not the mean of its own group. Zero then means "average over all". In multilevel models it mixes the difference within and between the groups.
gesamtmittelwertzentrierung.beispiel: Grand mean of study time 8 hours, a person has 12: the centred value is 4, whatever class they are in.
gesamtmittelwertzentrierung.vorsicht: The effect of a variable centred this way is a mixture of the effect within and between the groups. If both are needed separately, centre at the group mean.

geschachtelte-fall-kontroll.kurz: A case-control study within a known cohort. For each case, controls are drawn from those still free of the disease at that time. Costly measurements are then needed for only a few people.
geschachtelte-fall-kontroll.beispiel: A cohort has 10 000 stored blood samples and 200 cases. Two controls are drawn per case, so 600 samples are analysed.
geschachtelte-fall-kontroll.vorsicht: Controls must still be at risk at the time of the case.

geschaetzte-randmittel.kurz: What would the group means be under equal conditions? Estimated marginal means are group means computed from the model, for example for a fixed covariate value, usually its overall mean. This compares groups fairly.
geschaetzte-randmittel.beispiel: Pre-test means 50 and 52: raw post-test means 61.4 and 68.2, adjusted to the overall pre-test mean 51: 62.37 and 67.23.
geschaetzte-randmittel.vorsicht: The adjustment holds only if the model fits, in particular equal slopes in all groups. It does not replace random assignment.
geschaetzte-randmittel.statable: Two-way analysis of variance: for a factor with three or more levels the tables “Estimated marginal means” and “Pairwise comparisons of the marginal means” (Tukey, Bonferroni). Analysis of covariance: table “Adjusted means”.

geschichtete-stichprobe.kurz: How does one make sure every important subgroup appears? The population is divided into strata, and a random draw is made within each stratum. This often makes the sampling error smaller.
geschichtete-stichprobe.beispiel: 1000 learners, 600 primary and 400 secondary: at n = 100 proportional, 60 and 40 are drawn.
geschichtete-stichprobe.vorsicht: If strata are sampled at unequal rates, the analysis must use weights. Otherwise the overall values are biased.

geschlossenes-testverfahren.kurz: A multiple-testing procedure: a hypothesis is rejected if it and all hypotheses that contain it are each rejected at α. This keeps the familywise error rate at α. The Holm procedure is a special case.
geschlossenes-testverfahren.beispiel: Three groups are compared. A pairwise comparison is tested only if the overall test of all three groups was significant first.
geschlossenes-testverfahren.vorsicht: It is the basis of many procedures but laborious with many hypotheses. Simplified versions are therefore used.

gesetz-grosse-zahlen.kurz: The more independent repetitions, the closer the mean of the observations gets to the expected value. Likewise the relative frequency of an event approaches its probability.
gesetz-grosse-zahlen.beispiel: The mean of many die rolls comes arbitrarily close to 3.5 as the number of rolls grows.
gesetz-grosse-zahlen.vorsicht: It does not balance out streaks. After five heads, heads is not less likely on the sixth toss.

gestapeltes-balkendiagramm.kurz: A bar chart in which each bar is split into parts lying on top of each other. It shows total size and composition. If all bars are set to 100 %, it is called a percent stacked chart.
gestapeltes-balkendiagramm.beispiel: One bar per school type, split into answers “yes”, “partly” and “no”. With bars stacked to 100 %, the shares can be compared directly.
gestapeltes-balkendiagramm.vorsicht: Only the bottom part starts at 0 and compares well. The other parts float and are harder to read.

gestutzte-verteilung.kurz: A distribution in which values outside a range do not occur or are not observed. The rest is renormalised. Truncation differs from censoring in that the cut-off cases do not appear at all.
gestutzte-verteilung.beispiel: A standard normal distribution observed only for positive values has a mean of √(2/π) = 0.80 instead of 0.
gestutzte-verteilung.vorsicht: Anyone who sees only truncated data estimates mean and spread wrongly with the ordinary procedure.

getrimmtes-mittel.kurz: What does the mean look like without the extremes? The trimmed mean drops a fixed share from both ends of the sorted values (for example 10% each) and averages the rest. An extreme value then disturbs less.
getrimmtes-mittel.beispiel: Waiting times 3, 4, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9, 10, 40: dropping 10% on each side removes 3 and 40. The mean of 4, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9, 10 is 53 / 8 = 6.625. The untrimmed mean is 9.6.
getrimmtes-mittel.vorsicht: The trimmed share is a choice of the analyst. It should be fixed in advance and reported.
getrimmtes-mittel.statable: Under “Do groups differ?” and “Has something changed?”: the choice “Robust (trimmed means)”, trimming per side adjustable (default 20%). Statable drops whole values per side (as R mean with trim); the figure in the distribution card follows SPSS (5%, edge values in part).

gewichtete-kleinste-quadrate.kurz: A regression in which cases with greater precision count more. Weights proportional to 1/variance are usual. It is used with unequal error spread and with data of known precision.
gewichtete-kleinste-quadrate.beispiel: Two measurements have variances 4 and 16. The weighted mean of 10 and 14 with weights 1/4 and 1/16 is 10.8, closer to the more precise measurement.
gewichtete-kleinste-quadrate.vorsicht: Wrong weights improve nothing. With weights estimated from the data, the usual standard errors hold only approximately.

gewichtete-logrank.titel: Weighted log-rank tests (Gehan, Tarone-Ware, Peto-Peto, Fleming-Harrington)
gewichtete-logrank.kurz: Variants of the log-rank test that weight the time points differently. Gehan-Wilcoxon and Peto-Peto stress early differences; Fleming-Harrington can be tuned to early, middle or late differences. The ordinary log-rank test weights equally.
gewichtete-logrank.beispiel: The survival curves first move apart and then approach again. The Gehan-Wilcoxon test is more sensitive to this than the log-rank test.
gewichtete-logrank.vorsicht: The weighting has to be chosen in advance. A choice made after viewing the curves invalidates the test.

gewichtetes-kappa.kurz: A form of Cohen's kappa for ordered categories. Disagreements by one level count less than disagreements by several levels. The weights are linear or quadratic. With quadratic weights the measure resembles a correlation.
gewichtetes-kappa.beispiel: Two raters sort 70 cases into three ordered levels (rows: rater 1, columns: rater 2): 20, 5, 1 / 4, 15, 5 / 1, 4, 15. Unweighted kappa 0.57, linearly weighted 0.64, quadratically weighted 0.72.
gewichtetes-kappa.vorsicht: The choice of weights changes the result and has to be stated. For nominal categories unweighted kappa is right.

gewichtetes-mittel.kurz: What is the average when values count for different amounts? In a weighted mean each value is multiplied by its weight; the sum is divided by the sum of the weights.
gewichtetes-mittel.beispiel: Group A: 20 people, mean 5. Group B: 30 people, mean 8. Overall mean (20 · 5 + 30 · 8) / 50 = 6.8, not (5 + 8) / 2 = 6.5.
gewichtetes-mittel.vorsicht: The weights must fit the question (group size, share, importance). Different weights give a different result.

gewichtung.kurz: Cases count with different strength. A frequency weight says how often a row occurs. A survey weight adjusts a sample to the make-up of the population.
gewichtung.beispiel: A row with weight 12 stands for 12 identical people. A case with survey weight 2 stands for twice as many people of the population as a case with weight 1.
gewichtung.vorsicht: Treating a survey weight as a frequency weight gives wrong standard errors and p-values.

gini.kurz: How unequally is something distributed? The Gini coefficient sums up inequality, for example of income, in one number from 0 to 1. 0: everyone has the same. Near 1: one person has almost everything.
gini.beispiel: Five people with 10, 20, 30, 40 and 100 units (200 in total): Gini = 0.4.
gini.vorsicht: With few cases the value cannot reach 1 (at most (n - 1) / n, here 0.8). Different distributions can have the same Gini.

gini-simpson.kurz: The probability that two randomly drawn cases lie in different categories: 1 - Σ p². It is 0 with a single category and grows as the distribution gets more diverse.
gini-simpson.beispiel: Shares of 0.5, 0.3 and 0.2: 1 - 0.38 = 0.62. Two randomly drawn cases belong to different categories with a probability of 62 %.
gini-simpson.vorsicht: The index must not be confused with the Gini coefficient of the income distribution. The calculation is different.

glass-delta.kurz: How large is the difference, measured against the control group's spread? Glass's Δ divides the difference of means by the standard deviation of the control group alone. It makes sense when the treatment also changes the spread.
glass-delta.beispiel: Control mean 100, SD 10; treatment mean 108, SD 14: Δ = 8 / 10 = 0.8. Cohen's d with pooled SD would be 0.66 for equal group sizes.
glass-delta.vorsicht: Which group serves as control determines the value. This must be stated.

glaubwuerdigkeitsintervall.kurz: Between which values does the parameter lie, if model and prior hold? A 95% credible interval contains 95% of the posterior distribution. Under those assumptions the parameter lies inside it with 95% probability.
glaubwuerdigkeitsintervall.beispiel: Posterior Beta(15, 7): 95% of the distribution lies between 0.478 and 0.854 (2.5% cut off at each end).
glaubwuerdigkeitsintervall.vorsicht: A confidence interval is something different: it describes the hit rate of the procedure over repetitions, not the probability of the parameter. The credible interval, in turn, depends on the prior.
glaubwuerdigkeitsintervall.statable: In the learning lab, tab “Bayes with prior knowledge”: the 95% credible interval has equal tails (2.5% cut off each) and is hatched in the chart.

gleichverteilung.kurz: All values within a range are equally likely. The density is a flat line, the curve a rectangle. For continuous values only the length of the sub-range counts.
gleichverteilung.beispiel: Waiting time between 0 and 10 minutes, all equally possible: between 2 and 5 minutes has probability 3/10 = 0.3.
gleichverteilung.vorsicht: Computer random numbers are usually uniform between 0 and 1. p values are uniform only if the null hypothesis is true and the test fits.

gleitender-durchschnitt.kurz: What does the series look like without short-term noise? In a moving average, each value is replaced by the mean of itself and its neighbours. This smooths the series.
gleitender-durchschnitt.vorsicht: The wider the window, the smoother the curve, but the more peaks and turning points are lost. Values are missing at the ends.

gleitkomma.kurz: Computers store decimal numbers as floating-point numbers with limited precision. Some values such as 0.1 cannot be represented exactly. This produces tiny rounding errors that disturb comparisons for equality.
gleitkomma.beispiel: In many programs 0.1 + 0.2 is not exactly equal to 0.3. A test for equality reports “false”.
gleitkomma.vorsicht: Numbers should be tested for equality with a small tolerance. The display often shows rounded values while the calculation uses more digits.

glm.kurz: How can regression be carried over to outcomes that are not normally distributed, for example yes/no or counts? A GLM has three parts: a distribution for the outcome, a linear part made of predictors, and a link function between them.
glm.beispiel: Yes/no with a binomial distribution and logit is logistic regression. Counts with a Poisson distribution and log give Poisson regression.
glm.vorsicht: Not to be confused with the ‘general linear model’ (regression and analysis of variance with normal errors). Both are often abbreviated GLM.

glockenkurve.kurz: The curve of the normal distribution: it is symmetric, highest in the middle and falls off evenly on both sides. Its shape resembles a bell. The name is also used loosely for other bell-shaped distributions.
glockenkurve.beispiel: The heights of many adults form roughly a bell curve: most near the middle, few very short or very tall.
glockenkurve.vorsicht: Not every bell-shaped curve is a normal distribution, for example the t distribution and the logistic distribution. Bell shape alone does not prove normality.

goldfeld-quandt.kurz: A test for unequal spread of the errors. The data are ordered by a predictor, divided into two parts (with a gap in the middle), and the residual sums of squares are compared. The statistic is their ratio (F).
goldfeld-quandt.beispiel: 20 cases each in two parts, 2 coefficients, ratio of the sums of squares 3.0: F = 3.0 with 18 and 18 degrees of freedom, p = 0.012.
goldfeld-quandt.vorsicht: The test fits when spread grows with a predictor. With other forms of inequality it has little power.

goldstandard.kurz: What is a new test measured against? The gold standard is the best available method, whose result is taken as the truth. Sensitivity and specificity of a new test are computed against it.
goldstandard.beispiel: A new rapid test is compared with laboratory analysis as the reference in 200 people. The laboratory results are taken as true.
goldstandard.vorsicht: ‘Gold’ does not mean free of error. Errors in the reference method distort the sensitivity and specificity of the new test.

goodman-kruskal-tau.kurz: A directional association measure for two nominal characteristics: the share of errors in predicting Y that is avoided when X is known. Unlike Kendall's tau it is for nominal data and not symmetric.
goodman-kruskal-tau.beispiel: 80 cases: X = A has 30 with Y = 1 and 10 with Y = 2, X = B has 10 and 30. Without X, 40 errors are expected; with X only 30. τ = (40 - 30)/40 = 0.25.
goodman-kruskal-tau.vorsicht: There are two values, τ(Y|X) and τ(X|Y), that can differ. The name must not be confused with the rank tau.

gpower.kurz: A freely available program for power and sample size calculation for many tests (t tests, analysis of variance, correlation, regression, chi-square). It supports a priori, compromise, sensitivity and post hoc calculations.
gpower.beispiel: For a t test of two independent groups with d = 0.5, α = 0.05 and power 0.80, the program gives 64 people per group.
gpower.vorsicht: The results depend on the assumptions entered. The program does not check whether they fit.

grade.kurz: A system for judging the certainty of evidence for an outcome in four levels: high, moderate, low, very low. Randomised studies start high, observational studies low. Downgrading for risk of bias, inconsistency, indirectness, imprecision or publication bias.
grade.beispiel: Randomised studies with high risk of bias and a wide interval are downgraded from “high” to “low”.
grade.vorsicht: The rating is a reasoned judgement, not a calculation. It refers to an outcome, not to a study.

graded-response.kurz: A model of item response theory for ordered response options, such as Likert items. For each option it describes how likely that option or a higher one is chosen, depending on the trait.
graded-response.beispiel: For an item with five options there are four curves: the probability of at least option 2, at least 3, at least 4 and 5.
graded-response.vorsicht: The model assumes a clear order of the options. Items can differ in discrimination.

granger.kurz: A series X “causes” a series Y in the Granger sense if earlier values of X improve the prediction of Y beyond the earlier values of Y. This is a statement about prediction, not about cause.
granger.beispiel: Yesterday's weather improves the prediction of today's electricity use, even when yesterday's use is known. Weather Granger-causes use.
granger.vorsicht: The name is misleading: a common third cause can produce the same finding. The test depends on the number of lags.

grounded-theory.kurz: An approach in qualitative research in which a theory is built step by step from the data instead of testing hypotheses set beforehand. Data collection and analysis alternate until new data bring nothing new.
grounded-theory.beispiel: From interviews with nurses, categories arise through coding. Further interviews are conducted where the emerging theory still has gaps.
grounded-theory.vorsicht: The approach exists in several schools that differ in procedure. It is not a method for testing hypotheses statistically.

grubbs.kurz: A test of whether the largest or smallest value of an approximately normal sample is an outlier. The statistic is G = |value - mean|/s for the suspect value. It tests only one outlier at a time.
grubbs.beispiel: Values 10, 12, 11, 13, 12, 11, 25: mean 13.4, s = 5.19, G = (25 - 13.4)/5.19 = 2.23. The critical value for n = 7 and α = 0.05 (two-sided) is about 2.02. 25 counts as an outlier.
grubbs.vorsicht: Several outliers mask each other. An “outlier” in the test is not automatically an error and is not removed automatically.

gruppenmittelwertzentrierung.kurz: The mean of the group is subtracted from each value. The variable then measures only the difference within the group and separates it from the difference between groups. The group mean can additionally enter as a predictor.
gruppenmittelwertzentrierung.beispiel: Group mean of study time 10 hours, one person has 12: the centred value is 2.
gruppenmittelwertzentrierung.vorsicht: Centring changes the interpretation of the coefficients. Which centring fits depends on the question, not on the technique.

guetefunktion.kurz: The function giving, for every possible true value, the probability of rejecting the null hypothesis. At the null hypothesis it equals α, and it rises with growing distance.
guetefunktion.beispiel: Two-sided z test with H₀: μ = 100, σ = 10, n = 25, α = 0.05. At the true value 104 the power is 0.52, at the true value 100 exactly 0.05.
guetefunktion.vorsicht: At a fixed point, the value is the power. The whole curve shows how power depends on the true value.

guetekriterien.kurz: How good is a measurement? Quality criteria are standards for the quality of tests and measurements. The classical three are objectivity, reliability (dependability) and validity (soundness).
guetekriterien.beispiel: A scale: does it show the same number for the same weight (reliability), and is it the right weight (validity)?
guetekriterien.vorsicht: An unreliable measurement cannot be valid. A reliable one can still measure the wrong thing.

gueterkriterien-qualitativ.kurz: Standards by which qualitative studies are judged, as a counterpart to objectivity, reliability and validity. Usual are credibility, transferability, dependability (traceability of the procedure) and confirmability.
gueterkriterien-qualitativ.beispiel: Credibility is checked by asking participants back and by triangulation, traceability by an openly documented procedure.
gueterkriterien-qualitativ.vorsicht: There is no single list. Qualitative quality criteria are not the same as quantitative ones and should not be confused with numerical measures.

guttman-lambda.kurz: Reliability coefficients by Louis Guttman. Like Cronbach's alpha they estimate reliability from one testing, but assume less. Guttman's λ₂ is never smaller than alpha.
guttman-lambda.beispiel: Three items with intercorrelations of 0.6, 0.3 and 0.2 (variance 1 each) give alpha = 0.63 and λ₂ = 0.66. λ₂ is higher.
guttman-lambda.vorsicht: Both remain lower bounds of the true reliability if the errors do not correlate.

guttman-skala.kurz: A scale whose items have a fixed order of difficulty. Anyone who agrees with a harder item agrees with all easier ones. The number of agreements then shows which items were endorsed.
guttman-skala.beispiel: Three statements: “I walk 1 km”, “5 km”, “20 km”. Anyone who endorses 20 km also endorses the other two.
guttman-skala.vorsicht: Perfect Guttman scales are rare in real data. It is checked how closely the data approach the pattern.

gwet-ac1.kurz: A measure of agreement between two raters on categories. Like kappa it corrects for chance, but it assumes the chance agreement differently and stays more stable when categories are very unevenly distributed.
gwet-ac1.beispiel: Two raters agree in 90 of 100 cases, and the category “yes” is very common (95 %). Kappa is -0.05, AC1 is 0.89.
gwet-ac1.vorsicht: AC1 is not the same as kappa. Both values should be reported together with the percent agreement.

haeufigkeit.kurz: How often does a value occur? The frequency counts it. It is given either as an absolute number (a count) or as a relative number (the share of all cases).
haeufigkeit.beispiel: Of 25 people, 10 name the apple as their favourite fruit: frequency 10 (absolute) or 0.40 (relative).

haeufigkeitspolygon.kurz: A line through the midpoints of the bar tops of a histogram. It shows the shape of the distribution as a line and allows several distributions to be compared in one chart.
haeufigkeitspolygon.beispiel: The age distribution of two groups is drawn as two lines in one chart. A histogram would overlap itself.
haeufigkeitspolygon.vorsicht: The line usually starts and ends at a frequency of 0, beyond the outermost classes. The shape depends on the chosen classes.

haeufigkeitstabelle.kurz: How are the values distributed? A frequency table lists each value or class with its frequency, often with percent and cumulative percent as well.
haeufigkeitstabelle.beispiel: Favourite fruit of 25 people: apple 10 (40%), banana 8 (32%), pear 4 (16%), kiwi 3 (12%).
haeufigkeitstabelle.vorsicht: With many different values, such as exact body heights, the table becomes long and hard to read. Grouping into classes helps.

halo-effekt.kurz: One striking characteristic of a person or thing colours the judgement of other characteristics. Ratings of different characteristics are then more strongly related than the true relation.
halo-effekt.beispiel: An applicant comes across as likeable and is therefore also rated higher in expertise and reliability.
halo-effekt.vorsicht: Remedies are clear criteria per characteristic and rating the characteristics separately.

hanley-mcneil.kurz: A formula for the standard error of the area under the ROC curve (AUC) from the AUC and the group sizes. A confidence interval follows from it.
hanley-mcneil.beispiel: AUC = 0.80 with 50 ill and 50 healthy people: standard error 0.045, 95 % interval 0.71 to 0.89.
hanley-mcneil.vorsicht: It is an approximation. For dependent AUC values of the same group of persons the correlation of the curves is needed, that is a different method.

harking.kurz: HARKing stands for 'Hypothesizing After the Results are Known': a hypothesis is set up only after seeing the results and then presented as if it had been planned in advance.
harking.beispiel: An unexpected difference in women over 50 stands out. The report says this was suspected from the start.
harking.vorsicht: Reporting something found afterwards is fine if it is labelled as found afterwards.
sw: Hypothesizing After the Results are Known

harmonisches-mittel.kurz: What is the average for quantities such as speed? The harmonic mean is n divided by the sum of the reciprocals. It fits when the same distance or amount is covered at different speeds or prices.
harmonisches-mittel.beispiel: Outbound 60 km/h, return 40 km/h, same distance: 2 / (1/60 + 1/40) = 48 km/h, not 50.
harmonisches-mittel.vorsicht: If each speed is driven for the same time instead of the same distance, the arithmetic mean (50) is right.

harrells-c.kurz: A measure of how well a survival model predicts the order of events. Of all comparable pairs of persons, it is the share in which the person with the higher predicted risk has the event earlier. 0.5 is chance, 1 perfect prediction.
harrells-c.beispiel: Of 100 comparable pairs, 70 are ordered correctly and 30 incorrectly. C = 70/100 = 0.70.
harrells-c.vorsicht: The measure checks only the order, not whether the level of the predicted risks is right. With heavy censoring it depends on the censoring.

hartley-fmax.kurz: A test for equal variances in several groups of equal size. The test statistic is the largest variance divided by the smallest.
hartley-fmax.beispiel: Three groups have variances 16, 9 and 4. F-max = 16/4 = 4. This is compared with a tabulated value.
hartley-fmax.vorsicht: The test reacts strongly to departures from normality and needs groups of equal size. Today the Levene test is usually chosen.

hat-matrix.kurz: The matrix H = X(XᵀX)⁻¹Xᵀ that turns the observed values into the predicted ones: ŷ = Hy (“y hat”). Its diagonal elements are the leverage values. Its trace is the number of coefficients p.
hat-matrix.beispiel: With n = 50 and p = 3 the mean leverage is 3/50 = 0.06. A value above 2p/n = 0.12 is often seen as conspicuous.
hat-matrix.vorsicht: The limit 2p/n is a habit. Leverage shows only the position in the predictors, not the influence on the outcome.

hauptachsenanalyse.kurz: A method of factor analysis that explains only the shared variance of the items. The communalities are estimated iteratively until they no longer change. Unlike principal component analysis, the total variance is not considered.
hauptachsenanalyse.beispiel: Ten items are meant to reflect an underlying trait. Principal axis factoring separates the shared variance from item-specific noise.
hauptachsenanalyse.vorsicht: The results often differ only slightly from principal component analysis, especially with many items of high communality.

haupteffekt.kurz: Does a factor act on average across all levels of the other factors? A main effect is the difference between the levels of one factor after averaging over the levels of the other factors.
haupteffekt.beispiel: In the plant example, mean height is 11 cm under low light and 17 cm under high light, averaged over both fertiliser levels.
haupteffekt.vorsicht: With a clear interaction an average can mislead, because the effect is of different size at each level of the other factor.

hawthorne-effekt.kurz: Behaviour changes because people know they are being observed or studied, and not because of the intervention being tested.
hawthorne-effekt.beispiel: An office gets new chairs. Staff then work faster because they know their output is being counted, not because of the chairs.
hawthorne-effekt.vorsicht: Whether and how strongly the effect existed in the famous original study is disputed. It remains useful as a warning about the effects of being observed.

hazard.kurz: How large is the risk at this moment, given that the event has not occurred so far? The hazard is the instantaneous rate of the event among those not yet affected. It can change over time.
hazard.beispiel: On day 10, 50 people are still event-free and 2 experience it that day: 2 / 50 = 0.04 per day.
hazard.vorsicht: The hazard is not a probability but a rate per unit of time and can exceed 1. It differs from the share who experience the event overall.

healthy-worker.kurz: Employed people are on average healthier than the general population, because the severely ill do not work or leave work. Comparing workers with the population understates the hazards of an occupation.
healthy-worker.beispiel: A factory with pollutant exposure shows a lower death rate than the population, because only healthy people work there.
healthy-worker.vorsicht: A better comparison is with other workers without the exposure.

heatmap.kurz: A table or area in which cells are coloured according to their value. Patterns in many numbers show at a glance, for example in a correlation matrix.
heatmap.beispiel: A correlation matrix of 20 variables is coloured: dark for strong positive, light for weak. Blocks of related variables stand out.
heatmap.vorsicht: The colour scale has to be explained. People with colour-vision differences and screen reader users need the numbers as well.

heavy-tails.kurz: Extremely large or small values occur more often than the normal distribution would lead one to expect. The distribution is said to have heavy tails. Single extreme values can then dominate the mean and the spread.
heavy-tails.beispiel: A t distribution with 3 degrees of freedom lies more than 3 standard deviations from the mean in 1.4% of cases. For the normal distribution it is 0.27%, about a fifth of that.
heavy-tails.vorsicht: Heavy tails are not the same as skewness. A distribution can be symmetric and still have many extreme values.

heckman.kurz: A model for the case that the outcome is observed only for a non-randomly selected subgroup. In two steps, the selection equation and the outcome equation are estimated, with the selection entering as a correction term.
heckman.beispiel: Wages are known only for people in work. Who works is not random. The Heckman model allows for who enters employment.
heckman.vorsicht: It needs a variable that affects the selection but not the outcome. Without it the model is poorly identified.

hedges-g.kurz: How is Cohen's d made more accurate in small groups? Hedges' g is Cohen's d multiplied by a factor slightly below 1. The factor corrects for d slightly overestimating the true value in small samples. With large groups d and g are almost equal.
hedges-g.beispiel: d = 0.5 with 10 people per group: the factor is 0.958, so g = 0.48.
hedges-g.vorsicht: g is still an estimate. How much it can be trusted depends on sample size, so an interval for it matters.

helmert.kurz: A Helmert contrast compares the first level with the mean of all the others, then the second with the mean of those still to come, and so on. With equal group sizes the comparisons are independent.
helmert.beispiel: Means 5, 7, 9: A against the mean of B and C: 5 - 8 = -3 (t(9) = -6.0). B against C: 7 - 9 = -2 (t(9) = -3.46; p = 0.007).
helmert.vorsicht: The order of the levels determines the questions. A different order gives different comparisons.
helmert.statable: Under “Planned comparisons” insert the template “Helmert”: the weights then stand in the table and can be changed.

herfindahl.kurz: The sum of the squared shares of all categories. It measures how strongly a whole is concentrated in a few parts. With n equal shares it is 1/n, with a single part it is 1.
herfindahl.beispiel: Three firms have market shares of 50 %, 30 % and 20 %. The index is 0.5² + 0.3² + 0.2² = 0.38. With equal shares it would be 1/3.
herfindahl.vorsicht: The index is often multiplied by 10 000 (here 3800). Thresholds for “high concentration” are set by authorities.

hermeneutik.kurz: The theory of understanding and interpreting texts and actions. Meaning is worked out in the movement between the whole and its parts (hermeneutic circle). In social research it stands for methods based on understanding meaning.
hermeneutik.beispiel: An interview text is interpreted paragraph by paragraph, again and again related back to the overall understanding of the conversation.
hermeneutik.vorsicht: Interpretations can turn out differently. They are justified and checked in the group of researchers.

heterogen.kurz: From Greek heteros “other” and genos “kind”: of unlike kinds. Groups are heterogeneous if they differ strongly. In meta-analysis: effects differ by more than chance would lead one to expect.
heterogen.beispiel: The studies are heterogeneous: a training helped a lot in one, not at all in another.

heterogenitaet.kurz: Do the studies differ more than chance would lead one to expect? Heterogeneity means that the true effects are not the same in all studies. It is tested with Q; I² and τ² describe its size.
heterogenitaet.beispiel: Three studies (d = 0.30, 0.50, 0.10): Q = 2.69 with 2 degrees of freedom, p = 0.26, I² = 26%.
heterogenitaet.vorsicht: A non-significant Q does not prove equality, especially with few studies. High heterogeneity calls for a cautious reading of the overall effect.

heuristik.kurz: From Greek heuriskein: “to find”. A rule of thumb or approximate method that is often useful but guarantees no correctness.
heuristik.beispiel: The rule of flagging values beyond 1.5 times the IQR is a heuristic, not proof of an error.

heywood.kurz: An inadmissible solution of a factor analysis or structural equation model: a communality is larger than 1 or an error variance is negative. This is mathematically possible but nonsensical in content.
heywood.beispiel: The error variance of an item is estimated as -0.04, and its standardised loading is 1.02.
heywood.vorsicht: Common causes are too small samples, too many factors or too few items per factor. The solution is usually not simply forced into range; the model is re-examined.

hierarchische-daten.kurz: Do observations belong to groups, and do the groups belong to larger units? Then the data are hierarchical (nested). Observations from the same group tend to be more alike than observations from different groups.
hierarchische-daten.beispiel: 1,200 patients from 40 practices: patients of one practice share doctors, rooms and catchment area.
hierarchische-daten.vorsicht: If observations from the same group are treated as independent, standard errors are often too small. Significant results then become too easy to get.

hierarchische-regression.kurz: What does a predictor add beyond others? In hierarchical regression the predictors enter the model in blocks fixed in advance, and R² is compared after each block. The order is decided beforehand on substantive grounds.
hierarchische-regression.beispiel: Block 1: study hours (R² = 0.933). Block 2: plus practice tasks (R² = 0.958, ΔR² = 0.024).
hierarchische-regression.vorsicht: Not to be confused with stepwise regression, where the data decide the order. Nor with hierarchical data (multilevel models).

hierarchisches-bayes.kurz: A Bayesian model with several levels: the parameters of single groups come from a common distribution whose parameters are estimated in turn. Groups thus learn from each other.
hierarchisches-bayes.beispiel: Means of 20 schools are estimated jointly. Small schools are pulled more towards the overall mean, large ones less.
hierarchisches-bayes.vorsicht: Joint estimation has the price that single results look less extreme than their raw values. This is intended.

hierarchisches-clustern.kurz: A clustering method without a preset number of clusters. It starts with each case as its own group and, step by step, merges the two most similar groups until only one remains. The result is a dendrogram.
hierarchisches-clustern.beispiel: Ten cities are compared by climate. First the two most similar merge, in the end all form one group.
hierarchisches-clustern.vorsicht: How the distance between groups is measured (linkage: single, complete, average, Ward) changes the result clearly.

hierarchisches-testen.kurz: Several hypotheses are tested in a sequence fixed in advance, each at α. Testing stops at the first non-significant result. The familywise error rate stays at α without splitting α.
hierarchisches-testen.beispiel: The main outcome is tested first. Only if it is significant does the first secondary outcome follow, then the second.
hierarchisches-testen.vorsicht: The order must be fixed in advance. A later hypothesis is never tested if an earlier one fails, even if it would be strong.

hintertuerkriterium.kurz: A rule for causal diagrams: which variables to adjust for to estimate the influence of X on Y without bias? All “back doors” (paths from X to Y starting with an arrow into X) must be blocked, without conditioning on colliders or consequences of X.
hintertuerkriterium.beispiel: X is smoking, Y lung cancer. Age affects both; it is a back door. Adjusting for age blocks the path.
hintertuerkriterium.vorsicht: The rule holds only if the diagram is right. It handles only variables present in the diagram.

histogramm.kurz: How are metric values distributed? A histogram divides the values into adjoining classes and draws a bar over each. With classes of equal width, the height shows the frequency of the class.
histogramm.beispiel: 100 body heights in 5 cm classes: the class 165 to under 170 cm holds 22 people, so the bar is 22 high.
histogramm.vorsicht: The shape depends on class width and starting point: too wide blurs, too narrow gets jagged. A rule of thumb (Sturges: round up log₂(n) + 1, so 8 classes for n = 100) is only a start.

hodges-lehmann.kurz: By how much is one group typically higher, without outliers mattering much? The Hodges-Lehmann estimator is the median of all pairwise differences between the groups. It goes with the Mann-Whitney test and has the unit of the data.
hodges-lehmann.beispiel: Group A: 10, 11, 15, 17, 20, 21; group B: 14, 25, 27, 30, 31, 36, 38 minutes. Median of the 42 differences (B minus A) 14.5; difference between the medians 14.
hodges-lehmann.vorsicht: The estimator is usually not equal to the difference between the two medians.

holm.kurz: How can strict protection with many tests lose less power? In the Holm procedure the p values are sorted. The smallest is multiplied by m, the next by m - 1, and so on. It protects like Bonferroni but never rejects fewer.
holm.beispiel: p values 0.003, 0.012, 0.020, 0.300: Holm gives 0.012, 0.036, 0.040, 0.300, Bonferroni 0.012, 0.048, 0.080, 1. At α = 0.05, Holm rejects three, Bonferroni two.
holm.vorsicht: The number of tests must be fixed beforehand. Dropping tests afterwards makes the correction worthless.
holm.statable: Under the result of the analysis of variance at “Which groups differ?” choose the Holm procedure: difference, interval (as for Bonferroni) and adjusted p.

homogen.kurz: From Greek homos “same”: of like kind. A group is homogeneous if its members resemble each other. Homogeneity of variance means equal spread in the groups.
homogen.beispiel: If everyone in a group is between 20 and 22 years old, it is homogeneous in age.

homoskedastizitaet.kurz: Do the errors spread equally everywhere? Homoscedasticity means that the spread of the residuals in a regression is the same for all predicted values. The opposite is called heteroscedasticity.
homoskedastizitaet.beispiel: Spending by income: if the deviations spread much more at high income than at low income, there is heteroscedasticity.
homoskedastizitaet.vorsicht: It is seen in the residual plot. With a large sample a test alone flags even small differences.

horvitz-thompson.kurz: An estimator for a total from a sample with unequal selection probabilities: each value is divided by its probability of entering the sample and the results are added. It is unbiased.
horvitz-thompson.beispiel: Two units with values 10 and 30 and selection probabilities 0.1 and 0.2. Estimate of the total: 10/0.1 + 30/0.2 = 250.
horvitz-thompson.vorsicht: Very small selection probabilities produce very large weights and unstable estimates.

hosmer-lemeshow.kurz: Do the predicted probabilities match the actual proportions? The Hosmer-Lemeshow test sorts the cases by predicted probability into usually 10 groups and compares, in each, the expected with the observed number of cases (χ²).
hosmer-lemeshow.beispiel: 10 groups, statistic χ² = 9.8 with 8 degrees of freedom: p = 0.28.
hosmer-lemeshow.vorsicht: A p value above 0.05 does not prove a good fit; in small samples the test has little power. The result depends on the number of groups.

hot-deck.kurz: A method of replacing missing values: for a case with a missing value, the value of a similar case with an available value (donor) is taken over. Similar means agreeing in important characteristics.
hot-deck.beispiel: When the income of a 40-year-old woman with a university degree is missing, the value of another 40-year-old woman with a degree is inserted.
hot-deck.vorsicht: The value taken over is a real value, but the method does not show the uncertainty of the replacement if it is applied only once.

hotelling-lawley-roy.titel: Hotelling-Lawley trace and Roy's largest root
hotelling-lawley-roy.kurz: Two more test statistics of multivariate analysis of variance, besides Pillai's trace and Wilks' lambda. Both rest on the eigenvalues of the ratio of effect to error variance. Roy's root uses only the largest eigenvalue.
hotelling-lawley-roy.beispiel: A MANOVA with three outcomes gives four test statistics in the output. They usually lead to the same decision.
hotelling-lawley-roy.vorsicht: When the statistics differ slightly, Pillai's trace is often the most robust. Roy's root is most sensitive when assumptions are violated.

hotelling-t2.kurz: The test for comparing mean vectors: whether several means at once equal a target value or are equal between two groups. It is the multivariate counterpart of the t test. T² is converted into an F value.
hotelling-t2.beispiel: 25 people, 3 measures, T² = 15: F = (25 - 3)/(3 · 24) · 15 = 4.58 with 3 and 22 degrees of freedom, p = 0.012.
hotelling-t2.vorsicht: The test assumes approximately multivariate normality and equal covariance matrices. Separate tests are no substitute, because several t tests accumulate the error.

hurdle.kurz: A model for count data with very many zeros that has two parts: first it asks whether anything is counted at all (zero or above zero), then how much, among those above zero. Unlike the zero-inflated model, all zeros come from the first part.
hurdle.beispiel: For the number of doctor visits, one part decides whether someone goes at all, the other how often.
hurdle.vorsicht: The two parts can have different predictors. Interpretation needs both parts.

huynh-feldt.kurz: How can the degrees of freedom be corrected when sphericity is violated? The Huynh-Feldt correction multiplies the degrees of freedom by a factor epsilon (ε). It is less strict than the Greenhouse-Geisser correction.
huynh-feldt.beispiel: In the example (5 people, 3 time points) Greenhouse-Geisser ε = 0.941. The Huynh-Feldt formula would give 1.75 on paper. Because ε cannot exceed 1, ε = 1 applies, i.e. no correction.
huynh-feldt.vorsicht: A value of 1 means no correction is needed. The method can be somewhat too liberal, especially in small samples.
huynh-feldt.statable: Under the result of the repeated-measures analysis choose the correction “Huynh-Feldt”: degrees of freedom and p change at once. With two repeated-measures factors each effect has its own ε.

hypergeometrische-verteilung.kurz: How many successes occur when drawing from a small, limited set without replacement? Every draw changes the set, so the probability changes from draw to draw. The hypergeometric distribution gives the probability of every number of successes.
hypergeometrische-verteilung.beispiel: 20 tickets, 5 of them winners, 4 are drawn: exactly 1 winner has probability 0.470. With replacement it would be 0.422.
hypergeometrische-verteilung.vorsicht: If the set is very large compared with the draw, the result is hardly different from the binomial distribution.

hyperparameter.kurz: A setting of a learning method that is not estimated from the data but fixed in advance. It controls how the method works. It is usually chosen by cross-validation.
hyperparameter.beispiel: In the lasso, the strength of the penalty λ is a hyperparameter. In a random forest they are the number of trees and the depth.
hyperparameter.vorsicht: If the hyperparameter is chosen on the test data, the performance is too optimistic. It may be chosen only with training and validation data.

hyperprior.kurz: A prior for a parameter that itself describes a prior distribution. In hierarchical models it controls how similar the groups are.
hyperprior.beispiel: The spread between 20 schools gets a hyperprior, for example a half-normal distribution. It prevents the spread from being estimated as very large or exactly zero.
hyperprior.vorsicht: With few groups the hyperprior influences the result strongly. A sensitivity check is then needed.

hypothese.kurz: What is suspected? A hypothesis is an assumption that can be tested with data. It must be worded so that data are able to contradict it.
hypothese.beispiel: People who exercise in the evening for a week sleep longer on average than people who do not.
hypothese.vorsicht: Data do not 'prove' a hypothesis. They speak for or against it.

ibid.kurz: Abbreviation of “ibidem”, Latin for “in the same place”. It points to the same source as the reference just before. Used only in some citation styles; others repeat author and year.
ibid.beispiel: Two references in a row to the same book: the second reads “ibid., p. 14”.

icc-modelle.titel: ICC models (absolute agreement, consistency, single and average)
icc-modelle.kurz: The intraclass correlation exists in several forms. Single: how reliable is one single rating? Average: how reliable is the mean of all ratings? Absolute agreement: differences in the severity of the raters count. Consistency: they do not.
icc-modelle.beispiel: 10 cases, 3 raters, MS cases 20, MS raters 6, MS residual 2. Consistency single 0.75. Absolute single 0.71. Consistency average 0.90. Absolute average 0.88.
icc-modelle.vorsicht: The choice depends on the question and the design of the study, not on the result. It has to be stated, because values from different forms are not comparable.

ie-eg.kurz: “i.e.” stands for the Latin “id est”: “that is”, and introduces a rephrasing. “e.g.” stands for “exempli gratia”: “for example”, and introduces a selection of cases. The two are not interchangeable.
ie-eg.beispiel: Nominal variables (i.e., categories without an order) include eye colour (e.g., brown, blue).

ignorabilitaet.kurz: An assumption for causal estimates from observational data: after allowing for the measured characteristics, treatment is independent of the potential outcomes. The effect can then be obtained by comparing similar persons.
ignorabilitaet.beispiel: People who take tutoring differ in prior achievement. With the same prior achievement, age and school, the choice of tutoring is supposed not to depend on how success would turn out with and without tutoring.
ignorabilitaet.vorsicht: The assumption cannot be checked from the data. Unmeasured confounders violate it.

iid.kurz: Random variables that are independent of one another and all have the same distribution. Many procedures assume that the observations of a random sample are like this.
iid.beispiel: 10 rolls of the same fair die: each roll has the same distribution, and no roll depends on another.
iid.vorsicht: Repeated measurements on the same person are usually not independent.

immortal-time-bias.kurz: A period is credited to a group during which no event could occur, because assignment to the group happens only later. The group then looks too favourable.
immortal-time-bias.beispiel: Those who must survive until therapy starts have immortal time until then. Compared with the untreated, the therapy looks too good.
immortal-time-bias.vorsicht: Remedies are a time-dependent covariate or a landmark analysis.

implikation.kurz: From Latin implicare: “to enfold, to contain”. In logic: “if A then B”; A implies B. Conversely, B does not imply A. In a wider sense: a consequence.
implikation.beispiel: If event A is contained in event B, then P(A) ≤ P(B): A implies B.

impulsantwort.kurz: The reaction of a series in the following time steps to a one-off shock in one series or in a model. It shows how long and how strongly a change has an after-effect.
impulsantwort.beispiel: Suppose a one-off interest rate rise by one point leads to a fall in demand that is strongest after 4 quarters and has faded after 12 quarters. The numbers are invented and show only the shape.
impulsantwort.vorsicht: The response depends on assumptions, such as the order of the variables in the model. Uncertainty bands belong with it.

imputation.kurz: Missing values are replaced by estimated values. All cases then stay in the analysis. The filled-in value is an estimate, not an observation.
imputation.beispiel: If a body height is missing, it is estimated from the person's age and sex and filled in.
imputation.vorsicht: If every gap is filled with the same value (for example the mean), the spread looks too small and the standard error too low. The uncertainty of the estimate stays invisible.

in-sample-out-of-sample.kurz: Within the sample and outside the sample. In-sample: the model is judged on the same data it was fitted on; that looks too good. Out-of-sample: judged on new data, more informative.
in-sample-out-of-sample.beispiel: A model gets 90% right in-sample but only 70% out-of-sample: it is overfitted.

in-situ.kurz: Latin for “in place”. On the spot, in the natural setting, not brought into the lab. Measurements in situ are closer to everyday life but harder to control.
in-situ.beispiel: Noise level is measured in situ, at the workplace itself.

in-vivo-in-vitro.kurz: Latin for “in the living” and “in glass”. In vivo: in the living organism. In vitro: in the lab, for example on cells in a dish. Results from the lab do not transfer to the living organism without further checks.
in-vivo-in-vitro.beispiel: A substance acts on cells in vitro but not in vivo.

indexzahl.kurz: How has something changed compared with a starting point? An index number sets the value at a fixed point in time (base) to 100 and gives all other values relative to it.
indexzahl.beispiel: Price 80 in the base year, 92 today: index 92 / 80 · 100 = 115. The price is 15% above the base year.
indexzahl.vorsicht: Index values show change from the base, not the gap between two other years. For that, divide by the earlier index value rather than subtract.

indikationsverzerrung.kurz: Treated and untreated people differ in exactly the reason for the treatment, such as the severity of the illness. A treatment can then look harmful merely because it is given to sicker people.
indikationsverzerrung.beispiel: Those who get the drug are sicker. In observational data the treated have a higher death rate, although the drug helps.
indikationsverzerrung.vorsicht: This does not occur in randomised trials. In observational data, adjustment helps only for characteristics that were measured.

indikator.kurz: How can a construct be recognised? An indicator is an observable quantity that points to a construct that cannot be measured directly.
indikator.beispiel: Indicators of enjoyment of reading: number of books read voluntarily in a month, and agreement with the statement 'I enjoy reading'.
indikator.vorsicht: A single indicator usually covers only part of the construct. Several indicators give a fuller picture.

indirekter-effekt.kurz: Does A act on B through an intermediate quantity? The indirect effect is the effect of A on B through the intermediate quantity M (mediator). It is the product a · b of two coefficients: A on M, and M on B (A held constant).
indirekter-effekt.vorsicht: It has a causal meaning only if the assumptions about order and missing confounders hold. Otherwise it describes only a statistical path.

induktiv.kurz: From Latin inducere: “to lead into”. Reasoning from the particular to the general, for example from a sample to the population. Such conclusions are never certain; statistics states their uncertainty.
induktiv.beispiel: From 200 surveyed students, a conclusion is drawn about all students of the university.

inferenz.kurz: From Latin inferre: “to conclude”. The step from the sample to the population. Tests and intervals state how uncertain this step is.
inferenz.beispiel: From 40 measurements, a confidence interval is used to infer the mean of all possible measurements.

inferenzstatistik.kurz: What can be said beyond the data at hand? Inferential statistics draw conclusions from a sample about a population and state the uncertainty involved.
inferenzstatistik.beispiel: From 200 people surveyed to the share in the whole city, reported with a confidence interval.
inferenzstatistik.vorsicht: This requires that the sample was drawn suitably, for example at random. Otherwise the calculation does not carry over to the population.

inflation.kurz: The percentage change of a price index (usually of consumer prices) compared with an earlier point in time. It shows how much dearer a basket of goods has become.
inflation.beispiel: The price index rises from 100 to 103 within a year. The inflation rate is 103/100 - 1 = 3 %.
inflation.vorsicht: The rate applies to the basket, and single households differ from it. A falling inflation rate does not mean prices fall, only that they rise more slowly.

inhaltsanalyse.kurz: A method of analysing texts or other content systematically with a category system. Qualitative content analysis assigns text passages to categories and describes them. The quantitative kind counts how often categories occur.
inhaltsanalyse.beispiel: From 40 interviews, statements on “strain” are sorted into categories such as “time”, “money” and “health”. Then they are counted or described.
inhaltsanalyse.vorsicht: Quality depends on the category system and on agreement between coders. It is checked with measures such as Cohen's kappa.

inhaltsvaliditaet.kurz: Does the test cover the content it is about? Content validity means: the items represent the domain to be measured completely and appropriately.
inhaltsvaliditaet.beispiel: A fractions test contains only addition tasks and no division. Part of the content is missing.
inhaltsvaliditaet.vorsicht: It is mostly judged by expert judgement and comparison with a content plan, not by a single number.

inklusive-exklusive.kurz: From Latin includere “to shut in” and excludere “to shut out”. Inclusive: the limit value belongs to the range (≤, ≥). Exclusive: it does not (<, >). For classes and limits this must be clear.
inklusive-exklusive.beispiel: “Age 18 to 65 inclusive” includes 18 and 65. In “10 to under 20”, 20 is not included.

instrumentalvariable.kurz: How can an effect be estimated when not all confounders are measured? An instrumental variable influences the exposure but has no other path to the outcome and shares no causes with it. The effect is estimated for the part of the exposure it moves.
instrumentalvariable.beispiel: A random invitation to a course as an instrument for taking part: the invitation is random and acts on the grade only through participation.
instrumentalvariable.vorsicht: Whether it really moves the exposure can be checked; that there is no other path and no common cause cannot. A weak instrument makes the result very uncertain and prone to bias.

integral.kurz: The area under a curve between two limits. In probability, the probability that a continuous random variable lies between a and b is the integral of its density from a to b. The total area under a density is 1.
integral.beispiel: Uniform distribution on the range from 0 to 10: the density is 0.1 everywhere. P(2 ≤ X ≤ 5) is the area 3 · 0.1 = 0.3.
integral.vorsicht: With a continuous distribution a single point has probability zero. Only ranges have a probability.

integration-ordnung.kurz: A series is called integrated of order d, I(d), if it becomes stationary after differencing d times. A random walk is I(1): its changes from step to step are stationary, it itself is not.
integration-ordnung.beispiel: The price series grows irregularly and does not return to the mean. The difference from the previous day fluctuates around 0. The series is I(1).
integration-ordnung.vorsicht: Over-differenced material loses information and produces autocorrelation. The order is determined by tests and charts.

intention-to-treat.kurz: Analysis according to the planned assignment, also for people who stopped the treatment or did not adhere to it. This preserves the benefit of randomisation.
intention-to-treat.beispiel: Of 100 people in the treatment group, 20 do not take the tablets. All 100 are analysed in the treatment group.
intention-to-treat.vorsicht: With non-adherence, this approach estimates the effect of assignment, not that of the treatment taken in full.

inter-alia.kurz: Latin for “among other things”. Names one item out of several. The German abbreviation is “u. a.”.
inter-alia.beispiel: Recorded were, inter alia, age, gender and level of education.

interaktion.kurz: Does the effect of one factor depend on the level of another? An interaction exists when the effect of a factor is not the same everywhere but differs depending on the level of the other factor.
interaktion.beispiel: Fertiliser raises plants by 2 cm under low light (10 to 12) and by 6 cm under high light (14 to 20). The difference of 4 cm gives F(1, 8) = 12.
interaktion.vorsicht: An interaction is not the same as a relationship between the two factors. It only describes that the effects cannot simply be added up.

interaktionsterm.kurz: Does the effect of one predictor depend on the value of another? An interaction term is the product of two predictors (x₁ · x₂) used as an additional predictor. Its coefficient shows how the slope of one changes with the other.
interaktionsterm.beispiel: Score = … + 2.0 · hours + 0.5 · hours · prior knowledge: at prior knowledge 4 the slope of hours is 2.0 + 0.5 · 4 = 4.0.
interaktionsterm.vorsicht: With an interaction term, a predictor's coefficient holds only where the other is 0. Centering makes it readable.

intercoder.kurz: How well do two or more people agree when they sort the same material, for example interview texts, into categories by the same rules? Simple agreement counts only the hits. Kappa and Krippendorff's alpha remove chance agreement.
intercoder.beispiel: Two people sort 20 statements and agree on 17. Simple agreement is 17 / 20 = 0.85. Chance is not yet removed from this figure.
intercoder.vorsicht: High agreement shows that the rules are applied consistently. It does not show whether the categories are right in content.

interdependenz.kurz: From Latin inter “between” and dependere “to hang from”: mutual dependence. Two quantities influence each other, with no fixed direction. Methods without a dependent variable, such as factor or cluster analysis, are called interdependence methods.
interdependenz.beispiel: Price and sales influence each other: there is interdependence.

interimsanalyse.kurz: A planned analysis before the study is fully finished. It can stop the study early, for example for clear benefit, for harm, or for futility. To keep the overall α unchanged, it is spread over the time points.
interimsanalyse.beispiel: Two interim analyses are planned after one third and two thirds of the participants, plus a final analysis. Each is tested against a stricter limit than 0.05.
interimsanalyse.vorsicht: Unplanned peeking with α = 0.05 each time raises the type I error.

interne-konsistenz.kurz: Are the items of a scale related to each other? Internal consistency describes how uniformly the items measure the same thing. Cronbach's alpha is the usual measure.
interne-konsistenz.beispiel: All 10 items of a satisfaction scale correlate positively with each other.
interne-konsistenz.vorsicht: Items being related does not mean they measure one single construct.

interne-validitaet.kurz: Can the difference really be traced back to the condition under study? Internal validity is high when other explanations are ruled out.
interne-validitaet.beispiel: Randomly assigned, same rooms, assessors blinded: a difference in the test is more likely due to the learning method.
interne-validitaet.vorsicht: High internal validity does not mean the result holds outside the study. That is external validity.

interpolation.kurz: From Latin interpolare: “to insert”. Estimating a value between known values. Counterpart: extrapolation, outside the known values; it is less certain. Quantiles at in-between positions are often interpolated.
interpolation.beispiel: Between measurements at 10 and 20 degrees, the value for 15 degrees is estimated: interpolation.

intervallbreite.kurz: How precise is the estimate? Interval width is the upper limit minus the lower limit of an interval. It shrinks with more cases, less spread and a lower confidence level.
intervallbreite.beispiel: Share 0.5, 95%: at n = 100 the width is 0.196, at n = 400 only 0.098. Four times the sample size halves the width.
intervallbreite.vorsicht: A narrow width shows precision of the estimate, not correctness. It can be narrow even with biased data.

intervallschaetzung.kurz: Which range is plausible given the data? An interval estimate gives a range instead of a single number, calculated from the sample. Its width shows how uncertain the estimate is.
intervallschaetzung.beispiel: Five resting pulses 62, 70, 66, 74, 68: the 95% interval for the mean runs from 62.4 to 73.6.
intervallschaetzung.vorsicht: The interval does not say how probable it is that the true value lies inside. The level belongs to the procedure, not to this one interval.

intervallskala.kurz: Equal steps, but no true zero. On an interval scale equal differences mean equal differences in the trait. The zero point is a convention and does not mean “nothing”. Ratios (“twice as much”) are therefore not meaningful.
intervallskala.beispiel: Temperature in °C: going from 10 to 20 °C is the same rise as going from 20 to 30 °C. But 20 °C is not “twice as warm” as 10 °C.

intervallzensierung.kurz: The event is known only to have occurred between two examinations, not at what exact time. The time lies in an interval.
intervallzensierung.beispiel: With check-ups every 6 months, a disease is found at the check at 12 months but was absent at the 6-month check. It occurred between months 6 and 12.
intervallzensierung.vorsicht: Taking the end of the interval as the event time biases the result. Special methods exist for this.

intervention.kurz: From Latin intervenire: “to step in between”. A deliberate action whose effect is tested, such as a training or a drug. A group without the action serves as comparison.
intervention.beispiel: The intervention was an eight-week reading training; it was compared with a group without training.

interviewereffekt.kurz: Answers change because of the person conducting the interview, through their manner, their characteristics or their way of asking. This is a source of measurement error.
interviewereffekt.beispiel: When asked about prejudice, respondents answer more reservedly to an interviewer of a different background.
interviewereffekt.vorsicht: The effect can be reduced by training, standardisation and online interviewing. It is often described through the intraclass correlation per interviewer.

intraklassenkorrelation.kurz: How much of the total spread lies between groups? The intraclass correlation is the share of the between-group variance in the total variance. It also shows how similar observations from the same group are.
intraklassenkorrelation.beispiel: Variance between classes 16, within classes 48: ICC = 16 / (16 + 48) = 0.25. A quarter of the spread lies between classes.
intraklassenkorrelation.vorsicht: The abbreviation ICC is also used for agreement measures between raters. Here it concerns groups in multilevel data.

invariant.kurz: From Latin in “not” and variare “to change”: unchanged under a given change. A correlation is invariant to converting the unit, for example from metres to centimetres. In measurement invariance: the same measurement model in all groups.
invariant.beispiel: If body height is converted from metres to centimetres, its correlation with weight stays the same.

inverse-varianz-gewichtung.kurz: Which study counts for how much? Each study gets the reciprocal of its variance as weight, that is, 1 / standard error². More precise studies with a small standard error count more.
inverse-varianz-gewichtung.beispiel: Study A (SE 0.10) has weight 100, study B (SE 0.20) has weight 25. A counts four times as much as B.
inverse-varianz-gewichtung.vorsicht: The weight depends on the standard error, not on the quality of the study. A large but biased study still gets a lot of weight.

inzidenz.kurz: How many new cases arise in a period? They are counted against the number of people not yet affected at the start. A figure per unit of time is usual.
inzidenz.beispiel: 30 new cases in one year among 10000 people healthy at the start: 30/10000 = 0.003, that is 3 per 1000 per year.
inzidenz.vorsicht: Incidence counts only new cases, prevalence all existing ones.

inzidenzdichte.kurz: The number of new cases relative to the total observed person-time, such as person-years. Each person contributes only the time at which they are at risk. It is the right quantity when people are observed for different lengths of time.
inzidenzdichte.beispiel: 12 new cases in 800 person-years: 12/800 = 0.015 per person-year, which is 15 per 1000 person-years.
inzidenzdichte.vorsicht: The incidence density is a rate with the unit 1/time. It is not a proportion and not a probability.

ipw.kurz: A method for making groups comparable: each case is weighted by the reciprocal of the probability of receiving the treatment it actually received. The weighted groups then resemble each other in the measured characteristics.
ipw.beispiel: A person has a probability of 0.25 of being treated and is treated. Their weight is 1/0.25 = 4. A case with probability 0.8 has weight 1.25.
ipw.vorsicht: It helps only for measured characteristics. Very small probabilities produce very large weights, which are then truncated.

iq-skala.kurz: A norm score scale for intelligence tests, usually with a mean of 100 and a standard deviation of 15. Some tests use a different standard deviation. IQ = 100 + 15 x z.
iq-skala.beispiel: IQ 130: z = (130 - 100) / 15 = 2. Under a normal distribution, about 97.7% of the reference group lie below.
iq-skala.vorsicht: An IQ score has meaning only relative to a specific test and its norm sample.

iqr.kurz: How wide is the middle half of the values? The interquartile range is Q3 minus Q1. The middle 50% of the values lie in this range. Extreme values barely influence it.
iqr.vorsicht: Depending on the rule for quartiles, the IQR changes in small samples (here 5.25 instead of 4.5).

iqv.kurz: A measure of spread for nominal characteristics between 0 and 1. It is the Gini-Simpson index divided by its maximum 1 - 1/k for k categories. 0 means no spread, 1 equal frequency in all categories.
iqv.vorsicht: The index shows diversity, not the shape of the distribution. Two very different distributions can have the same value.
