satorra-bentler.kurz: An adjustment of the chi-square value and the standard errors in structural equation models when the data are not normally distributed. It reduces the error arising from departures from normality.
satorra-bentler.beispiel: The chi-square value of a model is 85.0. The correction factor is 1.25. The scaled chi-square is 85.0/1.25 = 68.0.
satorra-bentler.vorsicht: The correction applies to continuous but non-normal data. For ordinal items, other estimators are preferable.

saturiertes-modell.kurz: A model with as many parameters as observations (or distinct covariate patterns) that fits the data perfectly. It serves as a benchmark: the deviance of a model measures how far it is from the saturated model.
saturiertes-modell.beispiel: With 5 groups, the saturated model has 5 means, one per group. It fits all group means exactly.
saturiertes-modell.vorsicht: It explains the data completely, but nothing beyond. As a model for prediction it is useless.

satz-von-bayes.kurz: It reverses a conditional probability: from P(B | A) and the starting probabilities, P(A | B) follows. This updates an assessment with new information.
satz-von-bayes.beispiel: Condition 1 %, test detects 90 % of the ill, 5 % of the healthy falsely positive: P(ill | positive) = 0.009 / 0.0585 = 0.154.
satz-von-bayes.vorsicht: For rare events, even positive results of a good test are often false alarms.

sav.kurz: The data format of SPSS and PSPP. Besides the values it stores variable names, labels, value labels, level of measurement and missing-value codes. The information about the variables is therefore kept.
sav.beispiel: The file survey.sav contains the values and the labels of all questions.
sav.vorsicht: It is not a text file and cannot be read in a text editor. Saving as CSV loses the labels.

schaetzer.kurz: How does one get from a sample to a value for the whole group? An estimator is a rule that turns the data into an approximate value for an unknown quantity (parameter). The number it produces is called the estimate.
schaetzer.beispiel: Five resting pulses 62, 70, 66, 74, 68: the mean 68 is the estimate of the mean of all persons.
schaetzer.vorsicht: The estimator is the rule, the estimate is the number. Another sample gives another estimate.

schaetzfehler.kurz: How far off is the estimate? The estimation error is the estimate minus the true value. It has a sign and is usually unknown, because the true value is missing.
schaetzfehler.beispiel: True share in the group 0.40, in the sample 0.45: the estimation error of this sample is 0.45 - 0.40 = 0.05.
schaetzfehler.vorsicht: In practice the true value is unknown. Only the typical size of the error can be estimated (standard error), not the error itself.

scheffe.kurz: How cautiously can arbitrary comparisons of groups be tested? The Scheffé test keeps the error rate for all possible comparisons, including those chosen only after looking at the data. It is therefore more cautious than other procedures.
scheffe.beispiel: Same data as for the Tukey test: for pairs a difference of 1.68 or more counts as important, for Tukey 1.61.
scheffe.vorsicht: Being cautious, the test is more likely to miss real differences. For plain pairwise comparisons Tukey is usually the sharper choice.
scheffe.statable: Under the result of the analysis of variance at “Which groups differ?” choose the Scheffé test: difference, interval and p for all pairs.

scheinkorrelation.kurz: Do two quantities go together although neither affects the other? A spurious correlation arises when a third quantity influences both, or when chance produces it. If it goes back to a third quantity, it disappears once that quantity is taken into account.
scheinkorrelation.beispiel: In summer, ice cream sales and the number of sunburns rise together. Both follow the hours of sunshine.
scheinkorrelation.vorsicht: Whether a relationship is spurious only shows once the third quantity is measured and taken into account.

schichtung.kurz: How does one divide beforehand into groups that are similar within? In stratification, the population is divided into strata by a known characteristic. The characteristic is similar within and different between strata. It serves in drawing, assigning and analysing.
schichtung.beispiel: Employees by site: each site is a stratum, and a draw is made from each. With clusters, only some sites would be drawn.
schichtung.vorsicht: All strata are represented, clusters only the selected ones. Strata should be uniform within, clusters varied within.

schiefe.kurz: Is the distribution stretched out further on one side? Skewness measures how lopsided it is. Positive: long tail to the right (right-skewed). Negative: to the left (left-skewed). Near 0: roughly symmetric.
schiefe.beispiel: Values 1, 2, 2, 3, 3, 3, 4, 4, 10: mean 3.56 above the median 3, skewness (g₁) about 1.83, so right-skewed.
schiefe.vorsicht: Programs use differently corrected formulas (g₁ or G₁), and with few cases skewness fluctuates strongly. Limits such as ±1 are often quoted but are a habit.

schneeball.kurz: How does one find persons who are hard to reach? In snowball sampling, the first participants name further persons, who name more in turn. The group grows like a snowball.
schneeball.beispiel: For a rare condition, 5 persons come forward, each names up to 3 more. After this first round of nominations up to 20 persons are reached (5 + 15).
schneeball.vorsicht: Well-connected people are named more easily. The sample does not reliably reflect the whole group.

schwach-informativer-prior.kurz: A prior that expresses rough knowledge about the order of magnitude but is wide enough not to stand in the way of the data. It rules out absurd values and stabilises the estimate.
schwach-informativer-prior.beispiel: For a coefficient in logistic regression, a normal distribution with mean 0 and standard deviation 2.5 is often named. Extremely large values are then implausible.
schwach-informativer-prior.vorsicht: A default choice does not replace checking. A sensitivity analysis shows how much the prior matters.

scoping-review.kurz: A review that surveys a topic area broadly instead of answering a narrow question: which studies exist, which terms, which gaps? The quality of studies is usually not assessed, and no effects are pooled.
scoping-review.beispiel: A scoping review on “digital aids for learning” sorts the studies by methods, age groups and results and shows gaps.
scoping-review.vorsicht: A scoping review does not answer which measure works. That needs a systematic review with meta-analysis.

score-test.kurz: A test that checks the slope of the log-likelihood at the value the null hypothesis claims. It needs only the model under H₀, not the full estimate. Alongside the Wald test and the likelihood ratio test it is one of the three classical likelihood tests.
score-test.vorsicht: The three tests agree in large samples; in small ones they can differ. The score test is often more reliable than the Wald test.

scree-plot.kurz: A line chart of the eigenvalues, from largest to smallest. The point to look for is the bend after which the line flattens. Factors before the bend count as important. The name comes from the loose rubble at the foot of a slope.
scree-plot.beispiel: Eigenvalues 3.1, 1.4, 0.5, 0.4, 0.3, 0.3: after the second value the line hardly drops. That points to two factors.
scree-plot.vorsicht: Where the bend lies is a matter of judgement. With a gentle slope, two people often decide differently.

screening.kurz: How does one look for a disease in a group without complaints? In screening, a test is applied to many people to find those affected early. How useful a positive result is depends strongly on the prevalence.
screening.beispiel: 10,000 people, prevalence 1%, sensitivity 90%, specificity 95%: 90 true positives, 495 false positives. Only 15% of positive results are real cases.
screening.vorsicht: For rare diseases, many positive results are false even with a good test. A positive result is a reason for follow-up, not yet a diagnosis.

selbstselektion.kurz: Participants decide for themselves whether to take part. Those who take part often differ from those who do not, for example by stronger interest or opinion. The sample is then biased.
selbstselektion.beispiel: An online survey on a topic is answered mainly by people who are interested in it or annoyed by it.
selbstselektion.vorsicht: More participants do not remove the bias. A large self-selected sample can be worse than a small random sample.

sem.kurz: A method that tests a measurement model and a structural model in one step. It shows how latent variables arise from items and how they relate to each other. Whether the model fits the data is told by fit indices.
sem.beispiel: Three items form “enjoyment of learning”, three form “achievement”. The model estimates the loadings and the path from enjoyment to achievement at the same time.
sem.vorsicht: An arrow in the model is an assumption by the researchers. A fitting model does not prove a cause, and other models can fit equally well.

semantisches-differential.kurz: A method in which an object is rated on several pairs of opposite adjectives, usually on seven points. The pairs lie at the ends of the scale, such as “warm - cold”.
semantisches-differential.beispiel: A product is rated on seven points between “cheap - expensive”, “modern - old-fashioned” and “reliable - unreliable”.
semantisches-differential.vorsicht: The meaning of the poles depends on language and culture. Opposite pairs cannot be translated freely.

semipartialkorrelation.kurz: How much does a predictor add on its own once the other predictors are removed from it? The semipartial correlation adjusts only the predictor, not the outcome. Its square is the increase in R² that this predictor brings.
semipartialkorrelation.beispiel: Practice tasks are added to study hours: semipartial correlation 0.155, square 0.024. R² rises from 0.933 to 0.958.
semipartialkorrelation.vorsicht: Not to be confused with the partial correlation, which adjusts both variables. In the example it is 0.602.

sensitivitaets-power.kurz: Instead of calculating the sample size, the question is asked with a given sample size, α and power: which smallest effect could be detected? It is useful when the sample size is given.
sensitivitaets-power.beispiel: Two groups of 30 people each, α = 0.05 two-sided, power 0.80: differences from d = 0.74 can be detected.
sensitivitaets-power.vorsicht: Smaller effects stay undetected with this power. A non-significant result must not be read as proof of “no effect”.

sensitivitaetsanalyse.kurz: The analysis is repeated with other, equally defensible assumptions to see whether the result stays stable. What is varied includes the handling of missing values, the prior, outliers or the model form.
sensitivitaetsanalyse.beispiel: An effect is calculated once with all cases and once without the three most conspicuous. If it stays similar in both, it is stable against this decision.
sensitivitaetsanalyse.vorsicht: The word does not mean the sensitivity of a test. A sensitivity analysis removes no bias; it only shows how strongly the result depends on the assumptions.

sequenziell.kurz: From Latin sequi: “to follow”. One after the other, in steps. In statistics: sequential testing (checking repeatedly, by rules set in advance), stepwise regression, type I sums of squares. Without suitable rules, the type I error rises.
sequenziell.beispiel: In a sequential study, a check is made after each block whether enough evidence has accumulated.

serielle-mediation.kurz: A mediation through several mediators in sequence: X acts on M1, M1 on M2, M2 on Y. Each route has a specific indirect effect, the product of its paths. The sum of all routes is the total indirect effect.
serielle-mediation.beispiel: Paths X→M1 = 0.4, M1→M2 = 0.5, M2→Y = 0.3: the specific indirect effect through both mediators is 0.4 · 0.5 · 0.3 = 0.06.
serielle-mediation.vorsicht: The order of the mediators is an assumption that cannot be tested from the data alone. Contrasts between specific effects are hard to interpret.

sesoi.kurz: The smallest effect size that still matters in content. It is fixed before the study and serves as a yardstick for sample size planning, equivalence tests and the question of whether an effect counts in practice.
sesoi.beispiel: A course should improve the test score by at least 3 points, otherwise the effort is not worthwhile. 3 points are the SESOI.
sesoi.vorsicht: The choice must be justified, for example by costs, benefit or experience. Cohen's benchmarks do not replace it.

shannon-index.kurz: A measure of diversity across categories: H = -Σ p · ln(p). It is 0 when everything is in one category and largest when all categories are equally frequent. It takes number and evenness into account together.
shannon-index.beispiel: Shares of 0.5, 0.3 and 0.2 give H = 1.03. With three equally frequent categories, H would be ln 3 = 1.10.
shannon-index.vorsicht: The value depends on the base of the logarithm. With the base-2 logarithm the same example gives 1.49 bits.

sic.kurz: Latin for “thus”. In square brackets [sic] after a passage in a quotation: it stands so in the original, even if it is an error or unusual.
sic.beispiel: The author wrote “standart deviation [sic]”; the error in the original is marked this way.

sidak.kurz: An adjustment of the significance level for m tests: α' = 1 - (1 - α)^(1/m). It keeps the probability of at least one false alarm at α if the tests are independent. It is slightly less strict than Bonferroni.
sidak.beispiel: Five tests with α = 0.05: Šidák 1 - 0.95^(1/5) = 0.0102, Bonferroni 0.05/5 = 0.01.
sidak.vorsicht: The difference from Bonferroni is small. With dependent tests the correction is not always exact.

signifikant.kurz: From Latin significare: “to indicate”. Statistically significant means: the p value lies below the level chosen in advance, usually 0.05. It does not mean “important” and not “large”.
signifikant.beispiel: With a very large sample, a tiny difference can be significant without mattering in practice.

signifikante-stellen.kurz: The digits of a number that carry precision: from the first non-zero digit on. Stating three significant figures rounds accordingly. Leading zeros do not count.
signifikante-stellen.beispiel: 3.14159 to three significant figures is 3.14. 0.004560 to three significant figures is 0.00456.
signifikante-stellen.vorsicht: The word “significant” has nothing to do with statistical significance here. Intermediate calculations should not be rounded.

signifikanzniveau.kurz: At which p value is a result considered incompatible with the null hypothesis? The significance level α is set before the analysis. If p is below α, H₀ is rejected. α is the rate at which a true H₀ is wrongly rejected.
signifikanzniveau.beispiel: With α = 0.05, p = 0.042 leads to rejection, p = 0.08 does not.
signifikanzniveau.vorsicht: The value 0.05 is a habit, not a law of nature. α is not the probability that H₀ is true.

signifikanztest.kurz: Do the data fit the null hypothesis? A significance test computes a test statistic from the data and from it the p value. If p is below the chosen significance level, H₀ is rejected. The result is then called statistically significant.
signifikanztest.beispiel: Two groups of 20 people: t = 2.1 with 38 degrees of freedom, p = 0.042. At α = 0.05, H₀ is rejected.
signifikanztest.vorsicht: Statistically significant does not mean large or important. It says nothing about the size of the effect.

silhouette.kurz: A measure of how well a case fits its cluster. It compares the mean distance a within its own cluster with the mean distance b to the nearest other cluster. s = (b - a) / max(a, b). It lies between -1 and 1.
silhouette.beispiel: a = 2 and b = 5 give s = 3 / 5 = 0.6. The case is clearly closer to its own cluster.
silhouette.vorsicht: The mean over all cases is often used to choose the number of clusters. It is an aid, not proof of the right number.

simulation.kurz: The computer generates random data by set rules and repeats this many times. This shows what typically comes out. It helps where a formula is missing or too hard.
simulation.beispiel: 10 coin tosses, repeated 10,000 times: about 5.5% of the runs have 8 or more heads. The exact calculation gives 5.47%.
simulation.vorsicht: The result varies from run to run, and more repetitions make it more precise. A simulation shows what happens under the assumptions set and proves nothing beyond them.

simultan.kurz: From Latin simul: “at the same time”. At once. Simultaneous confidence intervals or tests hold for several comparisons together. The counterpart is sequential.
simultan.beispiel: The Tukey method gives simultaneous intervals for all pairwise comparisons with a joint confidence of 95%.

sine-qua-non.kurz: Latin for “a condition without which not”. A necessary condition. It is not sufficient on its own.
sine-qua-non.beispiel: That the cause comes before the effect is necessary for causality, but not sufficient.

skala.kurz: The word has two meanings. First, the measurement scale: the rule by which numbers are assigned to properties (see level of measurement). Second, a scale made of several items whose answers are combined into one total.
skala.beispiel: The scale 'enjoyment of learning' made of 6 items with 1 to 5 points each gives sum scores from 6 to 30.
skala.vorsicht: Whether answer steps may be treated as equally spaced is an assumption.

skalenniveau.kurz: What do the numbers of a variable tell? The level of measurement decides which calculations make sense. There are four levels, from little to much information: nominal, ordinal, interval and ratio.
skalenniveau.beispiel: Blood type is nominal, a school grade is ordinal, temperature in °C is interval, body weight in kg is ratio.
skalenniveau.vorsicht: The level is not visible in the number itself. A 1 can be a code for a category or a real quantity.

skalenwert.kurz: A person's total over the items of a scale: either the sum of the answers (sum score) or their mean (mean score). The mean score stays on the response scale and is comparable across different numbers of items.
skalenwert.beispiel: Four items with the answers 4, 5, 3 and 4 give a sum score of 16 and a mean score of 4.0.
skalenwert.vorsicht: If items are missing, a sum score is not comparable. The mean of the available items is then used, often only if enough answers are present. Not the same as the factor score: a factor score comes from factor analysis and weights the items by their loadings. A scale score is a simple mean or sum of the items.

smr.kurz: The ratio of observed to expected deaths in a group. What is expected is what would occur at the age-specific rates of a comparison population. 1 means as many as expected, above 1 more.
smr.beispiel: In an occupational group, 30 people die. According to the population rates, 20 would be expected. The SMR is 30/20 = 1.5.
smr.vorsicht: The SMR holds for the age distribution studied. Two SMRs from different groups are not directly comparable with each other.

sobel.kurz: Does an indirect effect differ from 0? The Sobel test divides a · b by its standard error √(b² · SEa² + a² · SEb²) and checks the quotient like a z.
sobel.vorsicht: The product a · b is usually not normally distributed, especially in small samples. A bootstrap interval is regarded as more reliable.

somers-d.kurz: How well does one ordered characteristic predict another? Somers' d is like gamma but also includes the ties in the predicted characteristic in the denominator. It has a direction: there is a predicting and a predicted characteristic.
somers-d.beispiel: Same table: fitness predicted from training d = 1584/3332 = 0.475; training predicted from fitness d = 1584/3324 = 0.477.
somers-d.vorsicht: There are two values per table, depending on direction. Clarify which characteristic counts as predicted before reading.

sozial-erwuenschtheit.kurz: Answering the way that goes down well. Social desirability is the tendency to give information that appears appropriate, even if it is not quite true.
sozial-erwuenschtheit.beispiel: When asked how many cigarettes are smoked per day, the number given may be lower in a face-to-face conversation than in an anonymous questionnaire.
sozial-erwuenschtheit.vorsicht: It concerns mainly sensitive topics. Anonymity and neutral wording reduce it but do not remove it.

soziodemografie.kurz: The information about the person that describes groups and allows comparisons: age, sex, education, occupation, income, place of residence. They belong at the end or start of a questionnaire and serve as control variables and for weighting.
soziodemografie.beispiel: A survey compares satisfaction by age group and educational level. Both come from the sociodemographic questions.
soziodemografie.vorsicht: This information is sensitive and can identify persons. It is collected sparingly and protected.

spannweite.kurz: How far do the values reach? The range is the largest value minus the smallest. It is the simplest measure of dispersion.
spannweite.vorsicht: It rests on just two values. One extreme value enlarges it greatly, and with more cases it tends to grow.

sparsamkeit.kurz: How simple may a model be? With similar fit, the model with fewer parameters is preferred. Parsimony reduces overfitting and makes a model easier to understand.
sparsamkeit.beispiel: Two models with R² 0.93 and 0.94: the one with 1 predictor instead of 5 is more parsimonious.
sparsamkeit.vorsicht: A model must not be so simple that an important part of the relationship is missing. Parsimony is a trade-off, not a law of nature.

spearman.kurz: Do two characteristics rise together, even if not in a straight line? Spearman's rho is the Pearson correlation of the ranks. It runs from -1 to 1 and captures same-direction relationships (monotonic), not only straight ones.
spearman.beispiel: 8 people, hours of practice and score: the sum of squared rank differences is 4, so ρ = 1 - 6·4/(8·63) = 0.952.
spearman.vorsicht: A value near 0 does not rule out non-monotonic relationships such as a U shape. A high value does not show a cause.

speed-power-test.kurz: A speed test has easy tasks and tight time. The score shows how fast someone works. A power test has hard tasks and enough time. The score shows how much the person can solve.
speed-power-test.beispiel: A test with 100 easy arithmetic tasks in 3 minutes is a speed test. A test with 10 hard puzzles in 60 minutes is a power test.
speed-power-test.vorsicht: For speed tests, splitting into odd and even tasks is not permitted; it overstates the reliability.

spektrumverzerrung.kurz: A test is evaluated on people who do not resemble those it will later be used on, for example only severely ill patients and healthy volunteers. Sensitivity and specificity then look better than in practice.
spektrumverzerrung.beispiel: A rapid test is tried only on clearly ill and on healthy people. In practice there are many borderline cases, and the hit rate falls.
spektrumverzerrung.vorsicht: Sensitivity and specificity are not fixed properties of the test; they depend on the group examined.

spezifikation.kurz: From Latin species “kind” and facere “to make”. Setting up the model: which variables and which form. If an important variable is missing or the form is wrong, the model is misspecified and coefficients can be biased.
spezifikation.beispiel: If age is missing from a regression and is related to both predictor and outcome, the model is misspecified; other coefficients can be biased.

spielerfehlschluss.kurz: The mistake of thinking that after a streak chance must “even out”. With independent trials chance has no memory: the probability of the next trial stays the same.
spielerfehlschluss.beispiel: Five heads in a row has probability 0.5⁵ = 0.031. The sixth toss still shows heads with 0.5.
spielerfehlschluss.vorsicht: The opposite error exists as well: concluding from a streak that “it is going well”. First check whether the trials are really independent.
sw: fallacy of the maturity of chances

splines.kurz: A curve made up of polynomial pieces that join smoothly at fixed points (knots). It reproduces nonlinear relations flexibly without needing a single polynomial of high degree.
splines.beispiel: Age acts on blood pressure first slowly, then more strongly. A spline with two knots reproduces this bend.
splines.vorsicht: Number and position of the knots are decisions. Too many knots lead to overfitting, and at the edge of the data the curve is uncertain.

spurios.kurz: From Latin spurius: “false”. Only apparent: a relation that arises only through a third quantity, not through a relation between the two. Also called spurious correlation.
spurios.beispiel: Shoe size and reading ability in children are related because both grow with age.

srmr.kurz: A fit index that shows how far the correlations expected by the model depart from the observed ones on average. It is built from the differences of all correlation pairs. Smaller is better, 0 is a perfect match.
srmr.beispiel: SRMR = 0.04 means: the correlations predicted by the model differ from the measured ones by about 0.04 on average.
srmr.vorsicht: Values below about 0.08 are often named as good fit, which is a habit. The average can hide single large deviations.

stamm-blatt.kurz: What do the individual values and their shape look like? Each number is split: the leading digits are the stem, the last digit is the leaf. The rows form a histogram on its side, but the values stay readable.
stamm-blatt.vorsicht: Practical only for few cases, up to a few dozen values. With many values the rows become unreadably long.

standard.kurz: From English: “yardstick, usual case”. In statistics “standard” often precedes a word: standard normal distribution (mean 0, standard deviation 1), standard deviation (spread), standard error (uncertainty of a statistic). Standard deviation and standard error are not the same.
standard.beispiel: The standard normal distribution has mean 0 and standard deviation 1.

standardisierte-rate.kurz: Do two areas really differ, or only in the age of their populations? An age-standardised rate converts both to the same standard population. The influence of the age structure then drops out.
standardisierte-rate.beispiel: Both places: 1 per 1,000 among the young, 20 per 1,000 among the old. Place A 80% young: crude 4.8; place B 20% young: crude 16.2. Standard 50 to 50: 10.5 for both.
standardisierte-rate.vorsicht: The standardised rate is a calculated quantity, not an observed value. Its level depends on the chosen standard population.

standardisierter-koeffizient.kurz: How strongly does a predictor act, measured in standard deviations? The standardized coefficient is the slope when all variables were z-standardized first: change in the outcome in standard deviations per standard deviation of the predictor.
standardisierter-koeffizient.beispiel: Slope 4.13 points per hour, SD of hours 2.449, SD of scores 10.474: β = 4.13 · 2.449 / 10.474 = 0.966.
standardisierter-koeffizient.vorsicht: Beta depends on the spread in the sample, and with related predictors comparing betas says little. Not to be confused with β as the type II error.

standardisiertes-residuum.kurz: Which cells deviate noticeably from independence? The residual is observed minus expected. It is standardized by dividing it by an estimate of its spread, so that cells of different size become comparable.
standardisiertes-residuum.beispiel: Inner district and car: observed 30, expected 45, difference -15. The adjusted standardized residual is -4.26, the simple one (difference over √45) -2.24.
standardisiertes-residuum.vorsicht: There are two variants: the adjusted one is approximately standard normal, the simple one usually varies less. An absolute value above 2 is often cited as noteworthy, but with many cells some such values also occur by chance.

standardisierung.kurz: The mean is subtracted from each value and the result is divided by the standard deviation: z = (x - mean) / s. Values then have mean 0 and standard deviation 1. A z-score tells how many standard deviations a value lies from the mean.
standardisierung.beispiel: The values 4, 6, 8, 10, 12 have mean 8 and s = 3.16. The value 12 becomes z = 4 / 3.16 = 1.26.
standardisierung.vorsicht: The shape of the distribution stays unchanged. Standardizing does not make values normally distributed.

standardnormalverteilung.kurz: The normal distribution in its basic form: mean 0, standard deviation 1. Any value of a normally distributed quantity can be converted to it by standardizing (z score). So one table serves all normal distributions.
standardnormalverteilung.beispiel: The share of values below z = 1.96 is 0.975. Between -1.96 and 1.96 lie 95%.
standardnormalverteilung.vorsicht: Standardizing does not make data normally distributed. It only shifts and rescales.

stanine.kurz: A norm score scale with nine steps (1 to 9), a mean of 5 and a standard deviation of 2. Every step except 1 and 9 is half a standard deviation wide. The name stands for 'standard nine'.
stanine.beispiel: Stanine 5 covers z values from -0.25 to 0.25. Under a normal distribution, about 19.7% of the reference group fall into it.
stanine.vorsicht: The steps are coarse. Small differences in the raw score can jump across a step boundary.

startwert.kurz: A number that fixes which sequence of random numbers a program produces. With the same seed the same sequence comes out every time. A calculation involving chance can thus be repeated exactly.
startwert.beispiel: With seed 42, every run delivers the same random sample of 30 from 500 cases.
startwert.vorsicht: The seed is set before calculating and not picked after seeing the result. Different programs produce different sequences from the same seed.

stationaritaet.kurz: Does the behaviour of a time series stay the same over time? A series is (weakly) stationary if mean and variance are constant and the relationships between values depend only on the distance, not on the point in time.
stationaritaet.beispiel: Measurement errors of a device that fluctuate equally strongly around 0 every day are stationary. Temperature itself, with its seasons, is not.
stationaritaet.vorsicht: Trend and seasonality make a series non-stationary. Often differencing makes it stationary.

statistik-kennwert.kurz: In the narrow sense, any number calculated from data is called a statistic, for example a mean or a t value. So the word means not only the field but also single figures. The test statistic is such a number.
statistik-kennwert.beispiel: Mean, median and t value are each a statistic. The field of statistics deals with them.
statistik-kennwert.vorsicht: When someone says “the statistic is 2.4”, a calculated number is meant, not the field.

steigung.kurz: By how much does the outcome change when the predictor increases by 1? The slope (regression coefficient) is this average change. With several predictors it holds with the others kept equal.
steigung.beispiel: Slope 4.13: people who study one hour more score 4.13 points more on average.
steigung.vorsicht: The slope describes differences between people. It does not say what happens when one person studies more.

steigungshomogenitaet.kurz: Does the control variable act equally strongly in all groups? Homogeneity of slopes checks whether the slope of the covariate is the same in every group (interaction group × covariate). Only then is there a single adjusted difference between the groups.
steigungshomogenitaet.beispiel: mtcars: group × weight F = 2.34, p = .117; group × horsepower F = 2.70, p = .087. No clear difference of the slopes (checked for each covariate).
steigungshomogenitaet.vorsicht: A non-significant test does not prove equal slopes, especially with small groups. If it is significant, Statable shows the slope for each group; a single adjusted difference then does not hold.
steigungshomogenitaet.statable: In the analysis of covariance: the table “Test of equal slopes”, one row per control variable. If a test is significant, a table with the slope for each group follows.

sterbetafel.kurz: How many reach which age? A life table shows, for each age, how many of a starting group are still alive and the risk of dying in the next interval. Life expectancy follows from it.
sterbetafel.beispiel: Of 1,000 births, 980 reach age 10 and 975 reach age 11. The risk of dying in the 11th year of life: 5 / 980 = 0.0051.
sterbetafel.vorsicht: A period life table describes mortality in one year, not the fate of a birth cohort. The life expectancy derived from it is no promise for individuals.

stetig.kurz: A variable that can take any value within a range. Between two values there are always more. Only the measurement precision limits how many digits are reported.
stetig.beispiel: Body height: 172 cm, 172.4 cm or 172.43 cm are possible. How precisely it is reported depends on the instrument.
stetig.vorsicht: Rounded measurements look discrete (whole centimetres), but the quantity itself stays continuous.

stetigkeitskorrektur.kurz: Counts jump in whole numbers, while the normal distribution is continuous. When approximating, half a unit is therefore added or subtracted so that the area fits the steps. This adjustment is called the continuity correction.
stetigkeitskorrektur.beispiel: Binomial with n = 20, p = 0.5: P(X ≤ 7) is exactly 0.1316. Normal approximation up to 7.5: 0.1318. Without correction (up to 7): 0.0899.
stetigkeitskorrektur.vorsicht: The correction only helps in small to medium cases. For very large n it hardly matters.

stichprobeneinheit.kurz: What is drawn in the selection? The sampling unit is the unit that enters the sample. It can differ from the unit of analysis.
stichprobeneinheit.beispiel: 30 schools are selected and all pupils at each are surveyed. The sampling unit is the school, the analysis is per child.
stichprobeneinheit.vorsicht: When the unit of selection and the unit of analysis differ, observations are not independent: children from the same school often resemble each other.

stichprobenfehler.kurz: Why does every sample differ somewhat from the true value? Sampling error is the deviation that arises solely because only part of the population is drawn. It is not a mistake in the sense of a slip, and it shrinks with more cases.
stichprobenfehler.beispiel: True share 0.40: two samples with n = 200 give 0.43 and 0.37. Typical size (standard error): 0.035.
stichprobenfehler.vorsicht: It covers only chance variation. Bias from selection or measurement comes on top and does not shrink with more cases.

stichprobenkennwert.kurz: A number calculated from the data of a sample, for example the mean x̄ or the standard deviation s. It estimates the matching parameter of the population and changes from sample to sample.
stichprobenkennwert.beispiel: 80 children give a mean sleep need of 9.4 hours. Another sample would give something slightly different.
stichprobenkennwert.vorsicht: A statistic is not the true value. The standard error and the confidence interval show how far off it may be.

stichprobenplan.kurz: The description of how a sample is drawn: stratification, clusters, selection stages and the selection probabilities. Weights and the correct calculation of standard errors follow from the plan.
stichprobenplan.beispiel: First 40 schools are drawn, then 25 children per school. The design has two stages. The analysis needs stratum, cluster and weight.
stichprobenplan.vorsicht: Anyone who ignores the design and calculates as for a simple random sample gets wrong standard errors and usually intervals that are too small.

stichprobenrahmen.kurz: What is the draw made from? The sampling frame is the list or description from which the sample is drawn. It should contain every element of the population exactly once.
stichprobenrahmen.beispiel: The membership list of a club with 800 names is the frame from which 80 persons are drawn.
stichprobenrahmen.vorsicht: Persons missing from the frame can never be drawn. This biases the result even if the draw itself is clean.

stichprobenumfang.kurz: How many cases belong to the analysis? The sample size n is the number of cases in the sample. N usually stands for all cases of the population.
stichprobenumfang.beispiel: 25 people are surveyed, 3 skip a question: for this question n = 22.
stichprobenumfang.vorsicht: n can differ from analysis to analysis because missing values are excluded. The number of cases belongs with every result.

stichprobenverteilung.kurz: How different would a statistic turn out if the same study were repeated again and again with new samples? The distribution of these values is called the sampling distribution. Its spread is the standard error.
stichprobenverteilung.beispiel: Measurements with standard deviation 10, 25 cases each: the means vary with 10 / √25 = 2.
stichprobenverteilung.vorsicht: The sampling distribution is imagined, not observed. It is not the distribution of values in the one sample.

stochastik.kurz: The branch of mathematics that deals with chance. It covers probability theory (models for chance) and statistics (conclusions from data).
stochastik.beispiel: Calculating how likely 3 heads in 5 tosses are is probability theory. Drawing a conclusion about the coin from 5 observed tosses is statistics.

stochastisch.kurz: Depending on chance and describable with probabilities. The word comes from Greek for “to aim, to guess”. The opposite is deterministic.
stochastisch.beispiel: The number a die shows is a stochastic process, the fall time of a stone from 5 m in a vacuum is a deterministic one.

stochastische-konvergenz.titel: Stochastic convergence (in probability, in distribution, almost surely)
stochastische-konvergenz.kurz: Ways in which a sequence of random variables tends towards something. In probability: deviations from a value become arbitrarily unlikely. In distribution: the distributions approach a limiting distribution. Almost surely: with probability 1 the sequence goes to the value.
stochastische-konvergenz.beispiel: The law of large numbers says that the sample mean converges in probability to the expected value. The central limit theorem is a convergence in distribution.
stochastische-konvergenz.vorsicht: Almost sure convergence is stronger than convergence in probability, which is stronger than convergence in distribution.

stochastischer-prozess.kurz: A sequence or family of random variables tied to time (or place). It describes how a random system evolves.
stochastischer-prozess.beispiel: The number of calls to a hotline, hour by hour, is a stochastic process. Each hour is a random variable.
stochastischer-prozess.vorsicht: A time series is a single realisation of such a process, not the process itself.

stoervariable.kurz: What distorts the comparison? A nuisance variable distorts how the studied quantity relates to the outcome. A confounder is such a variable that is related to both.
stoervariable.beispiel: Ice cream sales and sunburns rise together. Temperature influences both and is the confounder.
stoervariable.vorsicht: Only measured confounders can be adjusted for. Randomisation also protects against unmeasured ones.

straightlining.kurz: A person gives the same answer to all questions of a matrix regardless of content. This points to low attention and distorts relations between the items.
straightlining.beispiel: All 12 items of a matrix are answered with “3”, including reversed ones. This is implausible.
straightlining.vorsicht: Identical answers are not always carelessness; someone who really agrees with everything answers the same way. Reversed items help to tell the two apart.

stratifiziert.kurz: From Latin stratum “layer” and facere “to make”. Divided into layers: sampling or analysis is done separately per layer. Groups stay visible that would give a different picture when pooled.
stratifiziert.beispiel: A stratified analysis by gender means: results per group, not combined.

stratifizierte-cox.kurz: A Cox regression that allows a separate baseline hazard for each stratum but estimates common coefficients for the other predictors. It is the remedy when a variable violates the proportional hazards assumption.
stratifizierte-cox.beispiel: The study runs at three clinics. With the clinic as stratum, each has its own baseline hazard, and the treatment effect is estimated jointly.
stratifizierte-cox.vorsicht: The effect of the stratifying variable itself cannot be estimated. The treatment effect must be similar across strata.

streudiagramm.kurz: Are two quantities related? A scatter plot shows each case as a point: one value fixes the horizontal position, the other the vertical position.
streudiagramm.beispiel: 30 people: hours of study (horizontal) and points achieved (vertical). If the cloud rises to the upper right, more hours usually go with more points.
streudiagramm.vorsicht: A pattern shows an association, not a cause. Identical value pairs lie on top of each other: there are then more cases than points.

streudiagramm-matrix.kurz: A panel of many scatterplots in which each variable is set against every other. It shows relations, outliers and patterns between many variables at a glance.
streudiagramm-matrix.beispiel: With 4 variables there are 4 · 3 / 2 = 6 different scatterplots. The diagonal often shows the distributions of the single variables.
streudiagramm-matrix.vorsicht: With many variables the panel becomes confusing: with 10 variables there are 45 plots.

streuungsmass.kurz: How different are the values from each other? A measure of dispersion describes in one number how widely the values are spread around the centre. Examples: range, interquartile range, variance, standard deviation.
streuungsmass.beispiel: Two groups with mean 50: values 49, 50, 51 (range 2) and 30, 50, 70 (range 40).
streuungsmass.vorsicht: The same mean can come with very different spread. A measure of location alone does not describe data.

streuungstests-rang.titel: Rank tests for differences in spread (Ansari-Bradley, Mood, Siegel-Tukey)
streuungstests-rang.kurz: Methods that test for two groups whether the values differ in spread, without requiring normality. They work with the position of the ranks: extreme ranks point to larger spread.
streuungstests-rang.beispiel: Two instruments measure the same sample repeatedly. A rank test checks whether the measurements of one spread more widely.
streuungstests-rang.vorsicht: The tests assume equal location (equal median) in both groups. With different locations they are biased.

strukturbruch.kurz: A sudden, lasting change in the behaviour of a time series or of a relation, for example in level, trend or a regression coefficient, from some point in time. A structural break makes a single model unsuitable for the whole period.
strukturbruch.beispiel: After a change in the law, the level of registrations jumps and stays higher. A model for the whole period fits poorly before and after the break.
strukturbruch.vorsicht: A break is not the same as an outlier, which affects only one time point. The time point is often not known in advance and is searched for with tests (Chow, CUSUM).

strukturmatrix.kurz: The table of correlations between numbers and factors (after an oblique rotation) or between numbers and discriminant functions (within the groups). It tells what a factor or function stands for. For factors it follows from the pattern matrix times the factor correlation.
strukturmatrix.beispiel: Pattern loadings 0.70 and 0.10, factor correlation 0.4. Structure loading on factor 1: 0.70 + 0.10 · 0.4 = 0.74. On factor 2: 0.70 · 0.4 + 0.10 = 0.38.
strukturmatrix.vorsicht: With uncorrelated factors (for example after varimax) the pattern and structure matrices are the same.
strukturmatrix.statable: Under the result of the discriminant analysis: structure matrix with the share per function.

strukturmodell.kurz: The part of a model that describes the relationships among the latent variables, that is the paths between them. It complements the measurement model, which assigns the items to the latent variables.
strukturmodell.beispiel: A path from “enjoyment of learning” to “achievement” and from “achievement” to “self-image”. Which items belong to which construct is stated in the measurement model.

stuart-maxwell.kurz: A test of whether two measurements of the same cases have the same marginal distributions, with more than two categories. It is the extension of the McNemar test to marginal homogeneity.
stuart-maxwell.beispiel: The same 200 people rate a topic on three levels before and after some information. The test checks whether the overall distribution of the ratings changed.
stuart-maxwell.vorsicht: Equal marginal distributions do not rule out changes in both directions. They say nothing about individual changes.

studentisiertes-residuum.kurz: A residual divided by its own estimated standard error. The error of a case depends on its leverage, so raw residuals do not have equal spread. For the externally studentised residual, the case is left out when estimating the spread.
studentisiertes-residuum.vorsicht: Values above about 2 or 3 are often seen as conspicuous, a habit. With many cases, a few large values are expected even without errors.

subgruppe.kurz: From Latin sub “under”. A part of the sample, for example by age. The more subgroups are examined after the fact, the more likely a chance finding appears; they are also small.
subgruppe.beispiel: With 20 subgroup tests at α = 0.05, one chance hit is expected on average if there is no effect anywhere.

subjektive-wahrscheinlichkeit.kurz: A probability as a degree of belief: how certain is someone given what they know? It can be stated for one-off events and changes when new knowledge arrives.
subjektive-wahrscheinlichkeit.beispiel: The judgement “the train arrives on time with 0.7” rests on experience and the timetable.
subjektive-wahrscheinlichkeit.vorsicht: Subjective does not mean arbitrary. It must be free of contradiction and follow the rules of probability.

suffizienz.kurz: Which number from the data is enough for the estimate? A sufficient statistic (Latin: enough) holds all the information about the unknown value that is contained in the data. The rest of the data adds nothing more about it.
suffizienz.beispiel: 20 coin tosses, 13 heads: the number 13 is enough for the probability of heads. The order of the tosses adds nothing.
suffizienz.vorsicht: Sufficiency always refers to a particular model. If the model does not fit, the order or other details may matter after all.

suggestivfrage.kurz: A question that suggests a particular answer, for example through loaded words. Related errors are the double-barrelled question (two things in one question) and the double negative.
suggestivfrage.beispiel: “Isn't the programme also far too expensive?” suggests “yes”. “Satisfied with price and quality?” asks two things at once.
suggestivfrage.vorsicht: Someone who is satisfied with only one of the two cannot answer properly. The error is not noticed in the analysis.

summe-der-quadrate.kurz: How much deviation is there in the data altogether? The sum of squares adds the squared deviations of all values from the mean. Variance and analysis of variance are built on it.
summe-der-quadrate.vorsicht: The sum of squares grows with the number of cases. Only after dividing by the degrees of freedom (variance) can data sets be compared.

summenkurve.kurz: What percentage of cases lie up to a given value? The cumulative curve (empirical distribution function) plots over each value the share of cases that are at most that large. It rises from 0 to 1.
summenkurve.beispiel: Waiting times 3, 4, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9, 10, 40: at 6 minutes the curve is at 0.5, because 5 of 10 values are at most 6.
summenkurve.vorsicht: Steep parts mean many values close together. Peaks are harder to spot in a cumulative curve than in a histogram, but shares can be read directly.

suppressor.kurz: A variable that is hardly related to the outcome but is related to another predictor, and thereby strengthens that predictor's relation with the outcome in the model. It suppresses disturbing parts of the other predictor.
suppressor.beispiel: r(x₁, y) = 0.40, r(x₂, y) = 0, r(x₁, x₂) = 0.50. In the joint model β₁ rises to 0.40/0.75 = 0.53, β₂ becomes -0.27.
suppressor.vorsicht: The sign of x₂ in the model has no counterpart in the single correlation. Such effects are hard to interpret and need a justification in content.

surrogatendpunkt.kurz: A stand-in measure that is easier or quicker to obtain than what really matters. It helps only if it reliably signals the real goal.
surrogatendpunkt.beispiel: Blood pressure is measured instead of stroke, because it is available after weeks rather than years.
surrogatendpunkt.vorsicht: If a drug improves the stand-in value, it need not improve the real goal.

sutva.kurz: An assumption of causal analysis: a person's outcome depends only on their own treatment, not on the treatment of others, and there is only one version of the treatment. Without it, the effect is not uniquely defined.
sutva.beispiel: With a vaccination, a vaccinated person also protects contacts (herd protection). A person's outcome depends on others' treatment, so SUTVA is violated.
sutva.vorsicht: The assumption is made tacitly in many studies. With contagion, neighbourhoods or classes it often does not hold.

svm.kurz: A method for classification. It seeks the dividing line (in general a surface) between two groups with the largest distance to the nearest cases, the support vectors. With kernels it also separates groups that are not linearly separable.
svm.beispiel: Two groups of points in the plane are separated by the line running in the middle of the gap between them.
svm.vorsicht: Results are hard to interpret; the choice of kernel and the penalty for errors are hyperparameters.

symmetrie.kurz: Do both sides look the same? Symmetric means: the left half of the distribution is the mirror image of the right half, mirrored at the centre. Mean and median then coincide.
symmetrie.beispiel: Values 2, 4, 6, 8, 10: mean and median are 6, both sides are spread equally.
symmetrie.vorsicht: Symmetric is not the same as normally distributed; a uniform distribution is symmetric too. Mean equal to median alone does not prove symmetry.

syntax.kurz: Commands as text instead of clicks. In SPSS and PSPP the command file is called syntax. It records what was calculated and can be run again. An analysis thus becomes repeatable and checkable.
syntax.beispiel: The line FREQUENCIES VARIABLES=age. counts how often each age occurs.
syntax.vorsicht: Every program has its own command language. SPSS syntax does not run in R or Stata.

synthese.kurz: From Greek synthesis: “putting together”. Bringing parts or results together. A meta-analysis is a quantitative synthesis of several studies.
synthese.beispiel: From twelve studies on the same training, a pooled effect is computed: a synthesis.

synthetische-kontrolle.kurz: A method for estimating the effect of a measure in one unit (country, region). A weighted combination of many untreated units is built that closely resembled the treated unit before the measure. Its later course shows what would have happened without the measure.
synthetische-kontrolle.beispiel: A country introduces a tax. An artificial “comparison country” is built from other countries that had the same course before the tax. The later gap is the estimated effect.
synthetische-kontrolle.vorsicht: It holds only if the combination fits very well before the measure. Without repetitions, uncertainty is hard to state.

system-missing.kurz: An empty field in which the program finds no value. It counts as missing by itself and is excluded from calculations. Unlike a missing-value code such as 99 it need not be declared missing.
system-missing.beispiel: For 100 respondents the field “age” stays empty for 7 persons. The program counts 93 valid values.
system-missing.vorsicht: An empty field must be told apart from a 0. A 0 is a value and is included.

systematisch.kurz: From Greek systema: “arrangement”. First: planned, by a fixed procedure, like a systematic review. Second: acting in one direction, not by chance. A systematic error is a bias, unlike a random one.
systematisch.beispiel: A scale that always shows 2 g too much has a systematic error; values swinging up and down are random.

systematische-stichprobe.kurz: How does one draw from a long list without a draw for each entry? In a systematic sample, every k-th entry is taken after a random start. The step is k = N / n.
systematische-stichprobe.beispiel: 2000 index cards, n = 50: k = 40. Random start between 1 and 40, then every 40th card.
systematische-stichprobe.vorsicht: If the list has a regular pattern at spacing k, the sample is biased. A random start alone does not help then.

systematisches-review.kurz: How does one find all studies on a question and appraise them fairly? A systematic review searches by rules fixed in advance, selects studies by set criteria and appraises them. It may, but need not, end in a meta-analysis.
systematisches-review.beispiel: Search in three databases with search terms fixed in advance. Two people select independently of each other. Disagreements are settled by set rules.
systematisches-review.vorsicht: A literature overview without fixed rules for searching and selecting is not a systematic review.

t-test.kurz: Do means differ by more than chance would lead one to expect? The t test compares a mean with a target value, two groups, or two measurements of the same cases. The spread is estimated from the data; the statistic follows the t distribution.
t-test.beispiel: Three forms: 8 measurements against a target value, two separate groups, or the same people before and after.
t-test.vorsicht: The t test checks means and assumes roughly normal values or a large enough group. The p value says nothing about the size of the difference.

t-verteilung.kurz: How far is a mean from its expected value when the spread itself is only estimated? The t distribution describes this. It looks like the normal distribution but has wider tails. With more degrees of freedom it comes closer to the normal distribution.
t-verteilung.beispiel: With 9 degrees of freedom, 95% of t values lie between -2.262 and 2.262. For the normal distribution they would lie between -1.96 and 1.96.
t-verteilung.vorsicht: The wider tails make up for the uncertainty of the estimated spread. With few degrees of freedom the difference from the normal distribution is clear.

t-wert-norm.kurz: A norm score with a mean of 50 and a standard deviation of 10. It is calculated from the z score: T = 50 + 10 x z.
t-wert-norm.beispiel: Raw score 130, norm mean 100, norm standard deviation 20: z = 1.5 and T = 65.
t-wert-norm.vorsicht: Not to be confused with the t value of the t-test.

tamhane.kurz: A post hoc test for pairwise comparisons when the spreads in the groups are unequal. It is conservative and adjusts the error for all comparisons.
tamhane.beispiel: Five groups have very different spreads. Tamhane's T2 compares all pairs without assuming equal variances.
tamhane.vorsicht: It is more cautious than the Games-Howell test and therefore has less power. With equal spread, Tukey is used.

tau-aequivalent.kurz: An assumption about items: they measure the same trait with equal (unstandardised) loadings but may have different amounts of measurement error. Only then does Cronbach's alpha equal the reliability.
tau-aequivalent.beispiel: Three items all load 1.0 on the same trait, but their error variances are 0.5, 1.0 and 1.5. This is tau-equivalence. Standardised, the loadings then differ.
tau-aequivalent.vorsicht: If the loadings differ (congeneric), alpha underestimates reliability. McDonald's omega is better suited.

tau2-schaetzer.titel: Estimators of heterogeneity τ² (DerSimonian-Laird, Paule-Mandel, REML)
tau2-schaetzer.kurz: Different methods for estimating the spread of true effects between studies (τ²). DerSimonian-Laird is the oldest and most widespread. Paule-Mandel and REML are regarded as more reliable with few studies or large heterogeneity. Sidik-Jonkman is a further proposal.
tau2-schaetzer.beispiel: Eight studies with effects from -0.20 to 1.10 (variances 0.03 to 0.07) give τ² = 0.171 with DerSimonian-Laird and τ² = 0.178 with REML. The pooled interval is 0.09 to 0.73 and 0.09 to 0.74 respectively.
tau2-schaetzer.vorsicht: The choice of estimator has to be stated. With few studies the result can depend noticeably on it.

taxonomie.kurz: From Greek taxis “order” and nomos “law”. A division into classes by fixed rules. In statistics, for example, the division of scale types or the result of a cluster analysis.
taxonomie.beispiel: The levels of measurement form a taxonomy: nominal, ordinal, interval, ratio.

taylor-linearisierung.kurz: A method for computing standard errors of complicated statistics from complex samples. The statistic is approximated by a sum using a Taylor expansion, and the variance of that sum can be calculated with stratum, cluster and weight taken into account.
taylor-linearisierung.beispiel: The standard error of a ratio of two sums is computed from a linear approximation of the ratio, allowing for the sampling design.
taylor-linearisierung.vorsicht: The approximation is inexact for small samples and strongly nonlinear statistics. The alternatives are replication methods.

teilnehmende-beobachtung.kurz: The researchers take part in the events in the field and observe them at the same time. This captures processes that are not named in surveys. The observations are kept in field notes.
teilnehmende-beobachtung.beispiel: A researcher works in a kitchen for two weeks and notes how arrangements actually go.
teilnehmende-beobachtung.vorsicht: Participation and observation can get in each other's way. The role of the researchers in the field has to be disclosed.

teilpopulation.kurz: A group within the respondents for which separate results are calculated, such as women or an age group. In surveys with a complex design, the whole sample is kept and only the subgroup is analysed; the sample is not cut beforehand.
teilpopulation.beispiel: The mean of those aged over 65 is calculated with the domain function of the survey software, which preserves the design of the whole sample.
teilpopulation.vorsicht: Anyone who cuts the sample down to the subgroup beforehand loses stratum and cluster information and gets wrong standard errors.

tendenz-zur-mitte.kurz: The tendency to avoid extreme options and to choose the middle category or the options near the middle. It lowers the spread of answers.
tendenz-zur-mitte.beispiel: On a scale from 1 to 7, almost all answers lie at 3, 4 and 5.
tendenz-zur-mitte.vorsicht: Spread and correlations become smaller as a result. Means, by contrast, often stay similar.

testentzerrung.kurz: The procedure for bringing results of different test forms onto a common scale. The same score then means the same in form A and form B, even if one form is somewhat harder.
testentzerrung.beispiel: Form B is slightly harder than form A. After equating, a raw score of 30 on form B corresponds to 32 on form A.
testentzerrung.vorsicht: This requires common tasks or comparable groups. Without them the forms cannot be linked reliably.

testhalbierung.kurz: A test is divided into two halves, for example odd and even items. The halves are correlated and the result is stepped up to full length (Spearman-Brown formula).
testhalbierung.beispiel: The halves correlate r = 0.70. Stepped up: 2 x 0.70 / (1 + 0.70) = 0.82.
testhalbierung.vorsicht: The result depends on how the test is split. Cronbach's alpha avoids this choice.

testinformation.kurz: A curve that shows how precisely a test measures the trait at each level. The higher the information, the smaller the measurement error. It is the sum of the information of the individual items.
testinformation.beispiel: If a test has an information of 16 at some trait level, the standard error there is 1/√16 = 0.25.
testinformation.vorsicht: Precision is not the same everywhere. A test can measure precisely in the middle and hardly at the edges.

teststatistik.kurz: How far do the data depart from what the null hypothesis leads one to expect? The test statistic condenses this into one number, such as t, z, F or χ². Its distribution under H₀ gives the p value.
teststatistik.beispiel: Difference of means 4.0, standard error 1.6: t = 4.0 / 1.6 = 2.5. With 38 degrees of freedom, p = 0.017.
teststatistik.vorsicht: The same data give a different test statistic for each test. Only the matching distribution yields the matching p value.

theil-index.kurz: A measure of inequality built from ratios to the mean: T = mean of (x/μ) · ln(x/μ). It is 0 for equality and grows with inequality. It can be decomposed by groups into parts within and between the groups.
theil-index.vorsicht: The values are not bounded by 1 and are harder to read than the Gini coefficient. The index is therefore mostly used for decomposition.

theoretische-saettigung.kurz: The point at which further data show no new categories or relations. In qualitative research it determines when data collection ends, not a sample size fixed in advance.
theoretische-saettigung.beispiel: After 12 interviews no new themes appear. Three more interviews only confirm what is known.
theoretische-saettigung.vorsicht: Saturation is a judgement by the researchers and hard to check. It holds for the research question, not for the topic as a whole.

theoretisches-sampling.kurz: A selection of cases in qualitative research guided by the emerging theory: which cases would test or extend the categories so far? The selection is thus steered during the study.
theoretisches-sampling.beispiel: After the first interviews with teachers at city schools, a person from a rural school is interviewed on purpose to see whether a category looks different there.
theoretisches-sampling.vorsicht: It is not random selection and does not aim at representativeness. The selection has to be justified transparently.

theorie.kurz: How do things fit together, and why? A theory is a connected set of statements that explains observations and makes predictions that can be tested against data.
theorie.beispiel: Assumption: spaced practice strengthens memory more than one long session. Testable prediction: after a week, more words are remembered.
theorie.vorsicht: In everyday speech, 'theory' often means 'mere guess'. In science, a well-tested theory is the opposite of that.

thurstone-skala.kurz: An attitude scale in which judges first place each statement on a scale. From these placements each statement gets a scale value. A person's score is the mean scale value of the statements they agree with.
thurstone-skala.beispiel: One statement has the scale value 3 (a rather negative attitude to a topic), another 9 (a rather positive attitude). Someone who agrees only with the first scores 3.
thurstone-skala.vorsicht: The effort is high, so the Likert scale is far more widespread.

tli.kurz: A fit index that, like the CFI, compares the model with a null model but penalises models with many parameters more strongly. It is usually between 0 and 1 but can go slightly beyond.
tli.beispiel: Model: χ² = 48 with 24 degrees of freedom. Null model: χ² = 600 with 36. TLI = (16.667 - 2) / (16.667 - 1) = 0.936.
tli.vorsicht: Values from 0.95 are often named as good fit, which is a habit. CFI and TLI of the same model can differ slightly.

tobit.kurz: A regression model for an outcome that is censored at a limit, such as 0, because many values lie exactly at the limit. It assumes a continuous quantity behind it.
tobit.beispiel: Spending on concerts: many people spend nothing (0). The model assumes that behind the 0 lies an unobserved “interest” that stayed below the threshold.
tobit.vorsicht: The model is sensitive to wrong distributional assumptions. It does not distinguish whether a zero comes from lack of wish or lack of opportunity.

toleranz.kurz: How much of a predictor is independent of the other predictors? Tolerance is 1 - R²ⱼ, the share of its variation that the other predictors do not predict. It is the reciprocal of the VIF.
toleranz.beispiel: Tolerance 0.124 (= 1 - 0.9358²), which corresponds to a VIF of 8.05: only 12.4% of the variation in practice tasks is independent of study hours.
toleranz.vorsicht: A small tolerance means strong collinearity. Cut-offs such as 0.1 or 0.2 are habits.

toleranzintervall.kurz: An interval that encloses, with a given confidence, at least a certain share of all values in the population. It is meant for values, not for a parameter.
toleranzintervall.beispiel: A 95/95 tolerance interval for the thickness of parts contains at least 95 % of all parts with 95 % confidence.
toleranzintervall.vorsicht: The tolerance interval is often confused with the confidence interval and the prediction interval. It is wider than the confidence interval of the mean.

top-box.titel: Top box (share of the highest response options)
top-box.kurz: The share of respondents who chose the highest option(s) of a scale. “Top-2-box” combines the two highest levels. It is used as a simple key figure for satisfaction or agreement.
top-box.beispiel: Of 200 respondents, 60 choose level 5 and 50 choose level 4: top-2-box = 110/200 = 55 %.
top-box.vorsicht: The value throws information away, because the lower levels and the distribution stay invisible. Two very different distributions can have the same top-box value.

totale-wahrscheinlichkeit.kurz: If everything possible splits into groups that exclude each other, the probability of an event is the sum over the groups: group share times probability of the event within the group.
totale-wahrscheinlichkeit.beispiel: Plant A supplies 60 % with 2 % rejects, plant B 40 % with 5 %: 0.6 · 0.02 + 0.4 · 0.05 = 0.032.

trace-plot.kurz: A chart showing the drawn values of a parameter in the order of the draws, usually with several chains. It shows whether the chains mix and reach the same region.
trace-plot.beispiel: Four chains look like a dense jumble of hairs: they have converged. If they run apart or drift, they have not.
trace-plot.vorsicht: A good picture is no guarantee. It is one of the checks alongside R-hat and the effective sample size.

trainingsdaten.kurz: On which data does the model learn, and on which is it checked? The training data are used to fit the model. The test data stay untouched and serve only to check the prediction. Both come from the same source but do not overlap.
trainingsdaten.beispiel: 1,000 cases split at random: 800 for fitting, 200 for checking.
trainingsdaten.vorsicht: Anyone who changes the model because of the test result uses the test data as well. They are then no longer untouched.

transformation.kurz: Every value of a variable is converted by the same rule. The purpose is another unit, a comparable scale or a better distribution shape. The result is a new variable.
transformation.beispiel: Weight from kg to g (times 1000), or the logarithm of income.
transformation.vorsicht: Results hold on the converted scale. The mean of log values, converted back, is the geometric mean, not the arithmetic mean.

trend.kurz: Does it go up or down in the long run? The trend is the long-term direction of a time series, without the short-term fluctuations. It can be straight or curved.
trend.beispiel: Sales rise by 2 items per month on average, with fluctuations around that line.
trend.vorsicht: A trend makes a series non-stationary. Two series with trends often seem related even if they have nothing to do with each other.

trendanalyse.kurz: Do the means rise evenly with the levels, or does the pattern bend? Trend analysis splits the pattern across ordered groups into a linear, quadratic and cubic part and so on. Each part is a contrast with fixed weights and has its own test.
trendanalyse.beispiel: ToothGrowth, tooth length at dose 0.5, 1 and 2: linear trend t = 11.6, p < .001; quadratic trend t = −1.2, p = .24 (equal spacing).
trendanalyse.vorsicht: The result depends on whether the levels are equally far apart. The doses 0.5, 1 and 2 are not; with the true spacing the quadratic trend becomes clear (t = −3.35, p = .001).
trendanalyse.statable: Under the result of the analysis of variance: “Planned comparisons”, section trend analysis. Choose equal spacing or, if the groups are named by numbers, the true spacing.

trendbereinigung.kurz: Removing a trend from a time series so that the remaining fluctuations can be studied. Usual are residuals from a trend line and differencing.
trendbereinigung.beispiel: A series rises by about 2 points each year. Subtracting the trend line leaves the fluctuating remainder.
trendbereinigung.vorsicht: The choice of method changes the result. A trend line is unsuitable for a random walk, where differencing is used.

trendtest.kurz: Do the means rise or fall steadily across the levels? A trend test in an analysis of variance with ordered levels checks whether the group means follow a straight line (linear trend) or a curve (quadratic trend). Contrasts are used for this.
trendtest.beispiel: Dose 1, 2, 3 with means 5, 7, 9: linear contrast (-1, 0, 1) = 4; t(9) = 6.93; p = 0.00007. The quadratic contrast (1, -2, 1) = 0.
trendtest.vorsicht: The levels must have an order, and the standard weights assume equal spacing. The trend says nothing about values outside the tested levels.

trennung.kurz: A predictor predicts the outcome of a logistic regression perfectly, for example all cases from a certain value have the event. There is then no finite best coefficient, the estimate runs off to infinity, and programs issue warnings.
trennung.beispiel: All persons with a value of at least 5 have the event, none below do. The coefficient is estimated arbitrarily large.
trennung.vorsicht: A coefficient of 20 or more with a huge standard error points to it. The Firth correction or a prior (Bayes) helps.

triangulation.kurz: From Latin triangulum: “triangle”, a term from land surveying. The same topic is studied with several methods, data sources or people. If the results agree, that supports the finding.
triangulation.beispiel: The same topic is studied with a survey, observation and school grades; if all point the same way, the finding is strengthened.

trim-and-fill.kurz: How does the overall effect change if studies are missing in the funnel plot? The method trims the asymmetric studies, estimates the overall effect and adds mirrored, missing studies (fill). The overall effect is then recomputed.
trim-and-fill.beispiel: In the funnel plot, studies with a small effect are missing at the lower left: the method adds, for example, 3 mirrored studies, and the overall effect falls.
trim-and-fill.vorsicht: The result is only a sensitivity check, and the added studies are estimated, not real. It assumes that publication bias is the only cause of the asymmetry.

trivial.kurz: From Latin trivialis: “commonplace”. Of little consequence, or in mathematics self-evident. A trivial effect is a very small one; it can still be significant in a large sample.
trivial.beispiel: The correlation of a variable with itself is 1: a trivial result.

tschuprow.kurz: An association measure for two nominal characteristics, derived from chi-square. It lies between 0 and 1. Unlike Cramér's V it reaches 1 only for square tables.
tschuprow.vorsicht: There are no generally valid limits for “strong”. For non-square tables T is smaller than V and not directly comparable.

tukey.kurz: Which pairs of groups differ when all pairs are compared? The Tukey test (HSD) compares all pairs of groups and keeps the overall error rate. It suits groups of about equal size and similar spreads.
tukey.beispiel: Means 5, 7, 9, 4 values each: a difference of 1.61 or more counts as important. B-A = 2 (p = 0.018), C-A = 4 (p = 0.0002), C-B = 2 (p = 0.018).
tukey.vorsicht: When spreads differ a lot, the Games-Howell test is the alternative. For unequal group sizes there is the Tukey-Kramer version.

typ-iii-quadratsumme.kurz: How much does a term explain when all others are already in the model? The Type III sum of squares measures the gain in explained variation when a term is added last, adjusted for all other terms. SPSS calculates it by default.
typ-iii-quadratsumme.beispiel: Analysis of covariance with cylinders, weight and horsepower: the F value for weight (19.5; p < .001) tests weight beyond cylinders and horsepower.
typ-iii-quadratsumme.vorsicht: With equal cell sizes all types are the same. With unequal cells they are different questions: Type III tests each main effect on the unweighted means of the cells.
typ-iii-quadratsumme.statable: The tables of the two-way analysis of variance and the analysis of covariance contain the Type III sums of squares: each row is the gain due to this term beyond all others.

typenbildung.kurz: Grouping cases into types that are similar within and different from each other, based on several characteristics. In qualitative research this is done by comparison, in quantitative research often by cluster analysis.
typenbildung.beispiel: From interviews about commuting, the types “time optimiser”, “habitual driver” and “switcher” are formed.
typenbildung.vorsicht: Types are constructions by the researchers. They are tools, not groups that exist in the world.

ueberdeckung.kurz: How often does an interval procedure really contain the true value? Coverage is the actual share of intervals that include the true value. It should match the confidence level.
ueberdeckung.beispiel: Wald interval for a share with true p = 0.1 and n = 20: coverage is only 0.876 instead of the promised 0.95.
ueberdeckung.vorsicht: The stated level is a promise. Whether a procedure keeps it depends on n and on the true value.

ueberdispersion.kurz: For count data the Poisson distribution allows only a variance equal to the mean. If the data vary more, this is called overdispersion. Standard errors are then too small and p values too optimistic.
ueberdispersion.beispiel: Doctor visits per year: mean 2, variance 6. Poisson expects a variance of 2.
ueberdispersion.vorsicht: The cause can be missing predictors or clustering in certain persons. The negative binomial distribution often fits better then.

ueberextraktion.kurz: Over-extraction means keeping too many factors, under-extraction too few. Both distort the picture. The Kaiser criterion tends to over-extract; parallel analysis is more reliable.
ueberextraktion.beispiel: The Kaiser criterion keeps five factors, parallel analysis two. With five factors, some arise on which hardly any item loads.
ueberextraktion.vorsicht: The number of factors should never depend on one criterion alone. It also has to be justified in content.

ueberlebensrate.kurz: The share of people still alive after a given time, often counted from diagnosis or start of treatment. Usual are statements at 1, 5 or 10 years.
ueberlebensrate.beispiel: Of 100 treated people, 70 are still alive after 5 years. The 5-year survival rate is 70 %.
ueberlebensrate.vorsicht: With censored data the share is not enough; the rate is estimated with Kaplan-Meier. Comparisons between groups with screening are distorted by lead time.

ueberlebensverzerrung.kurz: Only what is left over is looked at. Those who dropped out are missing, which gives too favourable a picture.
ueberlebensverzerrung.beispiel: An analysis of only the firms that exist today shows high profits. The firms that failed are not included.
ueberlebensverzerrung.vorsicht: The error lies in the choice of data, not in the calculation.

ueberlebenszeitanalyse.kurz: How long does it take until an event? Survival analysis analyses times until an event, such as death, relapse, resignation or device failure. It also takes into account cases where the event has not yet occurred.
ueberlebenszeitanalyse.beispiel: Time until a disease returns in 120 people. In 70 it occurred, in 50 it did not until the end of observation.
ueberlebenszeitanalyse.vorsicht: The event need not be death, and the time need not be in years. Cases without an event must not be left out, otherwise the duration is underestimated.

ueberlegenheit.kurz: How likely is it that a randomly chosen value from one group is higher than a randomly chosen value from the other? 0.5 means no difference. Equal values count half. It is the U of the group in question divided by all pairs.
ueberlegenheit.vorsicht: The number refers to randomly drawn pairs, not to every single person.

uebertragungseffekt.kurz: The effect of an earlier condition reaches into the next one. In repeated-measures designs this distorts the comparison of conditions. Remedies are pauses and a balanced order.
uebertragungseffekt.beispiel: Someone who first solves a hard task is still tired during the second, easy task.
uebertragungseffekt.vorsicht: Balancing spreads the effect evenly over the conditions but does not remove it.

umfragegewicht.kurz: How does each respondent count properly? The survey weight states how many persons of the population a case stands for. The basic value is 1 divided by the chance of being drawn.
umfragegewicht.beispiel: Group A: every 10th person drawn, weight 10. Group B: every 50th drawn, weight 50.
umfragegewicht.vorsicht: Weights also change the standard errors. Unweighted formulas often underestimate them and do not suit weighted data.

unabhaengige-variable.kurz: Which quantity is meant to explain, or is changed? The independent variable (IV) is the quantity whose influence is studied. In an experiment the researchers set it. The dependent variable is the one that might change.
unabhaengige-variable.beispiel: Study time (10, 20 or 30 minutes) as the independent variable, test score as the dependent variable.
unabhaengige-variable.vorsicht: Outside experiments, 'independent' only describes the role in the calculation. The quantity need not be the cause.

unabhaengiger-t-test.kurz: Do the means of two separate groups differ? The independent samples t test compares two groups consisting of different people. In its standard form a common variance is assumed, with n₁ + n₂ - 2 degrees of freedom.
unabhaengiger-t-test.beispiel: Group A: 12, 14, 15, 11, 13 (mean 13); group B: 16, 18, 15, 17, 19 (mean 17): t = -4.0 with 8 degrees of freedom, p = 0.004.
unabhaengiger-t-test.vorsicht: The groups must be independent. With unequal spreads the Welch test is safer.

unabhaengigkeit.kurz: Two events are independent if knowing one does not change the probability of the other. Then the probability that both occur is the product of the single probabilities.
unabhaengigkeit.vorsicht: Mutually exclusive events (with probability above 0) are not independent: if one occurs, the other is certainly ruled out. Independent variables are uncorrelated, but uncorrelated ones are not always independent.

unabhaengigkeit-beobachtungen.kurz: Does one value influence the next? Independent observations arise from separate, unconnected measurements. Almost all tests assume this. It is violated, for example, by repeated measurements on the same person or by measurements within shared groups.
unabhaengigkeit-beobachtungen.beispiel: 30 children from 3 classes are not 30 independent cases. Children in the same class resemble each other. 10 measurements on one person do not count like 10 people.
unabhaengigkeit-beobachtungen.vorsicht: A violation usually makes p values too small. A larger sample does not fix it, only a fitting model does.
