ungerichtete-hypothese.kurz: Is there any difference, whichever direction? A non-directional hypothesis leaves open which group is higher, for example μ₁ ≠ μ₂. It is tested two-sided. This is the usual default.
ungerichtete-hypothese.beispiel: Hypothesis: the two teaching methods lead to different results. A clearly higher as well as a clearly lower mean speaks against H₀.
ungerichtete-hypothese.vorsicht: A two-sided test first says only that a difference exists. The direction is read from the means.

ungleichung-tschebyscheff.kurz: For any distribution with an expected value and a standard deviation, at least 1 - 1/k² of the values lie within k standard deviations of the expected value (k greater than 1). It needs no assumption about the shape.
ungleichung-tschebyscheff.beispiel: k = 2: at least 75 % of the values. k = 3: at least 1 - 1/9 = 88.9 %.
ungleichung-tschebyscheff.vorsicht: This is a lower bound. For a normal distribution about 95 % actually lie within k = 2.

unimodal.kurz: Does the distribution have one peak? Unimodal means single-peaked: there is one most frequent region, and the frequency falls off to both sides.
unimodal.beispiel: Reaction times in a task: most around 400 milliseconds, fewer cases shorter or longer.
unimodal.vorsicht: Single-peaked does not mean normally distributed. Skewed distributions are unimodal too.

univariat.kurz: Exactly one variable is looked at. Univariate analyses describe it on its own, for example with a mean, a measure of spread or a histogram.
univariat.beispiel: For 40 people only sleep duration is analysed, with no other characteristic.

unsicherheitskoeffizient.kurz: A directional association measure for two nominal characteristics based on entropy: the share of the uncertainty about Y that disappears when X is known. It lies between 0 and 1.
unsicherheitskoeffizient.beispiel: The same table as for Goodman-Kruskal tau: entropy of Y: ln 2 = 0.693. Entropy of Y given X: 0.562. U = (0.693 - 0.562)/0.693 = 0.19.
unsicherheitskoeffizient.vorsicht: Directional like tau: the values for the two directions differ. The uncertainty coefficient has nothing to do with measurement uncertainty.

unteranpassung.kurz: A model is too simple and misses the pattern in the data. It fits the training data poorly and new data equally poorly. The counterpart is overfitting.
unteranpassung.beispiel: A straight line is fitted to data that follow a curve. The residuals show a clear pattern.
unteranpassung.vorsicht: A poor fit is not always underfitting. Too much noise or missing predictors can also be the cause.

unterbrochene-zeitreihe.kurz: Has the course changed after an intervention? In an interrupted time series, the course before and after a known point in time is compared. A jump in level and a change in slope are tested.
unterbrochene-zeitreihe.beispiel: A speed limit applies from month 25. Level and trend of accident counts are compared for the 24 months before and after.
unterbrochene-zeitreihe.vorsicht: Other events at the same time cannot be separated from the measure. Without a comparison series, interpretation stays uncertain.

urnenmodell.kurz: A thought model in probability: balls that can be told apart are drawn from an urn, with or without replacement. Many random processes can be reduced to it.
urnenmodell.beispiel: An urn holds 3 red and 2 blue balls. Two are drawn without replacement. Both red: 3/5 · 2/4 = 0.3.
urnenmodell.vorsicht: With replacement the probabilities stay the same; without replacement they change with each draw.

ursachenspezifisches-hazard.kurz: With several competing events, the rate at which one particular event occurs among those who have had no event yet. Other events are treated like censoring. It answers the question about the cause, not about the actual share.
ursachenspezifisches-hazard.beispiel: Death from cancer and death from other causes compete. The cause-specific hazard for cancer treats other deaths like dropping out.
ursachenspezifisches-hazard.vorsicht: The share that actually dies of cancer by t also depends on the other hazards and is captured by the cumulative incidence.

validieren.kurz: From Latin validus: “strong, valid”. Checking whether a method, measurement or model does what it is meant to do. For measurements this concerns validity; for prediction models, testing on new data.
validieren.beispiel: A prediction model is validated on data that were not used for fitting.

van-der-waerden.titel: Van der Waerden test (normal scores test)
van-der-waerden.kurz: A rank test in which the ranks are converted into quantiles of the normal distribution before analysis. For data that are about normal, it approaches the power of the t test.
van-der-waerden.beispiel: The ranks of 20 values are converted into normal scores. Then they are compared as in an analysis of variance.
van-der-waerden.vorsicht: It is rare because Wilcoxon tests have similar properties and are better known.

var-modell.kurz: A time series model for several series at once: each series is explained by its own earlier values and the earlier values of all the other series. The order p says how many lags are included.
var-modell.beispiel: With 3 series and order 2, each equation has 3 · 2 + 1 = 7 coefficients.
var-modell.vorsicht: The number of coefficients grows quickly with series and order. Single coefficients are hard to interpret, so impulse responses and Granger tests are used.

variabilitaet.kurz: From Latin variare: “to change”. Values vary when they differ. Variability is the extent of this difference, measured as spread (standard deviation, variance, range). Without variability no relation can be computed.
variabilitaet.beispiel: If everyone scores exactly 4, there is no variability: a correlation cannot be computed.

variable.kurz: What differs between cases or points in time? A variable is a quantity that can take different values. In a data table, each variable forms a column.
variable.beispiel: Age, body height and favourite colour are three variables. Each person supplies one value for each variable.

variablenkarte.titel: Variables control chart (X-bar chart, individuals chart)
variablenkarte.kurz: A control chart for measured values. The X-bar chart (x̄-R, x̄-s) plots the mean and range or standard deviation of small samples, the individuals chart (I-MR) single values. Limits usually lie at ±3 standard deviations of the plotted quantity around the centre.
variablenkarte.beispiel: Five parts are measured every hour and their mean is plotted. A point outside the limits signals a change in the process.
variablenkarte.vorsicht: The limits describe the behaviour of the process, not the requirement on the product. The two must be kept apart.

varianz.kurz: What is the average squared deviation from the mean? For a whole population (σ²) the sum of squares is divided by N. The sample variance s² divides by n - 1 and so estimates the population variance. Its square root is the standard deviation.
varianz.beispiel: Values 2, 4, 4, 6, 9: mean 5, sum of squares 28, sample variance 28 / 4 = 7. If the five values were all the cases, σ² = 28 / 5 = 5.6.
varianz.vorsicht: The unit of the variance is the squared unit of the data (minutes²), which is why the standard deviation is usually reported. Programs by default give the sample variance with divisor n - 1.

varianz-zufallsvariable.titel: Variance of a random variable (Var(X), σ²)
varianz-zufallsvariable.kurz: The expected squared deviation from the expected value. It measures how strongly values spread around the expected value. Its square root is the standard deviation of the random variable.
varianz-zufallsvariable.vorsicht: This is the variance of the distribution. A sample variance is an estimate and is computed with n - 1.

varianzanalyse.kurz: Do several groups differ in their means by more than chance would lead one to expect? Analysis of variance (ANOVA) splits the spread of the values into a part between the groups and a part within the groups. Both are compared with the F test.
varianzanalyse.beispiel: Three teaching methods, 4 people each, means 5, 7 and 9 points: of the total spread of 38, 32 lies between the groups and 6 within them.
varianzanalyse.vorsicht: A significant result only shows that the group means are not all equal. A post hoc test or a contrast is needed to say which groups differ.

varianzhomogenitaet.kurz: Do the groups spread about equally? Homogeneity of variance means the variances of the compared groups are equal. Many methods, such as the pooled t test and classical analysis of variance, assume this.
varianzhomogenitaet.beispiel: Group A has SD 4, group B SD 12: the variances are 16 and 144. That is a ratio of 9 to 1.
varianzhomogenitaet.vorsicht: A non-significant Levene test does not prove equality. With unequal group sizes a violation has bigger consequences.

varianzkomponenten.kurz: The parts into which total variance can be divided, such as variance between groups and variance within groups. Their ratio gives the intraclass correlation coefficient.
varianzkomponenten.beispiel: Variance between schools 4, within 16: total 20, share between schools 4/20 = 0.20 (ICC).
varianzkomponenten.vorsicht: The parts are estimates with uncertainty, and they hold for the model. With additional predictors they change.

variation.kurz: A selection of k things out of n in which order matters. Without repetition there are n · (n - 1) · … · (n - k + 1) possibilities, with repetition n to the power k.
variation.beispiel: Code of 3 out of 5 letters: without repetition 5 · 4 · 3 = 60, with repetition 5³ = 125.

variational.kurz: A fast approximation method for Bayesian models: instead of exploring the posterior distribution by draws, a simple distribution is sought that comes as close to it as possible. It is optimisation instead of simulation.
variational.beispiel: With a very large dataset, MCMC takes hours. Variational inference gives approximations in minutes.
variational.vorsicht: The approximation often underestimates uncertainty. For important statements it is compared with MCMC.

variationskoeffizient.kurz: How large is the spread relative to the mean? The coefficient of variation is the standard deviation divided by the mean, often as a percentage. It compares spreads for different units or magnitudes.
variationskoeffizient.beispiel: Weight: mean 70 kg, SD 14 kg, so 0.20. Height: mean 170 cm, SD 8.5 cm, so 0.05. Weight varies more in relative terms.
variationskoeffizient.vorsicht: Only meaningful for a ratio scale with a true zero. When the mean is near 0 it becomes useless (for example temperature in °C).

varimax.kurz: The most common orthogonal rotation in factor analysis. Orthogonal means the factors stay uncorrelated, that is independent of each other. Varimax turns the solution so that each item loads high on one factor and low on the others.
varimax.beispiel: Before rotation all six items load on factor 1. After varimax, three items load on factor 1 and three on factor 2.
varimax.vorsicht: The assumption of uncorrelated factors often does not hold. If the factors are related in content, an oblique rotation fits better.

vektor.kurz: From Latin vector: “carrier”. An ordered list of numbers. The values of one person or one variable form a vector. In geometry: a quantity with length and direction.
vektor.beispiel: The values (3, 5, 4) of one person on three tasks form a vector.

venn-diagramm.kurz: A picture in which sets are drawn as overlapping circles. The overlap shows what lies in both sets. It makes rules of set theory and probability visible.
venn-diagramm.beispiel: P(A) = 0.5, P(B) = 0.3 and P(A and B) = 0.1: P(A or B) = 0.5 + 0.3 - 0.1 = 0.7. The overlap would otherwise be counted twice.
venn-diagramm.vorsicht: The areas in the picture are only a sketch and mostly not to scale with probability.

veraenderungswert.kurz: The value after treatment minus the value before. It seems simple but has lower reliability than the single measurements when they are strongly related, and it depends on the starting value.
veraenderungswert.beispiel: Before and after have spread 10 and a correlation of 0.70. The spread of the difference is √(100 + 100 - 2 · 0.7 · 100) = 7.75. With a reliability of 0.90 of the measurements, that of the difference is only (0.90 - 0.70)/(1 - 0.70) = 0.67.
veraenderungswert.vorsicht: In randomised studies, analysis of covariance with the baseline value as a covariate is often better than analysing the differences.

verallgemeinerte-kleinste-quadrate.kurz: An estimation method for linear models in which the errors may have unequal spread or correlations with each other. It uses the known error pattern to estimate more efficiently than ordinary least squares.
verallgemeinerte-kleinste-quadrate.beispiel: Measurements of the same person over time are related. GLS takes this dependence into account in the estimate.
verallgemeinerte-kleinste-quadrate.vorsicht: The error pattern must be known or well estimated. Otherwise the method is called feasible GLS (FGLS) and holds only approximately.

verblindung.kurz: Who knows who gets what? With blinding (masking), participants or assessors or both do not know the condition, so that expectations cannot influence the result.
verblindung.beispiel: Double blind: neither the participants nor the study staff who judge the effect know the assignment.

verdopplungszeit.kurz: The time a quantity needs to double at constant growth. With growth rate r per time unit, ln 2 / ln(1 + r) applies.
verdopplungszeit.beispiel: If a quantity grows by 3.5 % per year, the doubling time is ln 2 / ln 1.035 = 20.1 years. The rule of thumb 70/3.5 = 20 fits well.
verdopplungszeit.vorsicht: The calculation holds only for constant growth. Real growth seldom stays constant for long.

verhaeltnis.kurz: How large is one thing compared with another? A ratio divides one number by another, not by the whole. It is written as a : b or as a quotient.
verhaeltnis.beispiel: 12 cats and 8 dogs: 12 : 8 = 3 : 2, that is 1.5 cats per dog.
verhaeltnis.vorsicht: A ratio is not a proportion: the proportion of cats among all 20 animals is 12 / 20 = 0.60.

verhaeltnisschaetzer.kurz: An estimator that uses an auxiliary quantity whose total is known. The ratio of target to auxiliary quantity from the sample is multiplied by the known total. It is more precise when the two quantities are closely related.
verhaeltnisschaetzer.beispiel: Sample: mean turnover 12, mean number of employees 10. The total number of employees is known, 5000. Estimated total turnover: 12/10 · 5000 = 6000.
verhaeltnisschaetzer.vorsicht: It is slightly biased in small samples. With a weak relation it brings no gain.

verhaeltnisskala.kurz: Equal steps and a true zero. On a ratio scale zero means “none of it”. Ratios are therefore meaningful too: “twice as much” is a real statement.
verhaeltnisskala.beispiel: Body weight: 40 kg is twice as much as 20 kg. Duration in seconds and counts belong here as well.

verifikation.kurz: From Latin verus “true”: confirming as true. General statements cannot be finally confirmed by a finite number of observations. Statistics therefore says “supported”, not “proved”.
verifikation.beispiel: Many measurements support the hypothesis but do not prove it.

verifikationsverzerrung.kurz: In a study of a test, the reference examination is not carried out on everyone but mainly on those with abnormal results. Sensitivity and specificity are then biased.
verifikationsverzerrung.beispiel: Only those who test positive get a tissue sample. False negatives stay undetected, and the sensitivity appears too high.
verifikationsverzerrung.vorsicht: The error arises in the study, not in the test.

verlustfunktion.kurz: A rule that assigns a loss to an estimation error. Which estimate is best depends on it: with squared loss it is the mean (of the posterior distribution), with absolute loss the median.
verlustfunktion.beispiel: Two estimators are compared. Squared loss penalises an error of 10 a hundred times as much as an error of 1, absolute loss only ten times.
verlustfunktion.vorsicht: The choice of loss function is a decision. It determines which estimator counts as “good”.

verschachtelt.kurz: Does each level of one factor belong to only one level of another? In a nested design the levels of one factor are contained within the levels of another and occur only there. The factors cannot be freely crossed.
verschachtelt.beispiel: Classes within schools: every school has a class 1, but each class belongs to exactly one school.
verschachtelt.vorsicht: If the nesting is overlooked and all cases are treated as independent, the results look more certain than they are.

versuchsleitereffekt.kurz: The expectations or behaviour of those running the study unconsciously influence the results.
versuchsleitereffekt.beispiel: Experimenters who believe group A will do better unconsciously give it more time or friendlier feedback.
versuchsleitereffekt.vorsicht: Remedies are blinding and fixed, written instructions.

verteilungsform.kurz: What shape does the distribution have? The distribution shape describes how the values are spread: number of peaks, symmetric or skewed, light or heavy tails.
verteilungsform.beispiel: Waiting times: one peak at a few minutes, long tail on the right, so single-peaked and right-skewed.
verteilungsform.vorsicht: The shape decides which summary fits. With skewed distributions, median and IQR often serve better than mean and standard deviation.

verteilungsfrei.kurz: A procedure is distribution-free if it does not assume a particular shape of the distribution (for example the normal distribution). Such procedures often work with ranks. They are also called nonparametric.
verteilungsfrei.beispiel: Two small groups with strongly skewed values: the Mann-Whitney U test compares ranks and needs no normal distribution.
verteilungsfrei.vorsicht: Distribution-free procedures also have assumptions, such as independent observations. They are not assumption-free.

verteilungsfunktion.kurz: It states how likely it is that a random variable takes at most the value x. It rises from 0 to 1 and never falls. Range probabilities and quantiles can be read from it.

verteilungstafel.kurz: A table that gives the probability for values of a distribution, or the value for a probability. In the past the critical value was read from it. Today programs calculate the values directly.
verteilungstafel.beispiel: In a t table, the row for 9 degrees of freedom and the column 0.975 hold the value 2.262.
verteilungstafel.vorsicht: Tables differ in whether they give the area to the left, to the right or two-sided. Check the heading before reading.

vertrauensniveau.kurz: How reliable is the procedure that produces the interval? The confidence level, often 95%, states the share of many repetitions in which the calculated intervals contain the true value.
vertrauensniveau.beispiel: Mean 68, standard error 2 (normal approximation): 95% gives 64.1 to 71.9. 99% gives the wider interval 62.8 to 73.2.
vertrauensniveau.vorsicht: It says nothing about the single interval and not about the probability that the true value lies inside. 95% is only a habit.

vgl.kurz: “cf.” stands for the Latin “confer”: “compare”. The reference names a source or place that supports or adds to the point, without being quoted word for word.
vgl.beispiel: The spread is larger in group B (cf. Table 2).

vice-versa.kurz: Latin for “the position being reversed”. And the other way round. For a correlation the relation is symmetric; the direction of a possible cause does not follow from it.
vice-versa.beispiel: Those who practise more have higher scores, and vice versa; the correlation does not say which causes which.

vierfeldertafel.kurz: A table with two characteristics that each have two values. It shows the counts (or probabilities) of all four combinations with totals. Conditional probabilities can be read from it easily.
vierfeldertafel.beispiel: Suppose 2000 people: 20 ill (18 of them tested positive), 1980 healthy (99 of them positive). Of 117 positives, 18 are ill, so 0.154.

vif.kurz: How much does the relatedness of predictors inflate the uncertainty of a coefficient? The VIF states by what factor its variance is larger than with unrelated predictors. VIF = 1 / (1 - R²ⱼ), where R²ⱼ comes from predicting this predictor from the others.
vif.beispiel: Practice tasks and study hours: r = 0.9358, VIF = 1 / (1 - 0.9358²) = 8.05.
vif.vorsicht: Commonly quoted cut-offs (5 or 10) are habits, not rules.

violinplot.kurz: What shape does the distribution have in each group? A violin plot draws, for each group, a density curve mirrored at the centre, often with a small box plot inside. It also shows two peaks that a box plot hides.
violinplot.beispiel: Reaction times of three groups: where the violin is wide, many values lie; two bulges one above the other point to two peaks.
violinplot.vorsicht: The shape depends on the smoothing. With very few cases it is misleading, and the curve can extend beyond the values that actually occur.

visuelle-analyse.kurz: The judgement of single-case data from the plotted curve, not with test statistics alone. What is looked at are level, trend and variability within phases, overlap between phases, immediacy of change and consistency between similar phases.
visuelle-analyse.beispiel: In the B phase all values lie above the highest value of the A phase, and the change begins at once. This supports a clear effect.
visuelle-analyse.vorsicht: Judgements by different people do not always agree. Measures such as NAP, PND or Tau-U are added.

vollerhebung.kurz: Is the whole group recorded instead of a part? In a complete enumeration (census), every element of the population is recorded. There is then no sampling error.
vollerhebung.beispiel: All 120 employees of a firm fill in the questionnaire: the mean applies exactly to these 120.
vollerhebung.vorsicht: Nonresponse and measurement error remain. If the results are meant to hold beyond this group, it is a sample again.

vorhersagewert-regression.kurz: What does the model predict for a case? The predicted value ŷ (y hat) is the value of the regression equation for that case's predictor values. It estimates the mean of cases with these predictor values, not a certain single value.
vorhersagewert-regression.beispiel: At 5 study hours ŷ = 64.7. The person with 5 hours scored 66 points, so the residual is 1.3.

vorzeichentest.kurz: Are there more improvements than deteriorations? The sign test only counts in which direction each pair changed, not by how much. If both directions are equally likely, the number of plus signs follows a binomial distribution with p = 0.5.
vorzeichentest.beispiel: 10 people with a change: 8 better, 2 worse. Two-sided exact p value 0.109.
vorzeichentest.vorsicht: Pairs without change are dropped. Because the size of the differences is ignored, the test usually has less power than the Wilcoxon signed-rank test.

vs.kurz: Abbreviation of the Latin “versus”: “against”. It sets two groups or conditions side by side, such as “training vs. control”. It says nothing about direction or outcome of the comparison.
vs.beispiel: The study compares training vs. waiting list.

wachstumsmodell.kurz: How does something change over time, and how differently does it run for different individuals? The growth model describes for each person an own trajectory with a starting value and a slope. Links of these trajectories to other variables can be tested too.
wachstumsmodell.beispiel: Height of a child: 100 cm at age 4, +6 cm per year. At age 7 the model gives 100 + 6 · 3 = 118 cm.
wachstumsmodell.vorsicht: A straight course is an assumption. With only two time points, a curved course cannot be tested.

wachstumsrate.kurz: By what percentage has something grown? The growth rate is the change of a value in relation to the earlier value. Over several periods there is the average rate per period.
wachstumsrate.beispiel: From 200 to 230: growth 30 / 200 = 15%. From 100 to 121 in two years: 10% per year, because 1.1 · 1.1 = 1.21.
wachstumsrate.vorsicht: Growth rates are not simply averaged, they compound. Growth by 10% followed by a fall of 10% does not return to the starting value.

wahrer-wert.kurz: In classical test theory, the value a person would get on average if the same measurement were repeated endlessly under equal conditions. It is an imagined quantity and cannot be observed.
wahrer-wert.beispiel: A person scores 52, 48 and 50 on a test. The mean, 50, serves as an estimate of the true score.
wahrer-wert.vorsicht: “True” does not mean the value captures what is meant. Even a biased test has a true score of its own.

wahrscheinlichkeit.kurz: How certain is it that something happens? A probability is a number from 0 to 1. 0 means impossible, 1 means certain. The larger the number, the more likely the event.
wahrscheinlichkeit.beispiel: A fair die shows a number above 4 (that is 5 or 6) with probability 2/6 = 0.333.
wahrscheinlichkeit.vorsicht: A probability says nothing sure about a single throw. It describes what to expect in the long run.

wahrscheinlichkeitsfunktion.kurz: For a random variable with separate, countable values it states how likely each value is. All values together add up to 1. For continuous variables the density function takes its place.
wahrscheinlichkeitsfunktion.beispiel: Number of heads in 3 tosses: 0 → 0.125; 1 → 0.375; 2 → 0.375; 3 → 0.125. Sum 1.

wahrscheinlichkeitsverteilung.kurz: Which values can occur, and how likely is each one? A probability distribution assigns a probability to every possible value (or range of values). All probabilities together add up to 1.
wahrscheinlichkeitsverteilung.beispiel: Sum of two dice: a 7 has 6 of 36 possible outcomes, so 0.167. All eleven sums together add up to 1.
wahrscheinlichkeitsverteilung.vorsicht: A distribution describes what chance leads one to expect. It is not the same as the frequencies seen in a sample.

waic-dic.titel: WAIC and DIC (information criteria for Bayesian models)
waic-dic.kurz: Measures for comparing Bayesian models, similar to the AIC. Both describe the fit to the data minus a penalty for complexity. On the usual deviance scale the model with the smaller value is preferred.
waic-dic.beispiel: Model A has WAIC 312, model B 305. B is preferred. A difference of 7 has to be judged against its standard error.
waic-dic.vorsicht: A small difference is no proof. The leave-one-out (LOO) comparison is now usually regarded as more reliable than DIC.

wald-intervall.kurz: How can an interval for a proportion be calculated quickly? The Wald interval takes the sample proportion p̂ and adds and subtracts z · √(p̂ (1 - p̂) / n). It is simple but inaccurate when n is small.
wald-intervall.beispiel: 18 of 40: p̂ = 0.45, standard error 0.0787, interval 0.296 to 0.604. For 0 of 20 the result is 0 to 0.
wald-intervall.vorsicht: With small n and proportions near 0 or 1, coverage is often clearly too low. Then Wilson or Clopper-Pearson is better.

wald-test.kurz: Does a single coefficient differ from 0? The Wald test divides the coefficient by its standard error. Under the null hypothesis the quotient is approximately standard normal (Wald z), its square approximately χ² with 1 degree of freedom.
wald-test.beispiel: b = 0.50, standard error 0.20: z = 2.5, two-sided p = 0.012.
wald-test.vorsicht: With very large coefficients or small samples it is unreliable. The likelihood ratio test is then often more reliable.

ward.kurz: A method of hierarchical cluster analysis. In each step the two clusters are merged for which the spread within clusters grows the least. It usually forms compact clusters of similar size.
ward.beispiel: Two groups of cases with nearby centres hardly grow when merged. Ward merges them first.
ward.vorsicht: It assumes metric variables and, in principle, squared Euclidean distances. Outliers can influence the result strongly.

weibull.kurz: A distribution for lifetimes and times until failure. The shape parameter tells how the risk changes over time: below 1 it falls, at 1 it stays constant (exponential distribution), above 1 it rises.
weibull.beispiel: Shape 2, scale 1000 hours: by 500 hours 22.1% of the devices have failed (1 - e^-0.25). The risk rises with age.

welch-test.kurz: How are two means compared when the groups spread differently? The Welch test is a t test without the assumption of equal variances. It corrects the degrees of freedom for this, which then are often not whole numbers.
welch-test.beispiel: A: mean 11.5, SD 1.05; B: mean 18.67, SD 8.38; 6 people each: Welch t = -2.08, 5.16 degrees of freedom, p = 0.091. With pooled variance, p would be 0.064.
welch-test.vorsicht: Welch is often recommended as the default, because it loses little when variances are equal. It does not fix skewed distributions in very small groups.

wertelabel.kurz: A text attached to a code. Instead of just “2”, the table then shows “partly”. The label does not change the stored value; it only changes what is displayed.
wertelabel.beispiel: 1 = “disagree”, 2 = “partly”, 3 = “agree”. The frequency table shows the texts.
wertelabel.statable: On the page “Columns”: copy the value labels (group names) of a column to other columns, for example the same answer scale for many questions.

white-test.kurz: A test for unequal spread of the errors that does not presuppose a particular form of the inequality. The squared residuals are regressed on the predictors, their squares and products. The statistic is n · R² of this auxiliary regression.
white-test.beispiel: n = 100, simple regression: auxiliary regression on x and x² with R² = 0.08. LM = 100 · 0.08 = 8 with 2 degrees of freedom, p = 0.018.
white-test.vorsicht: The test also picks up other model errors, not just unequal spread, so a significant result is ambiguous.

wiederkehrende-ereignisse.kurz: An event can occur several times in the same person, such as hospital stays or infections. The times of the same person are not independent, and the analysis must take this into account.
wiederkehrende-ereignisse.beispiel: Among 100 people there are 140 hospital stays, none for some and several for others. A simple count of persons with an event loses this information.
wiederkehrende-ereignisse.vorsicht: Several models exist (Andersen-Gill, Prentice-Williams-Peterson, frailty). The choice depends on how the events are related.

wilcoxon-rangsumme.kurz: The same question as the Mann-Whitney test, with a different statistic: W is the sum of the ranks in one of the two groups. Both tests give the same p value. For that group, U = W - n(n + 1)/2.
wilcoxon-rangsumme.beispiel: The same 13 values: group A (n = 6) has rank sum 25, group B 66. Then U = 25 - 21 = 4.
wilcoxon-rangsumme.vorsicht: Not to be confused with the Wilcoxon signed-rank test for paired measurements. Here the groups are independent.

wilcoxon-vorzeichen.kurz: Has something changed in the same people when the direction and rough size of the differences matter, not the exact values? The test orders the differences by size, assigns ranks and adds up the ranks of the positive differences (V).
wilcoxon-vorzeichen.beispiel: 8 pairs, differences 3; -1; 4; 2; -2.5; 5; 6; 1.5: the positive ranks give V = 31, the negative ones 5; exact p value 0.078.
wilcoxon-vorzeichen.vorsicht: Differences of 0 are dropped. The test assumes that the differences lie roughly symmetrically around their centre.

wilks-lambda.kurz: How much spread is left once the groups are taken into account? Wilks' lambda is a test statistic of MANOVA between 0 and 1. Small values mean the groups separate the measures well.
wilks-lambda.beispiel: In the example Λ = 0.074. The share that goes to the groups is 1 - 0.074 = 0.926.
wilks-lambda.vorsicht: Unlike a share of explained variance, small means good here. With only two groups, Λ and Pillai's trace are equivalent (Pillai = 1 - Λ).

wilson-intervall.kurz: Which range is plausible for a proportion? The Wilson interval is a confidence interval for a proportion. It keeps its level better than the Wald interval for small samples and for proportions near 0 or 1.
wilson-intervall.beispiel: 18 of 40: Wilson 0.307 to 0.602. 0 of 20: Wilson 0 to 0.161, while Wald gives 0 to 0 here.
wilson-intervall.vorsicht: The limits are not symmetric around the sample proportion. That is intended.

winsorisieren.kurz: What to do with extreme values without deleting them? In winsorizing the outermost values are replaced by the next value inside. The number of cases stays the same.
winsorisieren.beispiel: Waiting times 3, 4, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9, 10, 40: the 3 becomes 4, the 40 becomes 10. The mean falls from 9.6 to 6.7.
winsorisieren.vorsicht: This changes the data and must be documented. It weakens the influence of an extreme value but does not repair a measurement error.
winsorisieren.statable: Under “Edit data” the assistant “Winsorize”: new column, the original column stays. Limits as percentiles (default 20% and 80%); the step appears in the log.

wirksamkeit-effektivitaet.kurz: Efficacy is the effect under strictly controlled conditions. Effectiveness is the effect in everyday practice, with a mixed group of participants and incomplete adherence.
wirksamkeit-effektivitaet.beispiel: A programme clearly works in a study with carefully selected participants (efficacy). In everyday school use, the effect is smaller (effectiveness).
wirksamkeit-effektivitaet.vorsicht: The two German words are not used consistently. In English the terms are kept apart.

wirkungsflaeche.kurz: A method of experimental design. It describes the relation between several settings and one outcome as a surface, usually a quadratic equation, to find the best setting.
wirkungsflaeche.beispiel: Temperature and baking time are varied in a few runs. The highest point of the fitted surface shows the best combination.
wirkungsflaeche.vorsicht: The surface holds only within the range studied.

within-subjects.kurz: The same people, several conditions: each person experiences all conditions or is measured several times. Measurements of the same person are compared.
within-subjects.beispiel: Reaction time of the same 25 people with and without distraction.
within-subjects.vorsicht: Order can have an effect (practice, fatigue). It is therefore often alternated or set at random (counterbalancing).

wlsmv.kurz: Estimation methods for factor and structural equation models when the items are ordinal (such as Likert answers). They work with polychoric correlations instead of ordinary ones and suit few response options better than maximum likelihood.
wlsmv.beispiel: Items with four response options are treated as ordinal with WLSMV. The loadings then refer to the underlying continuous quantity.
wlsmv.vorsicht: The results (such as loadings) are not directly comparable with those from maximum likelihood. The method needs more cases.

wurzeltransformation.kurz: The square root is taken of each value. It dampens large values, reduces right skew and stabilises the spread for count data whose variance grows with the mean.
wurzeltransformation.vorsicht: With zeros, √(x + 0.5) is often used. Today count data are usually analysed with Poisson regression instead of transformed values.

yates.kurz: Does the chi-square test become significant too often in a 2x2 table? The Yates correction subtracts 0.5 from each deviation before squaring it. This allows for the fact that frequencies are whole numbers and makes the test more cautious.
yates.beispiel: Table 18, 12 / 9, 21: χ² = 5.45 (p = 0.020) without and 4.31 (p = 0.038) with the correction. Fisher's exact test gives p = 0.037.
yates.vorsicht: It applies only to 2x2 tables and is also criticised as too strict. Fisher's exact test is an alternative.

youden.kurz: Which cutoff is a good compromise? The Youden index is J = sensitivity + specificity - 1. The cutoff with the largest J counts as a compromise that weighs both kinds of error equally.
youden.beispiel: Cutoff A: sensitivity 0.90, specificity 0.70, J = 0.60. Cutoff B: 0.80 and 0.85, J = 0.65. B is chosen.
youden.vorsicht: The index treats false alarms and misses as equal. If their consequences differ in weight, another cutoff is better.

yule-q.kurz: Association measures for a four-fold table, derived from the odds ratio. Q = (ad - bc)/(ad + bc), Y = (√(ad) - √(bc))/(√(ad) + √(bc)). Both lie between -1 and 1.
yule-q.vorsicht: Q becomes ±1 as soon as one cell is empty, even if the relation is otherwise weak. Y is more reserved.

z-test.kurz: Does a mean differ from a target when the true spread is known? The z test divides the deviation by the known standard error σ / √n and compares it with the standard normal distribution. It also serves as an approximation with very large samples.
z-test.beispiel: Target 500 ml, known spread of the filling machine σ = 2 ml, 25 bottles with mean 500.9: z = 0.9 / 0.4 = 2.25, p = 0.024.
z-test.vorsicht: The spread is rarely truly known. If it is estimated from the data, the t test is the right one.

z-wert.kurz: How far is a value above or below the mean, measured in standard deviations? The z-score is (value minus mean) divided by the standard deviation. 0 means exactly the mean.
z-wert.beispiel: A test with mean 50 and SD 8: 62 points give z = 1.5, 44 points give z = -0.75.
z-wert.vorsicht: The z-score describes position within a group. Percentages attached to it (z = 1 corresponds to about percentile rank 84) hold only for roughly normally distributed values.

zaehlprozess.kurz: A representation of survival data in which each person is split into one or more rows with start, stop and event indicator. This allows for time-dependent covariates, recurrent events and late entry (left truncation).
zaehlprozess.beispiel: A person is recorded as untreated from month 0 to 8 and as treated from 8 to 20, then censored. Two rows: (0, 8], (8, 20].
zaehlprozess.vorsicht: Intervals must not overlap. Errors in the format lead to wrong results.

zeichen-alpha.kurz: Pronounced: alpha. Most often the significance level, the cutoff for the p value (commonly 0.05; probability of a type I error); 1 - α is the confidence level. Also: Cronbach's α (reliability), Krippendorff's α (agreement), intercept, smoothing factor, shape parameter of gamma and beta distributions.
zeichen-alpha.beispiel: With α = 0.05, a result with p = 0.03 counts as significant, one with p = 0.08 does not.
zeichen-alpha.vorsicht: The significance level and Cronbach's α are unrelated. The researcher sets the significance level beforehand, Cronbach's α is computed from the data.

zeichen-apa.kurz: Rules of the American Psychological Association for statistics in text. Symbols such as M, SD, p, t, F, r, N are italic. Degrees of freedom go in brackets. Quantities capped at 1 (p, r) have no leading zero. Tiny p becomes p < .001.
zeichen-apa.vorsicht: Other fields and journals write differently, for example with a zero before the decimal point. The instruction of the journal or institute counts.

zeichen-b.kurz: Small b is the unstandardized regression coefficient: by how many units y differs on average when x is 1 larger (other predictors equal). Programs often print it as B. b₀ is the constant. B is also the number of bootstrap repetitions.
zeichen-b.beispiel: b = 2.5 for study hours: per additional hour the score is on average 2.5 higher.
zeichen-b.vorsicht: b and β differ. b depends on the unit of x, β does not.

zeichen-bedingt.kurz: Pronounced: P of A given B. The probability of A when B has already occurred. The vertical bar means “given”. P(A | B) and P(B | A) are usually different.
zeichen-bedingt.beispiel: 200 people, 40 with B, of these 30 with A: P(A | B) = 30 / 40 = 0.75.
zeichen-bedingt.vorsicht: The p value is P(data at least as striking as observed | H₀), not P(H₀ | data). Mixing up these directions is a common error.

zeichen-beta.kurz: Pronounced: beta (BAY-tuh or BEE-tuh). Probability of a type II error, missing an effect that exists (power = 1 - β); standardized regression coefficient (beta weight); true coefficient of the population in the regression equation, β̂ estimated. Also shape parameter of the beta distribution.
zeichen-beta.vorsicht: The standardized β and the unstandardized b (B) are different numbers. β allows only a rough comparison of predictors in different units, because it depends on the spread in the sample.

zeichen-betrag.kurz: Pronounced: absolute value of x. The distance from 0, without sign: |-3| = 3. For correlations |r| shows strength regardless of direction. In matrix notation |S| can mean the determinant.
zeichen-betrag.beispiel: Deviations -2, 0, 2: absolute values 2, 0, 2; mean absolute deviation 4 / 3 ≈ 1.33.
zeichen-betrag.vorsicht: The vertical bar has two meanings: |x| is an absolute value, P(A | B) a condition.

zeichen-chi.kurz: Pronounced: chi, like ky in sky. Almost only as χ²: sum of squared standard normal values (χ² distribution) and statistic of χ² tests (independence, fit, homogeneity), likelihood ratio, Wald, Friedman, McNemar tests. CFA's model test is χ² too. χ is not a Latin x.
zeichen-chi.beispiel: χ²(2) = 6.0: test statistic with 2 degrees of freedom.
zeichen-chi.vorsicht: Writing χ² as “x²” is understood as the same thing. The symbol χ² never stands for the square of a variable x.

zeichen-ci.kurz: CI stands for confidence interval: the range around an estimate that shows uncertainty. The notation 95 % CI [a, b] gives lower and upper limit. In the Bayesian approach the range is called a credible interval (CrI).
zeichen-ci.vorsicht: The 95 % refers to the procedure over many repetitions. It does not mean the true value lies in this one range with 95 % probability.

zeichen-d.kurz: Cohen's d: mean difference in standard deviations. Also d in the Durbin-Watson test (0 to 4, near 2 means no autocorrelation), D in the Kolmogorov-Smirnov test (largest distance), Cook's D (influence of a case), d̄ (mean paired difference), Somers' d, d in ARIMA (differencing steps).
zeichen-d.beispiel: Durbin-Watson d = 2.0: no first-order autocorrelation expected.
zeichen-d.vorsicht: d and D are not interchangeable. The name of the procedure before it decides.

zeichen-dach.kurz: Pronounced: hat. A hat over a symbol means: estimated from the data. β̂ estimates β, σ̂ estimates σ, θ̂ estimates θ, ŷ is a predicted value.
zeichen-dach.beispiel: β = value of the population (unknown), β̂ = estimate from the sample.
zeichen-dach.vorsicht: The hat does not turn a number into a fixed value. An estimate varies from sample to sample.

zeichen-delta.kurz: Pronounced: delta. Δ: change or difference, for example ΔR² (increase in R²), Glass's Δ (effect size), Δy (difference of successive time-series values). δ: true difference in the population, equivalence margin, in survival analysis often the event indicator (1 event, 0 censored).
zeichen-delta.beispiel: If R² rises from 0.30 to 0.38, ΔR² = 0.08.
zeichen-delta.vorsicht: Δ is not always a difference of means. The context shows whether it is the difference, an increase or an effect size.

zeichen-df.kurz: df stands for degrees of freedom. It counts how many values can vary freely once estimates are fixed. It appears in brackets after t, F and χ²: t(24), F(2, 27), χ²(3).
zeichen-df.beispiel: One-sample t test with n = 25: df = n - 1 = 24.
zeichen-df.vorsicht: In the Welch test and corrections such as Greenhouse-Geisser, df is not a whole number, for example 17.3.

zeichen-e.kurz: Pronounced: e, Euler's number. e is about 2.71828. exp(x) means e to the power x and is the inverse of ln. In logistic regression exp(b) is the odds ratio. A small e can also mean the residual.
zeichen-e.beispiel: Logit coefficient b = 0.693: exp(b) ≈ 2.0, the odds double per unit of the predictor.
zeichen-e.vorsicht: The capital E in 1.2E-05 is not Euler's number but ten to the power: 1.2 · 10⁻⁵.

zeichen-e-notation.kurz: Very small or very large numbers in output. 1.2E-05 means 1.2 times 10 to the power -5, that is 0.000012. 3.4E+06 is 3,400,000. The E stands for exponent, not for Euler's number.
zeichen-e-notation.vorsicht: The minus after the E moves the decimal point left: it is a very small number, not a negative one.

zeichen-epsilon.kurz: Pronounced: epsilon. Error term of a model: the part of y it does not cover (estimated: the residual); in time series white noise, in measurement models measurement error. Correction ε for repeated measures (Greenhouse-Geisser): 1 means sphericity holds, smaller means violated. ε² as effect size.
zeichen-epsilon.beispiel: ε = 0.70 reduces the degrees of freedom to 70 % of their value.
zeichen-epsilon.vorsicht: The error term ε is unknown, the residual is its estimate from the data. They are not the same.

zeichen-erwartung.kurz: Pronounced: expected value of X, variance of X, covariance. E(X) is the value X takes on average over very many repetitions, equal to μ. Var(X) equals σ². Cov(X, Y) measures how X and Y vary together.
zeichen-erwartung.vorsicht: E(X) is an average over many repetitions. 3.5 does not occur in a single throw.

zeichen-eta.kurz: Pronounced: eta (AY-tuh or EE-tuh). η² is an effect size of analysis of variance: the share of total variation going with group differences (also partial, generalized). Correlation ratio η. Also the linear predictor in generalized linear models, a latent variable in structural equation models.
zeichen-eta.beispiel: η² = 0.14: 14 % of the total variation goes with the group differences.
zeichen-eta.vorsicht: Like every effect size, η² shows an association, not proof of an effect. Partial and ordinary η² differ as soon as the model has several factors.

zeichen-f.kurz: The test statistic of analysis of variance and of the overall test in regression: a ratio of two variances (mean squares). F is never negative. It has two degrees of freedom, numerator and denominator: F(2, 27).
zeichen-f.beispiel: Mean square between groups 12, within groups 4: F = 3.
zeichen-f.vorsicht: Small f is usually Cohen's f or a density; F(x) without degrees of freedom is often a distribution function.

zeichen-fakultaet.kurz: Pronounced: n factorial. n! = n · (n - 1) · … · 1, the number of orders of n different things. By definition 0! = 1. The exclamation mark is a mathematical sign here.
zeichen-fakultaet.beispiel: 5! = 5 · 4 · 3 · 2 · 1 = 120 orders for 5 people in a queue.

zeichen-g.kurz: Hedges' g is an effect size for the difference of two means, like Cohen's d, but corrected for small samples. With large samples g and d are practically equal. In some books g₁ is the sample skewness.
zeichen-g.beispiel: d = 0.50 with 10 cases in each group: g ≈ 0.48.
zeichen-g.vorsicht: The letter g does not always mean Hedges. Without a name before it, it is unclear which quantity is meant.

zeichen-gamma.kurz: Pronounced: gamma. Goodman-Kruskal gamma measures the association of two ordered variables in a cross table. γ₁ and γ₂: in some books skewness and excess kurtosis. γ: fixed effects in multilevel models. Γ: gamma function, gamma distribution, coefficient matrix in structural equation models.
zeichen-gamma.beispiel: Gamma = 0.60 between study-time level and test level: of all pairs without a tie, 80 % are ordered the same way and 20 % oppositely, 0.80 - 0.20 = 0.60.
zeichen-gamma.vorsicht: Gamma uses only the order, not the distances, and leaves out tied pairs. The context shows whether a program means the Goodman-Kruskal gamma or skewness.

zeichen-griechisch.kurz: Statistics often names quantities with Greek letters. They usually stand for values of the population, Latin letters for values of the sample: μ for the population mean, x̄ for the sample mean. Many letters have more than one meaning.
zeichen-griechisch.beispiel: σ is the standard deviation of the population, s that of the sample.
zeichen-griechisch.vorsicht: The same symbol means different things in different procedures. What counts is the explanation given with the result.

zeichen-h0.kurz: Pronounced: H zero or H naught, and H one. H₀ is the null hypothesis, usually “no difference, no association”. H₁ (or Hₐ) is the alternative hypothesis. A test checks whether the data fit H₀.
zeichen-h0.beispiel: H₀: μ₁ = μ₂ (equal means in both populations). H₁: μ₁ ≠ μ₂.
zeichen-h0.vorsicht: If a test fits H₀, H₀ is not proven. There is just no evidence against it.

zeichen-index.kurz: A small number or letter below a symbol. xᵢ is the i-th value, x₃ the third; μ₁ and μ₂ are the means of groups 1 and 2; n₁ the size of group 1. In xᵢⱼ one index counts the groups, the other the persons.
zeichen-index.beispiel: x₁ = 4, x₂ = 6, x₃ = 8: the third value is x₃ = 8.
zeichen-index.vorsicht: x₂ is the second value, x² the square. Which index in xᵢⱼ counts the groups depends on the book.

zeichen-iqr-quartile.kurz: Q₁ is the first quartile: a quarter of the values lie below it. Q₂ is the median, Q₃ the third quartile: three quarters lie below it. IQR = Q₃ - Q₁ is the interquartile range, the width of the middle half of the data.
zeichen-iqr-quartile.beispiel: Q₁ = 12, Q₃ = 20: IQR = 8. Outlier fences by the 1.5 IQR rule: 12 - 12 = 0 and 20 + 12 = 32.
zeichen-iqr-quartile.vorsicht: Programs compute quartiles with slightly different methods, small differences are possible.

zeichen-k.kurz: Usually a count: the number of groups (analysis of variance, Kruskal-Wallis), of predictors (regression), of items of a scale (Cronbach's α), of clusters (k-means) or of studies (meta-analysis). In autocorrelation the lag.
zeichen-k.beispiel: Four groups: k = 4, the numerator degrees of freedom of the analysis of variance are k - 1 = 3.
zeichen-k.vorsicht: What is counted depends on the procedure. Kappa (κ) and the number k are also different.

zeichen-kappa.kurz: Pronounced: kappa. Cohen's κ measures how far two raters agree beyond chance: 1 means full agreement, 0 as much as chance gives. Fleiss' κ covers more than two raters, weighted κ ordered categories. κ also stands for the condition number in collinearity.
zeichen-kappa.beispiel: Two raters agree in 85 % of cases, by chance it would be 50 %: κ = (0.85 - 0.50) / (1 - 0.50) = 0.70.
zeichen-kappa.vorsicht: High percent agreement does not automatically give a high κ if one category covers almost all cases.

zeichen-lambda.kurz: Pronounced: lambda. Mean (rate) of the Poisson distribution, rate of the exponential distribution, hazard rate; Wilks' Λ in MANOVA; Goodman-Kruskal lambda (nominal cross tables); penalty strength in ridge and lasso; factor loading; eigenvalue; noncentrality parameter; exponent of the Box-Cox transformation.
zeichen-lambda.beispiel: Poisson with λ = 3: on average 3 events per time period, the variance is also 3.
zeichen-lambda.vorsicht: The same symbol means something different in every procedure. The procedure shows which meaning applies.

zeichen-ln.kurz: Pronounced: ln, natural logarithm; log, logarithm. ln has base e. For log the base depends on the program: calculators and Excel usually take 10, R takes e.
zeichen-ln.vorsicht: With a logarithm check the base first. The base changes the number, not the order of the values.

zeichen-m.kurz: M is the mean, Mdn the median, Mo the mode. They are italic, usually with SD: M = 5.2, SD = 1.1.
zeichen-m.vorsicht: M and μ differ: M belongs to the sample, μ to the population. In skewed distributions M and Mdn differ strongly.

zeichen-mengen.kurz: Pronounced: element of, union, intersection, empty set. ∪ means “A or B”, ∩ means “A and B”. Aᶜ or Ā is the complement: everything except A. {…} collects elements.
zeichen-mengen.vorsicht: ∩ and ∪ are not the letters u or n. P(A ∪ B) is not P(A) + P(B) when A and B overlap.

zeichen-mu.kurz: Pronounced: mu, like mew. The mean of the population, equal to the expected value. μ₀ is the null hypothesis mean, μ₁ and μ₂ the group means. With a link function μ is the predicted mean. As a prefix (µ) it means micro, one millionth.
zeichen-mu.beispiel: H₀: μ = 100 says the mean of the population is 100.
zeichen-mu.vorsicht: μ is a fixed but unknown value of the population. The sample mean x̄ only estimates it.

zeichen-n.kurz: Small n is the number of cases in a sample or group, capital N usually the total number of cases. For groups: n₁, n₂. In the binomial distribution n is the number of trials. Some books call the size of the population N.
zeichen-n.beispiel: Three groups of 20 people each: n = 20 per group, N = 60.
zeichen-n.vorsicht: Whether N means the sample or the population depends on the book. The result or its legend says which.

zeichen-normal-schreibweise.kurz: Pronounced: normal with mu and sigma squared. Shorthand for the normal distribution with mean μ and variance σ². N(0, 1) is the standard normal distribution.
zeichen-normal-schreibweise.vorsicht: Some books and programs write N(μ, σ) with the standard deviation instead of the variance. Never read the second number without a hint.

zeichen-ns.kurz: Abbreviation for not significant (German n. s., nicht signifikant): p lies above the chosen limit α. The test then gives no sufficient evidence of an effect.
zeichen-ns.vorsicht: n. s. does not mean “no effect” or “equal”. With a small sample often only power is missing. An equivalence test is needed to show equality.

zeichen-nu.kurz: Pronounced: nu, like new. In some books and programs the degrees of freedom (df), for example t(ν) or F(ν₁, ν₂). In structural equation models the intercepts of the measurement equations (measurement invariance). ν looks like a Latin v but is a separate symbol.
zeichen-nu.beispiel: Student's t with ν = 9: the same distribution as t with df = 9.
zeichen-nu.vorsicht: ν is not a frequency and not a mean, even though it looks like a v.

zeichen-omega.kurz: Pronounced: omega (oh-MAY-guh). ω²: effect size of analysis of variance. McDonald's ω: reliability of a scale. Cohen's ω (also w): effect size of χ² tests. Ω: sample space, ω one outcome; Ω also an error covariance matrix. In time series ω is frequency.
zeichen-omega.beispiel: ω² = 0.08 for a group factor lies between the commonly named benchmarks 0.06 (medium) and 0.14 (large).
zeichen-omega.vorsicht: ω² and ω differ: one measures an effect, the other reliability. Ω is never a measured value.

zeichen-or-rr.kurz: OR is the odds ratio, RR the relative risk (risk ratio), HR the hazard ratio. For all of them 1 means: no difference between the groups. Above 1 means higher in the group in the numerator (usually the first), below 1 lower.
zeichen-or-rr.vorsicht: OR and RR are similar only for rare events. An OR must not be read as an RR.

zeichen-p.kurz: Pronounced: p. Most often the p value: how striking are data at least as striking as those observed if the null hypothesis and the model assumptions hold? Also: the probability of an event (binomial distribution), the number of predictors, the order of an AR model.
zeichen-p.beispiel: p = 0.03: under H₀ such striking data would be expected in 3 % of cases.
zeichen-p.vorsicht: p is not the probability that the null hypothesis is true, and not a measure of the size of an effect. The Greek ρ is a different symbol.

zeichen-p-dach.kurz: Pronounced: p hat. The proportion in the sample. The hat shows: estimated. p̂ estimates the true proportion p or π of the population.
zeichen-p-dach.beispiel: 18 of 60 people have the trait: p̂ = 18 / 60 = 0.30.
zeichen-p-dach.vorsicht: p̂ varies from sample to sample. The number p̂ is not the true proportion.

zeichen-phi.kurz: Pronounced: phi, fie or fee. φ: phi coefficient, the correlation of two yes-no variables in a 2 by 2 table. φ(z) and Φ(z): density and distribution function of the standard normal (Φ⁻¹ in probit). φ also: autoregressive coefficient in ARIMA, dispersion in generalized linear models.
zeichen-phi.beispiel: Φ(1.96) = 0.975: 97.5 % of the standard normal distribution lies below z = 1.96.
zeichen-phi.vorsicht: Phi as a correlation and Φ as a distribution function are different. The form with z in brackets points to the distribution.

zeichen-pi.kurz: Pronounced: pi, like pie. The circle constant 3.14159…, found in the normal distribution's formula. Often the proportion or probability in the population (p̂ estimates it), also class proportions in mixture models, selection probability in surveys. Scott's π: agreement of two coders. Π: product sign.
zeichen-pi.beispiel: π = 0.25: in the population every fourth person has the trait.
zeichen-pi.vorsicht: π as a proportion and π as the circle constant are different. Next to proportions, tests and the binomial distribution it almost always means the proportion.

zeichen-plusminus.kurz: Pronounced: plus or minus. After the sign comes a spread around the value before it: 4.2 ± 1.1. It can be a standard deviation, a standard error or the half-width of a confidence interval.
zeichen-plusminus.beispiel: Mean 4.2 ± 1.1 (SD): values typically deviate by about 1.1 from the mean.
zeichen-plusminus.vorsicht: The sign does not say what the spread is. The legend or text must name it.

zeichen-proportional.kurz: Pronounced: proportional to. a ∝ b means: a is b times a fixed number. In Bayesian statistics: posterior ∝ likelihood × prior, up to a factor that scales everything to a sum of 1.
zeichen-proportional.vorsicht: ∝ is not an equals sign. The fixed factor is simply left out.

zeichen-prozent.kurz: Percent is one hundredth, per mille one thousandth. 0.25 is 25 %. The difference between two percentages is given in percentage points.
zeichen-prozent.beispiel: From 10 % to 15 %: plus 5 percentage points, relatively plus 50 %.
zeichen-prozent.vorsicht: “5 %” and “5 percentage points” differ. A percentage without a base (of what?) says little.

zeichen-psi.kurz: Pronounced: psi, usually like sigh. ψ in analysis of variance: a contrast, a weighted sum of group means. Ψ in structural equation models: covariance matrix of the residuals of latent variables. ψ also: influence function of robust M estimators (Huber).
zeichen-psi.beispiel: ψ = μ₁ - (μ₂ + μ₃) / 2 compares group 1 with the average of groups 2 and 3.
zeichen-psi.vorsicht: A contrast ψ makes sense only if the weights add up to 0, here 1 - 1/2 - 1/2 = 0.

zeichen-q.kurz: Cochran's Q measures heterogeneity in meta-analysis; the Cochran Q test for repeated yes-no data has the same name. Ljung-Box Q tests autocorrelation of residuals. q is the studentized range in the Tukey test; q = 1 - p often the complement. Q-Q plots compare quantiles.
zeichen-q.vorsicht: Q and q are not the same in any procedure. Q₁ and Q₃ are the quartiles, not Cochran's Q.

zeichen-r.kurz: Small r is the correlation in the sample (-1 to 1). Capital R is the multiple R, the correlation between observed and predicted values. R² is the coefficient of determination: the share of the variation of y that goes with the model.
zeichen-r.beispiel: r = 0.6: in simple regression R² = r² = 0.36.
zeichen-r.vorsicht: R² is often called “explained share”; that is an association, not a cause. With many predictors R² rises on its own, then the adjusted R² helps.

zeichen-rho.kurz: Pronounced: rho, like row. The correlation in the population (Pearson). Spearman's ρ is the rank correlation (in the sample often rₛ). Reliability (test theory), intraclass correlation and autocorrelation are also often called ρ. ρ looks like a Latin p but is a separate symbol.
zeichen-rho.beispiel: Spearman's ρ = 0.80: whoever ranks high on one list usually ranks high on the other.
zeichen-rho.vorsicht: ρ is not a p value. The p value is a Latin p.

zeichen-s.kurz: Pronounced: s and s squared. s is the standard deviation of the sample, s² its variance. The denominator is n - 1. With subscripts: s_p for the pooled spread of two groups, s_d for the differences of paired values.
zeichen-s.beispiel: Values 4, 6, 8: sum of squares 8, s² = 8 / 2 = 4, s = 2.
zeichen-s.vorsicht: Some calculators and tables also show the spread with n in the denominator. It comes out slightly smaller.

zeichen-sd.kurz: Abbreviation of standard deviation. It says how far values typically spread around the mean. In output also “Std. Deviation” or “Std.-Abw.”.
zeichen-sd.beispiel: M = 52, SD = 8: values typically lie about 8 points from the mean.
zeichen-sd.vorsicht: SD describes the spread of the values. How precisely the mean is determined is told by the standard error (SE).

zeichen-se.kurz: SE stands for standard error: how much a statistic, usually the mean, varies from sample to sample. SEM usually means the standard error of the mean: SE = s / √n. SEM is also the standard error of measurement (test theory) and structural equation modeling.
zeichen-se.vorsicht: SE is not the spread of the measured values, and the SEM of a mean is not the standard error of measurement. Four times the sample size halves the SE.

zeichen-sigma.kurz: Pronounced: sigma. σ is the standard deviation of the population, σ² its variance (σ̂ estimates it); σ with subscript x̄ the standard error of the mean. Σ is the summation sign or the covariance matrix. In “Six Sigma”, σ is the variation of a process.
zeichen-sigma.beispiel: With σ = 15, values typically lie about 15 points from the mean.
zeichen-sigma.vorsicht: σ belongs to the population, s to the sample. The context shows whether Σ sums or means a covariance matrix.

zeichen-ss-ms.kurz: SS (sum of squares) is the sum of squared deviations. MS (mean square) is SS divided by the degrees of freedom. SSB between, SSW within groups, SST total; SSR regression, SSE residual. F = MS between / MS within.
zeichen-ss-ms.beispiel: SS between = 60 with 3 degrees of freedom: MS = 20.
zeichen-ss-ms.vorsicht: SS and MS must not be mixed up. SSR means the regression sum of squares in some books and programs, the residual sum of squares in others.

zeichen-sterne.kurz: Asterisks on numbers mark how small the p value is. Common: * for p < 0.05, ** for p < 0.01, *** for p < 0.001. Some use † for p < 0.10. The legend under the table gives the limits.
zeichen-sterne.vorsicht: The stars do not show how large an effect is; more stars only mean a smaller p. The limits are a habit and not the same everywhere.

zeichen-summe.kurz: Pronounced: sigma, sum. Σ means: add up all values of the series. Start and end are written below and above: Σᵢ₌₁ⁿ xᵢ adds x₁ up to xₙ. The mean is Σx / n.

zeichen-t.kurz: The test statistic of t tests and of coefficient tests in regression. t = (estimate - reference value) / standard error: how many standard errors is the value from the reference value? The degrees of freedom follow in brackets, for example t(24).
zeichen-t.beispiel: Mean difference 3.0 with standard error 1.5: t = 2.0.
zeichen-t.vorsicht: t does not show how large an effect is; the effect size does. The T score of a norm scale (mean 50) is something else.

zeichen-tau.kurz: Pronounced: tau, rhymes with cow. Kendall's τ is a rank correlation. In meta-analysis τ² is the variance of true effects between studies, in multilevel models the variance of random effects. Tau-U measures change in single cases. In test theory τ is the true score.
zeichen-tau.beispiel: Kendall's τ = 0.40 without ties: 70 % of all pairs of cases are ordered the same way, 30 % oppositely, 0.70 - 0.30 = 0.40.
zeichen-tau.vorsicht: τ² in meta-analysis is not the spread of measured values but of the true effects. Less often τ stands for the quantile level in quantile regression, a time shift (lag), a threshold in ordinal models or the precision 1/σ² in Bayesian programs.

zeichen-theta.kurz: Pronounced: theta (THAY-tuh). A general symbol for an unknown parameter of a model; θ̂ is its estimate. Item response theory: person ability. ARIMA: coefficients of the moving averages. Negative binomial regression: dispersion parameter. Θ in structural equation models: covariance matrix of the measurement errors.
zeichen-theta.beispiel: In the Rasch model a person with θ = 0 has ability at the middle level under the usual scaling.
zeichen-theta.vorsicht: θ never denotes one fixed quantity. Always check what the book or program uses it for here.

zeichen-tilde.kurz: Pronounced: tilde. In X ~ N(0, 1) it means “is distributed as”. In model formulas of some programs (y ~ x) it separates the outcome from the predictors. It can also mean “approximately”. Over a letter (x̃) it stands for the median in some books.
zeichen-tilde.beispiel: X ~ N(100, 15²): X follows a normal distribution with mean 100.
zeichen-tilde.vorsicht: The tilde has several meanings depending on the setting. In formulas y ~ x does not mean “y is about x”.

zeichen-u-w-h.kurz: Test statistics of rank tests. U belongs to the Mann-Whitney test (two independent groups), W to the Wilcoxon tests (R calls the statistic of the signed-rank test for paired values V), H to the Kruskal-Wallis test (more groups). They are computed from ranks.
zeichen-u-w-h.beispiel: U₁ + U₂ = n₁ · n₂; with 8 and 9 cases the sum is 72.
zeichen-u-w-h.vorsicht: W also means Shapiro-Wilk W and Kendall's W. The name before the value shows which test is meant.

zeichen-unendlich.kurz: Pronounced: infinity. The symbol for “without limit”. The normal distribution extends from -∞ to +∞. With very many degrees of freedom (df → ∞) the t distribution becomes the normal distribution. Output often shows Inf, for example for the open limit of a one-sided interval.
zeichen-unendlich.beispiel: One-sided 95 % CI [1.2, Inf): no limit upward.
zeichen-unendlich.vorsicht: ∞ is not a number that can be plugged in. Inf in output can also mean that something was divided by 0.

zeichen-ungleich.kurz: Pronounced: not equal, approximately equal, less than or equal, greater than or equal. Also < (less than) and > (greater than). In hypotheses ≠ stands for “some difference”.
zeichen-ungleich.vorsicht: With p < 0.001 the output gives no exact value, only a bound. “≈” means an approximation, not equality.

zeichen-v.kurz: Cramér's V measures the association of two categorical variables in a cross table, from 0 to 1. Pillai's V is the test statistic of MANOVA, the Pillai trace. V can also mean a variance.
zeichen-v.beispiel: For a 2 by 2 table V = 0.10 is often called small, 0.30 medium, 0.50 large; for larger tables these benchmarks are lower.
zeichen-v.vorsicht: V has no direction. Cramér's V and Pillai's V are different quantities.

zeichen-wurzel.kurz: Pronounced: square root. √x is the number that gives x when multiplied by itself. The standard deviation is the square root of the variance: s = √s². The standard error is s / √n.
zeichen-wurzel.vorsicht: Because of √n the standard error falls only slowly: to halve it, one needs four times the sample size.

zeichen-x-quer.kurz: Pronounced: x bar. The arithmetic mean of the sample: sum of all values divided by their number. ȳ (y bar) is the same idea for y. The mean of the population is called μ.
zeichen-x-quer.vorsicht: x̄ is an estimate from the data; the true value μ stays unknown.

zeichen-x-y.kurz: Usually x is the explanatory quantity (predictor, independent variable) and y the explained one (dependent variable). Small letters are concrete values, capital X, Y random variables before observation.
zeichen-x-y.beispiel: y = test points, x = study hours: one pair (x, y) for each person.
zeichen-x-y.vorsicht: Which quantity goes on x and which on y is a decision of the analysis. In correlation both are on equal terms.

zeichen-xi.kurz: Pronounced: xi (ksigh or zigh). In structural equation models an independent latent variable (ξ), Φ its covariance matrix. In extreme value theory the shape parameter ξ of the generalized extreme value and Pareto distributions.

zeichen-y-dach.kurz: Pronounced: y hat. The predicted value of y that the regression equation gives for a particular x. The remainder y - ŷ is the residual.
zeichen-y-dach.beispiel: ŷ = 2 + 0.5 · x. At x = 10, ŷ = 7; the observed value was 8, the residual is 1.
zeichen-y-dach.vorsicht: ŷ is the value expected under the model, not the value that has to occur.

zeichen-z.kurz: The z score says how many standard deviations a value lies from the mean: z = (x - x̄) / s. As a test statistic z = (estimate - reference value) / standard error, compared with the normal distribution; an approximation for large samples.
zeichen-z.vorsicht: Fisher's z' is something else: a transformation of the correlation. And z is not the p value.

zeichen-zeta.kurz: Pronounced: zeta (ZAY-tuh). In structural equation models the residual (the unexplained rest) of a dependent latent variable; Ψ is its covariance matrix. Outside this, ζ is rare in statistics.

zeitabhaengige-kovariate.kurz: A predictor whose value changes during the observation, such as a drug started later. In survival analysis each person is split into time intervals within which the value is constant. The method avoids immortal time bias.
zeitabhaengige-kovariate.beispiel: A person starts a therapy after 8 months. Until month 8 they count as untreated, afterwards as treated. Both periods enter the analysis.
zeitabhaengige-kovariate.vorsicht: A variable influenced by the event itself is not suitable. The dataset needs start and stop times.

zeitreihe.kurz: How does something develop over time? A time series is a sequence of measurements taken one after another at equal intervals. The order carries information, and the values are usually not independent.
zeitreihe.beispiel: Monthly number of visits to a library over four years: 48 values in time order.
zeitreihe.vorsicht: A time series must not be treated like a sample of independent cases. Neighbouring values are often related.

zellhaeufigkeit.kurz: How many cases have exactly this combination? The cell frequency is the number of cases in one cell of the cross table, that is, in one particular row and column at once.
zellhaeufigkeit.beispiel: In the inner district 30 people drive a car: the cell (inner, car) has frequency 30.

zentrierung.kurz: The mean is subtracted from every value. Afterwards the mean is 0 and the spread stays the same. Zero then means “average”.
zentrierung.beispiel: Ages 20, 30, 40, 50 have mean 35. Centered, they become -15, -5, 5, 15.
zentrierung.vorsicht: In a simple regression the slope does not change, but the constant does. It then applies to a person with an average value.

zentroid.kurz: The centre of a group of cases: the point whose coordinates are the means of all the variables of the group. It describes the typical profile of a cluster.
zentroid.beispiel: A cluster of three people with ages 30, 40 and 50 and incomes 2000, 3000 and 4000 has the centroid (40; 3000).
zentroid.vorsicht: The centroid need not be an actual case. With outliers it shifts strongly; the medoid (a real case) is more stable.

ziehen-mit-zuruecklegen.kurz: After each draw the item is put back. The starting position is the same at every draw, so the draws are independent. The same item can occur several times.
ziehen-mit-zuruecklegen.beispiel: Urn with 3 red and 2 blue balls, red twice: (3/5)² = 0.36.

ziehen-ohne-zuruecklegen.kurz: What is drawn stays out. At each draw the starting position changes, so the draws are dependent. Each item occurs at most once, as in most real samples.
ziehen-ohne-zuruecklegen.beispiel: Urn with 3 red and 2 blue balls, red twice: 3/5 · 2/4 = 0.3.
ziehen-ohne-zuruecklegen.vorsicht: If the population is very large compared with the sample, the difference from drawing with replacement is small.

zpl.kurz: An IRT model in which each item has two properties: difficulty b and discrimination a. Discrimination tells how steeply the chance of “right” rises with ability. It extends the Rasch model.
zpl.beispiel: P = 1 / (1 + e^(-a(θ - b))). With θ - b = 0.5 the chance is 0.73 for a = 2 and 0.62 for a = 1.
zpl.vorsicht: Items with a very small a hardly separate people. In a 2PL model the curves of different items can cross.

zufaellige-steigung.kurz: Does a predictor work with different strength in each group? With a random slope, the slope of the line may differ from group to group. These differences are described as a distribution with a variance.
zufaellige-steigung.beispiel: Mean slope 2.0 points per hour of practice, spread 0.5: the slopes of about 95% of classes lie between 1.0 and 3.0.
zufaellige-steigung.vorsicht: Random slopes need enough groups and enough observations per group. Otherwise their variance can hardly be estimated.

zufaelliger-achsenabschnitt.kurz: Does each group have its own starting level? With a random intercept, the starting value of the regression line may differ from group to group. These differences are described as a distribution with a variance.
zufaelliger-achsenabschnitt.beispiel: Overall mean 50 points, spread of school means 4 points: the means of about 95% of schools lie between 42.2 and 57.8 (50 ± 1.96 · 4).
zufaelliger-achsenabschnitt.vorsicht: The intercept refers to the value 0 of the predictors. Without centering, that value often makes little sense.

zufaelliger-effekt.kurz: Do groups depart from the overall picture, and by how much? A random effect treats the departures of groups as draws from a distribution. What is mainly estimated is their variance, not every single group.
zufaelliger-effekt.beispiel: 30 schools are a sample of many possible ones. What is estimated is how much schools differ on average.
zufaelliger-effekt.vorsicht: The word random does not mean something is unexplainable. It means the groups are regarded as a sample from a larger set.

zufaelliger-faktor.kurz: Are the levels a sample from many possible ones? A random factor has levels that were drawn at random from a larger set. The conclusion should refer to the whole set, not just to the levels drawn.
zufaelliger-faktor.beispiel: 8 schools, drawn at random from all schools in a region: school is a random factor.
zufaelliger-faktor.vorsicht: Whether a factor is fixed or random depends on the question, not on the data set. The choice changes the appropriate error term in the test.

zufallsexperiment.kurz: A process whose outcome is not known in advance, but which could be repeated as often as wanted under the same conditions. The possible outcomes are known.
zufallsexperiment.beispiel: Rolling a die twice: there are 36 possible outcomes, and which one occurs is not known beforehand.

zufallsstichprobe.kurz: Who ends up in the sample, and is it decided by chance? In a random sample every element of the population has a known chance greater than 0 of being selected. Only then can errors and intervals be justified.
zufallsstichprobe.beispiel: From a list of 200 employees, 50 are drawn with random numbers. Each person had a chance of 0.25.
zufallsstichprobe.vorsicht: Random is not the same as arbitrary. Approaching passers-by who happen to come along is not a random sample.

zufallsvariable.kurz: A quantity whose value depends on chance. It assigns a number to each outcome of a random experiment. It is usually written with a capital letter such as X.
zufallsvariable.beispiel: X = number of heads in 3 coin tosses. X can be 0, 1, 2 or 3.
zufallsvariable.vorsicht: The random variable is the rule, the observed value is its realisation.

zufallszahl.kurz: A number generated so that it resembles chance. Usually it is a number between 0 and 1 where stretches of equal length are equally likely (uniform distribution). Numbers of other distributions are made from it.
zufallszahl.beispiel: A die can be imitated: a number between 0 and 1 is turned into a whole number from 1 to 6.
zufallszahl.vorsicht: Random numbers from a computer are normally pseudo-random numbers: calculated, not truly random.

zusammengesetzter-index.kurz: Several characteristics are combined into one value, usually by adding or averaging the parts, with weights if needed. Unlike a scale, the parts need not measure the same construct.
zusammengesetzter-index.beispiel: A wealth index combines income, living space and household equipment.
zusammengesetzter-index.vorsicht: The choice of parts and their weights are decisions. An index can hide differences between the parts.

zuteilung-schichten.kurz: The rule for how the sample size is divided among the strata. Proportional: by the size of the stratum. Neyman (optimal): by size times spread of the stratum, so that the variance of the overall result is minimal.
zuteilung-schichten.beispiel: Two strata with 1000 and 2000 units, spreads 10 and 5, n = 100. Proportional: 33 and 67. Neyman: 50 and 50, because 1000·10 = 2000·5.
zuteilung-schichten.vorsicht: Neyman allocation needs knowledge of the spreads. For many characteristics at once there is no single best allocation.

zuteilungsverdeckung.kurz: The assignment to groups stays unknown to those involved until the moment of assignment. It prevents inclusion or assignment from being influenced. This is not the same as blinding, which applies later.
zuteilungsverdeckung.beispiel: The assignment comes by telephone from a central office, only after the person has been enrolled. The list of assignments cannot be seen.
zuteilungsverdeckung.vorsicht: Anyone who knows the list in advance, or uses see-through envelopes, can steer the assignment. Randomisation without concealment loses its value.

zwei-anteile-test.kurz: A test of whether two proportions from independent groups differ. Under the null hypothesis a common proportion is estimated. z = (p₁ - p₂) / √(p̄(1 - p̄)(1/n₁ + 1/n₂)).
zwei-anteile-test.beispiel: 60 of 100 against 45 of 100: common proportion 0.525, standard error 0.0706, z = 0.15/0.0706 = 2.12, p = 0.034.
zwei-anteile-test.vorsicht: The approximation needs large enough numbers in every cell, otherwise Fisher's exact test is better. The test is equivalent to the chi-square test of the two-by-two table.

zweifaktorielle-anova.kurz: Do two groupings act on a measured value at the same time? Two-way analysis of variance tests the influence of each of the two factors (main effect) and whether the two factors influence each other (interaction).
zweifaktorielle-anova.beispiel: Suppose: Plant height by light (low, high) and fertiliser (none, with), 3 plants per cell: main effects F(1, 8) = 108 and 48, interaction F(1, 8) = 12 (p = 0.0085).
zweifaktorielle-anova.vorsicht: If the interaction is important, the main effects alone do not say enough. The effects are then looked at level by level.

zyklisch.kurz: From Greek kyklos: “circle”. Repeating, in cycles. Time series can have cycles. For cyclic quantities such as clock time or direction, the ordinary mean is misleading.
zyklisch.beispiel: The mean of 11 pm and 1 am is midnight, not noon as the ordinary calculation says.

statistisches-modell.kurz: How can a measured value be predicted from other quantities? A statistical model is a rule that predicts a value for every person. What it does not explain remains as error: outcome = model + error. The mean is the simplest model.
statistisches-modell.beispiel: Study hours 4, 10, 2, 9 and 5. Model: the mean 6 for everybody. For the person with 2 hours the error is 2 - 6 = -4.
statistisches-modell.vorsicht: A model is a simplification. It fits better or worse, but it is never the whole reality.

signal-rausch-verhaeltnis.kurz: How clearly does a difference stand out from chance? Many test statistics divide the effect (the signal) by the error (the noise). t, F and χ² have this shape. The larger the ratio, the less chance alone fits.
signal-rausch-verhaeltnis.beispiel: Two groups differ by 4 points, the standard error of the difference is 2: t = 4 : 2 = 2.
signal-rausch-verhaeltnis.vorsicht: A large ratio says nothing about practical importance. With very many people even a tiny effect stands out clearly.

referenzgruppe.kurz: Who is the comparison made with? In a regression model with 0/1 columns the reference group gets the value 0. The constant b₀ is its mean, every b is the difference of another group from it.
referenzgruppe.beispiel: Without training = 0, with training = 1. b₀ is the mean without training, b₁ the difference with training.
