referenzgruppe.vorsicht: Making another group the reference changes b₀ and the signs of the b, but not the predictions.

kennung.kurz: How is a person recognised in the table? The identifier is a column with a unique value per person, for example P01. It lets tables be merged, measurements of the same person be matched and duplicates be found.
kennung.beispiel: P01, P02, P03: in the long form each identifier occurs three times, once per time point.
kennung.vorsicht: Names do not make good identifiers: they are not unique and give the person away. A number without meaning is enough.

codebuch.kurz: What does a number in the table mean? The codebook names for every column what it measures, in which unit or scale, which codes exist and which code stands for missing values. This keeps data readable months later.
codebuch.beispiel: Column sex: 1 = female, 2 = male, 3 = diverse, 99 = no answer (missing).
codebuch.vorsicht: A codebook only helps if it fits the data. Whoever changes codes also changes the codebook.

abgeschnittene-achse.titel: Truncated axis (axis does not start at 0)
abgeschnittene-achse.kurz: How does a chart mislead when its axis does not start at 0? The eye compares the height of the columns, not the numbers. If the lower part is missing, small differences look huge. Columns and bars should therefore start at 0.
abgeschnittene-achse.beispiel: 80% and 90% satisfaction, axis from 70: the columns are 10 and 20 high. B looks twice as high although the value is only 12.5% larger.
abgeschnittene-achse.vorsicht: In dot and line charts the axis may start later when position and course matter, not length. The start should then be clearly visible.
sw: axis does not start at zero

dreidimensionale-diagramme.kurz: Why are three-dimensional columns hard to read? Depth, perspective and shadows change how tall a column looks. The third dimension carries no information but makes reading harder. Flat columns or dots show the same numbers more clearly.
dreidimensionale-diagramme.beispiel: Two columns of equal height look different when one stands further in front.
dreidimensionale-diagramme.vorsicht: A real third quantity is better shown with colour, shape, groups side by side or several charts.

linearitaet.kurz: Is the relationship straight? The assumption of linearity says that the mean of the outcome follows a straight line in the predictor. If it is violated, even the estimated coefficients are biased. A curve in the residuals gives it away.
linearitaet.beispiel: Points against hours: the residuals lie above at the left and right and below in the middle. That is a curve, not a line.
linearitaet.vorsicht: Linear means: linear in the coefficients. Even a curve such as y = b₀ + b₁·x + b₂·x² is a linear model.

gauss-markov-satz.kurz: Why does the method of least squares work so well? The theorem says: with equal spread of the errors and a suitable model form it gives the most precise estimate among all linear, unbiased estimators. The theorem needs no normally distributed errors.
gauss-markov-satz.beispiel: The least-squares line varies less from sample to sample than any other linear, unbiased estimate of the line.
gauss-markov-satz.vorsicht: With unequal spread of the errors the theorem does not hold. The estimate stays unbiased but is no longer the most precise, and the usual standard errors are wrong.

schrumpfung.kurz: Why does a model predict new cases worse than the cases it was built on? Shrinkage is the loss of explanatory power when a model is applied to new data. It grows with the number of predictors and falls with the number of cases.
schrumpfung.beispiel: A model with 10 variables and 25 cases has R² = 0.52 and adjusted R² = 0.18. With new data the second value is more likely to be expected.
schrumpfung.vorsicht: The adjusted R² is only an approximation of the shrinkage. Checking with new data (cross-validation) is more reliable.

korrelationen-vergleichen.kurz: Is the relationship stronger in one group than in another? Both correlations are converted to Fisher z, their difference is divided by the standard error, and the result Z is judged with the normal distribution.
korrelationen-vergleichen.beispiel: r = 0.60 (n = 40) against r = 0.30 (n = 60): Z = 1.82, p = 0.069. The difference is not established with these groups.
korrelationen-vergleichen.vorsicht: The test applies to independent groups. For the same people at two points in time a test for dependent correlations is needed.

spaghetti-diagramm.kurz: How does each single person change over time? A spaghetti plot draws one line through each person's measurements, plus the mean as a thick line. You see whether everyone follows a similar course or whether people differ a lot.
spaghetti-diagramm.beispiel: Ten children, each measured four times: ten lines. If they run almost parallel, the children differ mainly in level, hardly in their course.
spaghetti-diagramm.vorsicht: With very many people the picture becomes a tangle. Then only a selection of lines is drawn and the mean uses everyone.

cousineau-morey-intervall.titel: Cousineau-Morey interval (error bars for repeated measures)
cousineau-morey-intervall.kurz: How certain are the differences between the measurements of the same people? For the Cousineau-Morey interval, the fixed difference between people is removed from each measurement. The bars become narrower and suit a look at change.
cousineau-morey-intervall.beispiel: Reaction time on four days for 18 people: the ordinary 95% interval is about twice as wide as the Cousineau-Morey one.
cousineau-morey-intervall.vorsicht: For looking only, not for testing. The test for repeated measures calculates differently, and overlapping bars are not a test.

innersubjektfaktor.kurz: Which condition or time point is compared within the same people? A within-subject factor is a factor whose levels every person goes through, for example the time points before, after and later. It is also called a repeated-measures factor.
innersubjektfaktor.beispiel: A reading test with the same 16 children at three time points (factor time) and five hours (factor hour): two within-subject factors, 3 × 5 = 15 measurements per child.
innersubjektfaktor.vorsicht: Several measurements of the same person belong together. This is why each effect gets its own error term and sphericity is checked.
innersubjektfaktor.statable: Under the result of the repeated-measures analysis: “Two repeated-measures factors (A × B), also with groups”. Assign the chosen columns to the cells of a grid and name the factors and levels.

zwischensubjektfaktor.kurz: Which grouping compares different people? A between-subject factor divides the people into groups: each person belongs to exactly one level, for example treatment A, B or control. In a mixed design it stands next to a within-subject factor.
zwischensubjektfaktor.beispiel: 16 people in three treatment groups (control, A, B), all measured at three time points: the treatment is the between-subject factor, time the within-subject factor.
zwischensubjektfaktor.vorsicht: Unequal group sizes are possible; the Type III sum of squares then applies, which compares the unweighted group means.
zwischensubjektfaktor.statable: In the method “Does something change over several time points?” choose a grouping column: the result then has time, group and interaction; with two repeated-measures factors seven effects.

dreifach-wechselwirkung.kurz: Does the interaction of A and B look different at each level of C? The three-way interaction (A × B × C) shows exactly that. If it is significant, main effects and two-way interactions do not simply hold for all levels of the third factor.
dreifach-wechselwirkung.beispiel: Yield by nitrogen, phosphorus and potassium (3 plots per combination): three-way interaction F(1, 16) = 1.20; p = .289. Not significant, the two-way effects can be read together for both potassium levels.
dreifach-wechselwirkung.vorsicht: A significant three-way interaction requires reading the two-way effects at each level of the third factor. It is hard to interpret; a chart with one panel per level helps.
dreifach-wechselwirkung.statable: Under the three-way analysis of variance there is a sentence on the three-way interaction and the interaction chart with one panel per level of the third factor; in repeated measures with groups it is the last effect of the table (group × A × B).

kontrast-eigener-fehlerterm.titel: Contrast with its own error term
kontrast-eigener-fehlerterm.kurz: How can a specific comparison be tested in repeated measures without sphericity? For each person the weighted value of their measurements is formed; a t test checks whether it differs from 0 on average. The error term comes from this contrast alone.
kontrast-eigener-fehlerterm.beispiel: 16 people, three time points, linear trend (weights -1, 0, 1): estimate 2.00; t(15) = 4.90; p < .001.
kontrast-eigener-fehlerterm.vorsicht: The test holds for exactly this comparison. With several contrasts the Holm adjustment corrects the p values; contrasts planned beforehand are more credible than ones chosen afterwards.
kontrast-eigener-fehlerterm.statable: Under the result of the repeated-measures analysis: “Contrasts for … with their own error term”. Trend, linear, quadratic, Helmert, repeated or own weights; t, df and p for each contrast, also Holm-adjusted when there are several.

dreifaktorielle-varianzanalyse.kurz: Do three groupings act on a score at the same time? The three-way analysis of variance tests seven effects: three main effects, three two-way interactions and the three-way interaction.
dreifaktorielle-varianzanalyse.beispiel: Yield by nitrogen, phosphorus and potassium (3 plots per combination): only nitrogen is significant, F(1, 16) = 6.16; p = .025. All other effects are not.
dreifaktorielle-varianzanalyse.vorsicht: Every combination of the three factors needs at least one case, and the more cells, the more cases are needed. With a significant three-way interaction the two-way effects are to be read at each level of the third factor.
dreifaktorielle-varianzanalyse.statable: Under the result of the two-way analysis of variance: “Add a third factor”. Seven effects with ηp², a sentence on the three-way interaction and an interaction chart per level of the third factor.

yuen-test.kurz: How do I compare two groups when outliers disturb the mean? The Yuen test compares trimmed means instead of ordinary ones and calculates the spread from winsorized values. It is the robust relative of the Welch t test.
yuen-test.beispiel: ToothGrowth, orange juice against vitamin C, 20% trimmed: difference of the trimmed means 5.12, t(33.49) = 2.29, p = .029, 95% interval [0.57, 9.68].
yuen-test.vorsicht: The trimming is a choice of the analyst and belongs in the report. Trimmed means are compared, not ordinary means.
yuen-test.statable: Under the result of “Do groups differ?” or “Has something changed?” at “Assumption of a normal distribution” choose “Robust (trimmed means)”. Paired values are calculated with the Yuen test for paired values.

robuste-varianzanalyse.kurz: How do I compare three or more groups when the distributions are skewed or have outliers? The robust analysis of variance (t1way) compares trimmed means and needs neither equal spread nor a normal distribution. Pairwise comparisons follow with adjusted p values.
robuste-varianzanalyse.beispiel: PlantGrowth, 20% trimmed: F(2, 9.64) = 8.28, p = .008. The trimmed means are 4.99, 4.55 and 5.46.
robuste-varianzanalyse.vorsicht: It compares trimmed means, not ordinary ones. With very small groups it too remains uncertain.
robuste-varianzanalyse.statable: Under the result of “Do groups differ?” with three or more groups at “Assumption of a normal distribution” choose “Robust (trimmed means)”.

hc4.titel: HC4 standard error (robust for high leverage)
hc4.kurz: How certain is a coefficient when single cases lie far out at the edge? HC4 is a version of the robust standard errors that takes cases with high leverage into account more strongly than HC3. It is more cautious when a few cases largely determine the line.
hc4.beispiel: mtcars, consumption against weight, horsepower and displacement: the standard error of the horsepower term is 0.0144 with HC3 and 0.0261 with HC4.
hc4.vorsicht: Without cases of high leverage HC3 and HC4 are close together. Both fix only unequal spread, not a wrong model.
hc4.statable: Under the linear regression in the section “Robust standard errors” choose the version HC4.

hierarchisches-loglineares-modell.kurz: Which interactions may a model contain? In a hierarchical log-linear model every interaction includes all its parts: with A times B, A and B are in the model too. Only then do the effects stay readable.
hierarchisches-loglineares-modell.beispiel: The model with hair colour × eye colour and hair colour × sex also contains the three main effects, but not eye colour × sex.
hierarchisches-loglineares-modell.vorsicht: A model without a main effect but with the related interaction is not hierarchical and is not calculated.
hierarchisches-loglineares-modell.statable: Under the result of the log-linear models: “More options: choose the model” or the automatic search “backward as SPSS”.

rueckwaerts-eliminierung.kurz: How do you find a simple model that still fits? Backward elimination starts with the largest model and deletes, step by step, the term that contributes least, until every remaining term is demonstrably needed.
rueckwaerts-eliminierung.beispiel: HairEyeColor: hair colour × eye colour × sex is dropped (p = .66), then eye colour × sex (p = .17). Final model: G² = 11.76, df = 12, p = .46.
rueckwaerts-eliminierung.vorsicht: An automatic search depends on chance: with other data a different model can result, and the p values of the final model are too favourable. The result is a suggestion.
rueckwaerts-eliminierung.statable: Under the result of the log-linear models: open “Automatic search: backward as SPSS (hierarchical)” and choose “Calculate backward elimination”.

k-weg-effekt.kurz: From which order on are there no more associations? A k-way effect is an effect in which k variables take part: 1 for main effects, 2 for pairs, 3 for three-way interactions. The k-way table tests whether they can be zero.
k-weg-effekt.beispiel: HairEyeColor: for k = 3 p = .66 (the three-way interaction can be dropped), for k = 2 p < .001 (there are pairwise associations).
k-weg-effekt.vorsicht: “k-way and higher effects” and “exactly k-way effects” are two different tests. A small p means in both: there are such effects.
k-weg-effekt.statable: The table “K-way effects” is in the automatic search “backward as SPSS” under the result of the log-linear models.

diskriminanzfunktion.kurz: Which mix of numbers separates the groups best? A discriminant function is a weighted sum of the numbers. The first separates the groups most strongly, each further one separates what is left. There are at most as many functions as groups minus 1.
diskriminanzfunktion.beispiel: Iris, three species and four measures: two functions. Function 1 carries 99.1% of the separation, function 2 only 0.9%.
diskriminanzfunktion.vorsicht: The sign of a function is arbitrary, SPSS may show the opposite one. What a function stands for is shown by the structure matrix, not by the coefficient alone.
diskriminanzfunktion.statable: Under the result of the discriminant analysis: the coefficients, the share per function and the plot of the function values.

gruppenzentroid.kurz: Where is the centre of a group in the plot of the functions? The group centroid is the mean of the function values of all cases in a group. In the plot it appears as a large point in the middle of the group's cloud of points.
gruppenzentroid.beispiel: Iris: the centroid of the species setosa is at function 1 = 7.608 and function 2 = -0.215.
gruppenzentroid.vorsicht: The centroid need not be a real case. If the centroids lie close together, the functions separate the groups poorly.
gruppenzentroid.statable: In the plot of the discriminant analysis: large points with their own shape per group, plus the table “Group centroids”.

spaltentyp.kurz: Is a column number, text or date? The column type decides how Statable reads the values and what can be calculated with them. Numbers can be analysed, text only counted, a date has an order.
spaltentyp.beispiel: The number 20260905 can be read as the date 5 Sep 2026. The word “four” cannot be turned into a number and becomes missing when the type is changed.
spaltentyp.vorsicht: When the type is changed, values that cannot be converted become missing. Statable first shows in a preview how many there are. Undo is possible.
spaltentyp.statable: On the page “Columns”: change the column type, with a preview and a log entry.

dezimalstellen.kurz: How many places after the point does the column show? The decimal places only set the display. The stored value and all calculations keep their full precision.
dezimalstellen.beispiel: The value 3.14159 with two decimal places is shown as 3.14, but 3.14159 is used in calculations.
dezimalstellen.vorsicht: Fewer displayed places hide differences but do not calculate them away. A value 2.499 and a value 2.501 then both look like 2.50.
dezimalstellen.statable: On the page “Columns”: set the decimal places per column. The values stay unchanged.

teiltext.kurz: A piece of a text. In find and replace a partial text matches every cell in which the piece occurs anywhere. With “whole cell” only a cell that reads exactly like that matches.
teiltext.beispiel: The partial text “Vienna” matches “Vienna”, “Vienna 1” and “New Vienna”. As a whole cell it matches only “Vienna”.
teiltext.statable: In “Find and replace” in the data view: either whole cell or partial text.

wechselwirkung.kurz: Does a factor act the same everywhere? An interaction exists when the effect of one factor depends on the level of the other. In the chart of the cell means the lines then do not run parallel. It is the difference between the simple effects.
wechselwirkung.beispiel: Feedback brings 1 point for easy tasks and 6 points for hard ones: the benefit depends on the type of task.
wechselwirkung.vorsicht: With a clear interaction the main effect describes neither level correctly. Then the simple effects are read.
wechselwirkung.statable: The result of the two-way analysis of variance shows the row of the interaction (A × B); below it are the chart and the simple effects.

differenz-der-differenzen.titel: Difference of the differences (interaction in the 2×2 table)
differenz-der-differenzen.kurz: How is an interaction calculated by hand? In a 2×2 table the difference between the two rows is formed in each column, then the two differences are subtracted from each other. The result is the interaction; 0 means parallel lines.
differenz-der-differenzen.beispiel: With feedback 18 and 15, without 17 and 9: differences 1 and 6, difference of the differences 5.
differenz-der-differenzen.vorsicht: The sign depends on the order. What was subtracted from what has to be stated.

einfache-effekte.kurz: What does a factor bring at each level of the other? A simple effect compares only within one level of the other factor, for example the training separately for low and high prior knowledge. They are read when an interaction exists.
einfache-effekte.beispiel: Training at low prior knowledge: 8 points ahead, at high prior knowledge: 1 point. The main effect of 4.5 fits neither group.
einfache-effekte.vorsicht: Several simple effects are several tests; the level is adjusted for them (for example with Holm).
einfache-effekte.statable: Below the result of the two-way analysis of variance are the simple effects: effect of A at each level of B and the other way round, with Holm correction.

familienfehlerrate.titel: Familywise error rate (false alarm rate across several tests)
familienfehlerrate.kurz: How large is the risk of at least one false alarm when several tests belong together? With m independent tests without a real effect it is 1 minus (1 minus α) to the power of m. It rises with every test and soon lies far above α.
familienfehlerrate.beispiel: 5 tests at 5% each: 1 - 0.95^5 = 0.226, so 22.6%. With 14 tests the risk is already above 50%.
familienfehlerrate.vorsicht: The formula assumes independent tests; for tests on the same data it is only an approximation. The Bonferroni correction α : m keeps the rate at most at α.

varianz-der-differenzen.kurz: What does sphericity look at? For each pair of points in time the difference per person is formed and its variance calculated. Sphericity means that all these variances are similar in size. A large ratio of the largest to the smallest variance shows a violation.
varianz-der-differenzen.beispiel: Variances of the differences 0.5, 2 and 4.5: the ratio 9 clearly speaks against sphericity.
varianz-der-differenzen.vorsicht: The variances of the single points in time are not meant. Only the variances of the differences per person count.

epsilon.kurz: How strongly is sphericity violated? Epsilon lies between the smallest possible value and 1; at 1 it is met. The degrees of freedom of the F test are multiplied by epsilon; the smaller epsilon, the stricter the test. So there is no yes-no decision.
epsilon.beispiel: Epsilon 0.70 with 2 and 20 degrees of freedom: the test uses 1.4 and 14.
epsilon.vorsicht: Epsilon is estimated from the data in the program. Greenhouse-Geisser tends to be too strict, Huynh-Feldt too generous.

greenhouse-geisser-korrektur.kurz: How to deal with violated sphericity? The Greenhouse-Geisser correction estimates epsilon from the data and shrinks the degrees of freedom of the F test with it. The p value becomes larger, the decision more cautious. It can also be reported when sphericity is met, without a pre-test.
greenhouse-geisser-korrektur.beispiel: Epsilon 0.75 with 3 points in time and 20 people: degrees of freedom 2 and 38 become 1.5 and 28.5.
greenhouse-geisser-korrektur.vorsicht: With a very small epsilon the correction is rather strict. The Huynh-Feldt correction is then an alternative.

kontrastwert.titel: Contrast value (weighted sum of the means)
kontrastwert.kurz: How large is the comparison? The contrast value arises by multiplying each group mean by its contrast weight and adding everything up. The weights add up to 0, so the value is a difference. Divided by its standard error it gives t.
kontrastwert.vorsicht: The value depends on the choice of weights. Only contrasts with the same scale of weights can be compared in size.

linearer-trend.kurz: Does the mean rise or fall evenly with the levels? The linear trend is a contrast whose weights form a straight line. With four equally spaced levels they are −3, −1, +1 and +3. It is the first trend of the trend analysis.
linearer-trend.beispiel: Means 10, 14, 15, 17 at zero to three hours: linear contrast value 22, about 93% of the spread between the groups.
linearer-trend.vorsicht: A significant linear trend does not mean the points lie on a straight line. Whether a bend is added is shown by the quadratic trend.

quadratischer-trend.kurz: Does the course of the means bend? The quadratic trend is a contrast that imitates a curve with one bend: first steeper, then flatter, or the other way round. With four equally spaced levels the weights are +1, −1, −1 and +1.
quadratischer-trend.beispiel: Means 10, 14, 15, 17: quadratic contrast value −2, hardly more than chance.
quadratischer-trend.vorsicht: With very unequal spacing of the levels the weights are no longer +1, −1, −1, +1. Then the true spacing has to be used.

forschungskreislauf.titel: Research cycle (observation, theory, hypothesis, prediction, test)
forschungskreislauf.kurz: How does one get from an observation to a test? An observation leads to a theory, from it follows a hypothesis, from that a prediction which is tested with data. The result is again an observation, and the circle starts over.
forschungskreislauf.beispiel: After short nights people seem slower (observation). Theory: lack of sleep lengthens reaction time. Prediction: someone who sleeps 4 hours has the higher mean reaction time than someone who sleeps 8 hours.
forschungskreislauf.vorsicht: The prediction must stand before the measurement and name a direction. Whoever formulates it only after the result is HARKing.

forschungsfreiheitsgrade.kurz: How many paths lead from the same data to a result? Researcher degrees of freedom are the many decisions in collection and analysis: collecting more, excluding values, merging groups, choosing outcomes or control variables. Every path can give a different p.
forschungsfreiheitsgrade.beispiel: 4 open decisions with 2, 3, 2 and 2 options give 2 · 3 · 2 · 2 = 24 analysis paths. If the path with the smallest p is reported, it is no longer a five-percent result.
forschungsfreiheitsgrade.vorsicht: The freedoms work even without intent. A plan fixed beforehand locks them.

registrierter-bericht.kurz: Review before the result is known. In a registered report a journal reviews the question and plan before the data are collected and, given good quality, promises publication regardless of the result. This weakens the incentive for p-hacking and publication bias.
registrierter-bericht.beispiel: A study on the learning program is submitted with hypotheses, 120 people and analysis plan. After acceptance the data are collected, then the report appears, even with an unremarkable result.
registrierter-bericht.vorsicht: A registered report does not replace a good plan. Additional analyses remain allowed if they are marked as post hoc.

optionales-stoppen.kurz: Stopping as soon as the result fits. In optional stopping one tests after every new observation and ends the collection as soon as p is below the limit. That drives the false alarm risk far above 5%. The stopping rule belongs in the plan beforehand.
optionales-stoppen.beispiel: Test after every new person per group, start at 10, upper limit 50: in a simulation this gave a false alarm in about 22% of cases although there was no effect.
optionales-stoppen.vorsicht: Looking in between is not forbidden. It needs a suitable procedure with an adjusted level that is fixed beforehand.

beta-binomial-modell.kurz: How does one combine prior knowledge about a proportion with new data? The prior is a beta distribution Beta(a, b), the data are s successes in n trials. The result is again a beta distribution: Beta(a + s, b + n - s).
beta-binomial-modell.beispiel: Prior Beta(3, 7), then 14 successes in 20 trials: Beta(17, 13) with the mean 17 : 30 = 0.57.
beta-binomial-modell.vorsicht: The result depends on the prior. Recalculate with a weak prior such as Beta(1, 1) and report both values.

prior-staerke.kurz: How much does the prior knowledge weigh? For a beta distribution Beta(a, b) the strength is a + b: the prior counts as much as a + b earlier observations. The larger the strength, the more new data it takes to shift it.
prior-staerke.beispiel: Beta(3, 7) weighs like 10 observations, Beta(1, 1) like 2. With 20 new people the data determine the result more strongly than the weak prior, but only twice as strongly as the prior Beta(3, 7).
prior-staerke.vorsicht: The strength is a decision. It should be stated openly.

refi-qda.kurz: An open exchange format for qualitative projects. Programs such as MAXQDA, ATLAS.ti, NVivo and QualCoder use it to save texts, codes, codings, coders, memos and cases in one file ending in .qdpx.
refi-qda.beispiel: A team codes in MAXQDA, exports the project as .qdpx and reads it into Statable to check the agreement of the coders.
refi-qda.vorsicht: Every program fills the format a little differently. That is why Statable shows after reading what it could not take over.
refi-qda.statable: Page “Interviews”, section “Read in a project from MAXQDA, ATLAS.ti, NVivo or QualCoder”.

segment.kurz: In qualitative coding, a marked section of a text with a start and an end position. A segment can carry one or more codes. In Statable positions are counted in characters, and the end is not part of the segment any more.
segment.beispiel: In the interview the sentence “Every Sunday I write down what is coming up that week.” is marked and given the code “Planning”.
segment.vorsicht: Changing the text afterwards shifts the positions. That is why pseudonymising is the only text change Statable allows for documents with segments.

ueberlappung.kurz: How strongly two marked passages coincide. Statable divides the shared text by the text of both together: 100 % means the same place, 0 % means no shared character.
ueberlappung.beispiel: A marks 100 characters, B the same except the last 20. 80 characters are shared out of 100 together: overlap 80 %.
ueberlappung.vorsicht: Whether two passages count as the same depends on the chosen threshold (default 90 %). The threshold therefore always belongs with the figure.
ueberlappung.statable: Page “Interviews”, section “Do we code the same?”: threshold as a select field.

quantitizing.kurz: Turning qualitative findings into numbers, for example “code occurs in the case” as 1 or the number of passages. Coded interviews then become a table that can be calculated further.
quantitizing.beispiel: Three coded interviews become a case-code matrix: one row per case, one column per code, cell 0 or 1.
quantitizing.vorsicht: 0 only means “not coded”, not “does not apply”. With few, purposefully chosen cases a p-value says little.
quantitizing.statable: Page “Interviews”, section “How often does which code occur?”.

pseudonymisierung.kurz: Names and other details are replaced by placeholders. A key list can make the persons recognisable again, which is why pseudonymised data remain personal data.
pseudonymisierung.beispiel: “Anna” becomes “[Person 1]” throughout the project. The list “[Person 1] = Anna” is kept apart.
pseudonymisierung.vorsicht: Pseudonymised is not anonymous. Occupations, places and times together can still make persons recognisable.

indirekter-identifikator.titel: Indirect identifier (detail that only identifies in combination)
indirekter-identifikator.kurz: A detail that reveals nobody on its own but makes a person recognisable together with others, for example a rare occupation in a small town or a unique experience. Direct identifiers, by contrast, are names or addresses.
indirekter-identifikator.beispiel: “Teacher at the only school in the village who stood in for the head in 2019” leads to one person although no name is given.
indirekter-identifikator.vorsicht: No rule in Statable recognises this. That is another reason why interviews must be read in full and such clues rephrased.

zuordnungsliste.kurz: The list that assigns the original text to each placeholder, for example “[Person 1] = Anna”. Whoever has it together with the data can recognise the persons again. It should therefore be kept apart and preferably encrypted.
zuordnungsliste.beispiel: Statable creates it as a separate CSV file (replacement, original, kind, count), never in the project file.
zuordnungsliste.vorsicht: Without the list the assignment cannot be restored. If it is lost, the data can practically no longer be traced back.
zuordnungsliste.statable: Page “Interviews”, button “Save key list” after replacing.

konsens.kurz: Two coders discuss every disagreement and agree on a joint coding, with a reason. The result is a new, third coding; the two original ones are kept.
konsens.beispiel: A gave “Time pressure”, B “Strain/high”. The team decides “keep both” and writes the rule into the codebook.
konsens.vorsicht: The match with the consensus is no longer a quality measure but shows how much has changed. Reliability is shown by the agreement before the discussion.

kodieren.kurz: Giving a passage of text a code that says what it is about. This turns many pages of text into an ordered collection of evidence per topic. Deductive means the codes are fixed beforehand. Inductive means they come out of the material.
kodieren.beispiel: The sentence “Every Sunday I write down what is coming up.” gets the code “Planning”.
kodieren.vorsicht: Coding is interpretation, not measuring. That is why a clear coding guide and a second person who codes the same passages help.

code-qualitativ.kurz: A short name a passage of text receives, such as “Time pressure”. Codes can be ordered in a tree with parent codes and sub-codes. Every code needs a definition so that others apply it in the same way.
code-qualitativ.beispiel: Parent code “Strain” with the sub-codes “Time pressure” and “Money worries”.
code-qualitativ.vorsicht: Too many codes make coding confusing. It is better to start with a few and refine later.

kategorie-qualitativ.kurz: A topic to which several passages are assigned. In qualitative content analysis a category is a code with a definition and rules. A category system orders all categories, often as a tree.
kategorie-qualitativ.beispiel: Category “Support”: passages about help from family, friends or lecturers.
kategorie-qualitativ.vorsicht: Categories should not overlap. If a passage fits two, the definition is often unclear.

codebaum.kurz: The codes of a project, ordered like folders: the big topics on top, the finer ones beneath. A parent code can be “not codable” and only serve to order. Moving a code changes only the order, not the codings already given.
codebaum.beispiel: Strain (parent code) with Time pressure and Money worries beneath it; next to it Support.
codebaum.vorsicht: If a code is deleted, its passages lose that code. Sub-codes move up one level.

memo-qualitativ.kurz: Your own note on a passage, a document, a code or the whole project. Memos record what you notice while coding: questions, ideas, doubts. They are part of the analysis and do not belong in the text.
memo-qualitativ.beispiel: On a passage: “She says time pressure here but probably means money worries. Check with the code.”
memo-qualitativ.vorsicht: Memos with names or hints about people are data and must be protected just like the text.

fallvariable.kurz: A fact about a person or a case, for example age or field of study. With case variables the evidence for a code can be filtered by group, and qualitative and quantitative data can be linked later.
fallvariable.beispiel: Variable “Semester” with the value 3 for Anna and 5 for Ben. Evidence for “Time pressure” can then be shown for semester 5 only.
fallvariable.vorsicht: With very few cases, group comparisons are only hints, not proof.

fall-kategorie-matrix.kurz: A table: every row is a case (usually one person), every column a code. The cell holds what this person said on this topic: a summary in your own words, with the evidence. This allows comparing people and topics.
fall-kategorie-matrix.beispiel: Row “Anna”, column “Time pressure”: “Too few days before exams, still plans every Sunday.” (2 pieces of evidence)
fall-kategorie-matrix.vorsicht: The summary is written by a person. It is description, not yet interpretation. The code matrix, by contrast, only counts how often a code occurs.
fall-kategorie-matrix.statable: Page “Coding”, section “Analysis”, view “What does each case say on each topic? (case-by-category matrix)”.

framework-analyse.kurz: A procedure of qualitative analysis in seven stages: transcribing, getting familiar, coding, developing a category system, applying it, charting the statements into the matrix and finally interpreting. It suits interviews on similar topics and teams in which not everybody has experience in qualitative work.
framework-analyse.beispiel: Ten interviews on studying are coded; each person and topic gets a short summary; only afterwards are patterns and differences interpreted.
framework-analyse.vorsicht: The matrix looks like a table from statistics, but it is not one. Interpretation needs qualitative care. Gale and others (2013) describe the procedure.
framework-analyse.statable: Page “Coding”: the view “case-by-category matrix” is the stage “charting into the matrix”.

fallzusammenfassung.kurz: A short text in your own words that records what a case said on a topic. It balances shortening against the meaning of the statement and points to fitting evidence. It describes first and does not yet interpret.
fallzusammenfassung.beispiel: Anna, “Time pressure”: “Feels pressure before exams, still organises the week.”
fallzusammenfassung.vorsicht: Statable summarises nothing. The summary is written by a person and saved by them in the project.
fallzusammenfassung.statable: Page “Coding”, view “case-by-category matrix”: choose a cell, field “Summary”, “Save”.

code-landkarte.kurz: A picture in which every code is a point. Codes that often occur in the same documents lie close together. It is based on the Jaccard distance over the documents, drawn with multidimensional scaling (MDS). Only the position relative to each other counts, the axes mean nothing.
code-landkarte.beispiel: “Time pressure” and “Exhaustion” lie close together because they appear in almost the same interviews.
code-landkarte.vorsicht: Occurring together does not mean the topics are related. The picture can over-interpret; that is why the goodness of fit and a table of the distances stand beside it.
code-landkarte.statable: Page “Coding”, view “Which codes occur together? (code map)”: “Draw map”.

tf-idf.titel: TF-IDF (word similarity, rare words count more)
tf-idf.kurz: A measure of how similar two texts are in their words. A word counts more when it occurs often in the text and is rare in the whole material. Common words such as “and” or “I” hardly count. Statable uses it for “Similar passages”.
tf-idf.beispiel: Two sentences that both contain “exam” and “side job” are more similar than two sentences that share only “I” and “and”.
tf-idf.vorsicht: Only words are compared, not meaning. The measure does not recognise negation (“not overwhelmed”) or words with the same sense (“stress”, “pressure”). It does not suggest codes.
tf-idf.statable: Page “Coding”, view “Where is there something similar? (similar passages)”, switch “Offer similar passages”.

dokument-uebersicht.titel: Document overview (what is coded where in this document?)
dokument-uebersicht.kurz: A list for one document: for each paragraph the codes given there and the number of passages. A button jumps to the paragraph in the text. This shows at a glance where much is coded and where nothing is.
dokument-uebersicht.vorsicht: The list shows only what was coded. A paragraph without a code can still be important; the switch “Also show paragraphs without a code” is there for that.
dokument-uebersicht.statable: Page “Coding”, view “What is coded where? (document overview)”.

spearman-brown-formel.kurz: How reliable would the whole scale be if only the halves are known? The Spearman-Brown formula steps the correlation of the two test halves up to full length: 2r / (1 + r). It also tells how reliability changes when a test becomes longer or shorter.
spearman-brown-formel.beispiel: The halves correlate r = 0.60. Stepped up: 2 × 0.60 / (1 + 0.60) = 0.75.
spearman-brown-formel.vorsicht: The formula assumes that both halves measure equally well. There is a variant for halves of unequal length.
spearman-brown-formel.statable: Card “How reliably does my scale measure?”, section “How reliable is the scale when it is cut in half? (split-half reliability, Spearman-Brown)”: “Calculate split-half”. The table shows Spearman-Brown for equal and for unequal length.

guttman-split-half.kurz: A second step-up in split-half reliability. It does not assume that both halves have the same spread. It is calculated from the variances of the two halves and the variance of the whole sum.
guttman-split-half.beispiel: Variances 4.0 and 5.0 for the halves, 14.0 for the whole sum: 2 × (1 − 9.0 / 14.0) = 0.71.
guttman-split-half.vorsicht: If the halves have the same spread the value equals Spearman-Brown; otherwise it is lower.
guttman-split-half.statable: The table of the split-half result has the row “Guttman split-half” below the two Spearman-Brown values.

retest-korrelation.kurz: How closely are the two measurements of the same people related? The test-retest correlation r_tt is the Pearson correlation between the first and the second measurement. It shows only whether the order of the people stays, not whether the values stay the same.
retest-korrelation.beispiel: Everyone rises by 10 points: r_tt = 1.00, but the values did not stay the same.
retest-korrelation.vorsicht: For test-retest reliability the ICC for absolute agreement is the recommendation. r_tt is the value the Reliable Change Index needs.
retest-korrelation.statable: Card “Do ratings agree?” with exactly two number columns: the sentence on the ICC contains “Test-retest correlation r_tt = …”.

thema-qualitativ.kurz: A pattern of meaning that the person analysing builds from several codes. A theme is more than a heading: it says something about the data. In Statable a theme has a history and is never silently merged with another.
thema-qualitativ.beispiel: The codes "time pressure", "exhaustion" and "no breaks" become the theme "constant strain without recovery".
thema-qualitativ.vorsicht: A theme is built by the person, not found in the text like a discovery. It is also not the subject of conversation ("topic of the interview").

themenanalyse-reflexiv.kurz: A method of qualitative research after Braun and Clarke. The person codes texts, builds themes from them and records how their own perspective shapes the interpretation. The themes are their result, not a measurement.
themenanalyse-reflexiv.beispiel: From twelve interviews about studying alongside a job, a researcher builds three themes and notes in the journal how her own work experience steers the selection.
themenanalyse-reflexiv.vorsicht: Not to be confused with a content analysis with a fixed category system. Agreement between several coders is not regarded as a quality measure in this method.

reflexives-tagebuch.kurz: Notes in which the person records how their own attitude, assumptions and decisions shape the analysis. In Statable it is a kind of memo (a note made while coding).
reflexives-tagebuch.beispiel: "I read the statement about breaks immediately as overload because I was often overloaded myself. Check an alternative reading."
reflexives-tagebuch.vorsicht: It makes the interpretation traceable. It does not automatically make it correct.

kodierphase.kurz: The stage at which a code arose in grounded theory: open (breaking up the text and naming), axial (relating codes to each other) or selective (organising everything around a core category). In Statable the phase can be noted on the code.
kodierphase.beispiel: The code "time pressure" arises in open coding and is later linked axially with "exhaustion".

theoretisches-memo.kurz: A note recording how codes or categories might be connected and what idea lies behind this. It is provisional and is revised as the comparison continues. Especially common in grounded theory.
theoretisches-memo.beispiel: "Time pressure seems to intensify exhaustion, but perhaps only when nobody can cover. Look for cases with cover."

framework-matrix.kurz: A table with the cases in the rows and the themes in the columns. Each cell holds a summary of what this case says about this theme. Cases and themes can then be read side by side.
framework-matrix.beispiel: Row "Interview 4", column "constant strain": "Keeps working in the evening and sees no choice."
framework-matrix.vorsicht: The summaries are written by the person. Statable does not summarise by itself.

interpretative-phaenomenologische-analys.kurz: A method that aims to understand how people experience and make sense of an event. Each case is interpreted on its own first, and only then are cases compared. The researcher interprets the interviewee's interpretation ("double hermeneutic").
interpretative-phaenomenologische-analys.beispiel: Four interviews with people after a diagnosis: interview 1 is interpreted completely, then interview 2 and so on, and the themes are compared afterwards.
interpretative-phaenomenologische-analys.vorsicht: The abbreviation IPA also stands for the phonetic alphabet. Here it means the method of analysis.

einzelfall-modus.kurz: A view in Statable that shows only the chosen case. The other cases are hidden. This helps with methods such as IPA, which interpret each case on its own before cases are compared.
einzelfall-modus.beispiel: In single-case mode for interview 2, interviews 1 and 3 cannot be seen. Only after switching back can the cases be compared.
einzelfall-modus.vorsicht: A view, not a method of analysis. It has nothing to do with the single-case analysis of statistics (few people, many measurements).

randnotiz.kurz: A note at the edge of a piece of text. In IPA there are three layers: descriptive (what is said), linguistic (how it is said, such as word choice or pauses) and conceptual (what it might mean).
randnotiz.beispiel: For "I just functioned": descriptive - talks about the time after the diagnosis; linguistic - "functioned" sounds like a machine; conceptual - possibly distance from one's own experience.

feinstrukturanalyse.kurz: A method of interpretive social research that interprets a short extract of text piece by piece (Froschauer and Lueger). Each unit of meaning gets several readings, and the following text is looked at only afterwards.
feinstrukturanalyse.beispiel: The first sentence of an interview is broken into short units. Interpretations are written for each unit before the next one is read.
feinstrukturanalyse.vorsicht: The result remains an interpretation. It is tested against the further text and may change.

sinneinheit.kurz: A short piece of text marked off as one unit of meaning. It can be a word, a group of words or a sentence. The person sets the boundaries.
sinneinheit.beispiel: "I have | actually | never | talked | about it" is divided into five units.
sinneinheit.vorsicht: A unit of meaning is not the same as a sentence. It can be shorter or longer.

lesart.kurz: One possible interpretation of a unit of meaning. Several readings are noted for each unit, including opposing ones. Later units show which reading holds, which is rejected and which stays open.
lesart.beispiel: "That is none of my business" can be read as setting a boundary, as consideration or as embarrassment.
lesart.vorsicht: A reading is a proposal that is tested against the text. It is not a statement about what the person "really" meant.

zwischenfazit.kurz: A summary of the state so far, supported by passages of text: which patterns appear and which readings have held so far. It is written after a series of units and remains provisional.
zwischenfazit.beispiel: After eight units: "The speaker presents herself as an observer (units 3, 5, 7); the reading withdrawal has held so far."

spaltensatz.kurz: The columns that a sequence analysis has in Statable. The choices are fine structure, IPA (descriptive, linguistic, conceptual), one free column or a set of your own. The set determines what kind of interpretation is entered.
spaltensatz.beispiel: Anyone working in the IPA way picks the set with three margin-note columns.

sequenzanalyse-qualitativ.kurz: A text is interpreted step by step in its order, without reading ahead. Each step supports or corrects the interpretations so far. Fine-structure analysis is one example.
sequenzanalyse-qualitativ.beispiel: The opening of a conversation is interpreted utterance by utterance: what could follow this utterance, and what actually follows?
sequenzanalyse-qualitativ.vorsicht: Not to be confused with the sequence analysis of statistics, which describes sequences of events such as life courses.

folgetext-verdecken.titel: Hide the following text (do not read ahead)
folgetext-verdecken.kurz: A setting in which only the text up to the current unit is visible. Readings are then formed before the continuation is known. The later text is not displayed.
folgetext-verdecken.beispiel: At the third unit only the text up to the third unit can be seen.

interviewprotokoll.kurz: Notes made straight after an interview: place, mood, interruptions, anything striking and first impressions. They add to the transcript what the recording does not show.
interviewprotokoll.beispiel: "Conversation in the office, door open, interrupted twice. She spoke more quietly when it came to the dismissal."
interviewprotokoll.vorsicht: In English the interview guide is often also called an "interview protocol". Here the notes made afterwards are meant.

gedaechtnisprotokoll.kurz: A record that the person writes from memory after a conversation or observation because nothing was recorded. The sooner it is written, the less is lost.
gedaechtnisprotokoll.beispiel: After a conversation in the corridor the researcher writes down that same evening what was said.
gedaechtnisprotokoll.vorsicht: It is a recollection, not a verbatim quotation. Wording should be marked as verbatim only when the person is sure.

feldnotizen.kurz: Notes made during an observation, usually as keywords first and worked out later. They record what was seen, heard and experienced, and, kept apart from that, first interpretations.
feldnotizen.beispiel: "9:40 - Three people waiting at the counter, nobody speaks." Kept apart, as interpretation: tension?

einwilligung-prozess.kurz: Consent is not given just once at the start. It can be given in steps, changed and partly withdrawn. Statable keeps a history for this.
einwilligung-prozess.beispiel: A person allows the analysis of her interview and later withdraws the use of verbatim quotations.
einwilligung-prozess.vorsicht: What applies legally depends on the country and the institution.

aenderungsprotokoll-codebuch.kurz: A list recording when a code was created, renamed, moved or merged. It makes it traceable how the coding system changed. It never contains text from the documents.
aenderungsprotokoll-codebuch.beispiel: "Code 'stress' renamed 'time pressure' because it only means deadlines."

ki-offenlegung.kurz: The statement of whether and for what AI tools were used in an analysis, for example for transcribing or translating. Statable itself uses no AI.
ki-offenlegung.beispiel: "The transcript was drafted with a speech recognition tool and corrected by hand."

arbeitsweise-verfahren.titel: Working approach (method) in the coding workspace
arbeitsweise-verfahren.kurz: A switch that changes the order of the areas and what the view starts with, to suit the chosen method, such as reflexive thematic analysis. It never changes the data.
arbeitsweise-verfahren.beispiel: When switching from one approach to another, codes and evidence stay unchanged. Only the arrangement changes.

methodenanhang.kurz: A text for the appendix of a report that records the procedure: approach, changes to the codebook, themes and use of AI. Statable produces it as a Word file.
methodenanhang.beispiel: The appendix states that the codebook was revised in four steps and that no AI tool was used.

berichtshilfe.kurz: A checklist showing which points a report on qualitative research should mention. For each point the person marks fulfilled, open or not applicable. There is no overall score.
berichtshilfe.beispiel: The point "Who conducted the interviews?" is backed up with a location in the report.
berichtshilfe.vorsicht: If all points are fulfilled, that only means the study is reported. It does not prove the study is good.

coreq.kurz: A list of 32 items ("Consolidated criteria for reporting qualitative research") on what a report on interviews and focus groups should mention. It is meant for reporting, not for judging.
coreq.beispiel: One item asks whether the researchers disclose their role and their closeness to the topic.
sw: Consolidated criteria for reporting qualitative research

srqr.kurz: A list of 21 items ("Standards for reporting qualitative research") on what a report on qualitative research in general should mention, not only on interviews. It is meant for reporting, not for judging.
srqr.beispiel: One item asks how the data were collected and analysed and why this approach was chosen.

meta-inferenz.kurz: A conclusion that arises only from the numbers and the texts together and from neither alone. It is the aim of integration in mixed-methods studies.
meta-inferenz.beispiel: The survey shows that few students seek help, and interviews name shame as one reason. Meta-inference: counselling services may fail less for lack of knowledge than because of the threshold to use them.
meta-inferenz.vorsicht: The meta-inference is also an interpretation. The person is responsible for it.

passung-mixed.titel: Fit of numbers and texts (confirmation, expansion, discordance)
passung-mixed.kurz: Records how numbers and texts relate: they confirm each other, expand on each other or are discordant. This distinction comes from Fetters and colleagues.
passung-mixed.beispiel: The survey shows mostly satisfaction, while several interviews describe dissatisfaction: discordance.
passung-mixed.vorsicht: Discordance is a reason to investigate further. It is not a flaw of the study.

design-steckbrief.kurz: A short description of a mixed-methods design in Morse's notation: capital letters for the main part, lower case for the supplementary part, an arrow for in sequence, a plus sign for at the same time.
design-steckbrief.beispiel: QUAN → qual means: first a survey as the main part, then interviews as a supplement.

simple-matching-koeffizient.kurz: A similarity measure for two yes/no columns: the share of cases in which both agree, whether both are "yes" or both are "no".
simple-matching-koeffizient.beispiel: 10 cases: 3 with both codes, 5 with neither, 2 with only one. The coefficient is (3 + 5) / 10 = 0.8.
simple-matching-koeffizient.vorsicht: It counts joint absence. With rare codes the similarity then looks large. The Jaccard measure does not count joint absence.

instrumentenentwicklung.titel: Instrument development (from codes to questionnaire items)
instrumentenentwicklung.kurz: In mixed-methods studies: qualitative findings give rise to questions for a questionnaire (items), which is then tested. Statable takes over codes and themes as item suggestions in the questionnaire plan.
instrumentenentwicklung.beispiel: From the code "shame about asking" comes the item "I find it uncomfortable to ask for help."

mmat.kurz: A checklist for appraising the quality of studies with qualitative, quantitative and mixed parts. In Statable it serves for self-appraisal of one's own study. There is no overall score.
mmat.beispiel: The checklist asks, for example, whether the integration of the qualitative and quantitative parts was justified and carried out.

gramms.kurz: A list of six items ("Good reporting of a mixed methods study") on what a report on a mixed-methods study should mention. It is meant for reporting, not for judging.
gramms.beispiel: One item asks why mixed methods were chosen and how the two parts were brought together.
sw: Good reporting of a mixed methods study

selbstpruefung-mixed.kurz: The person goes through a checklist for their own study and records yes, no, unclear or not applicable for each item. Statable calculates no overall score.
selbstpruefung-mixed.beispiel: For the item "rationale for mixed methods" the entry is "yes" with a pointer to the methods section.

q-sort.kurz: Sorting statements into a grid by agreement, usually with a fixed number of statements per place. One person's result is called a Q sort. It is the basis of Q methodology.
q-sort.beispiel: 30 statements are placed on a grid from -4 to +4: few at the ends, many in the middle.
q-sort.vorsicht: The distribution is prescribed. Not every statement can stand at the top; the person ranks in comparison.

begriffskarte.kurz: A group collects statements on a topic, and each person puts them on piles by similarity. This yields a map on which statements that were often put together lie close to each other.
begriffskarte.beispiel: Twelve people sort 40 ideas for improving teaching onto piles. The map shows which ideas belong together for the group.
begriffskarte.vorsicht: Closeness on the map only means that many people put the statements together. The axes have no meaning of their own.

wortliste.kurz: A table showing which words occur in one or more texts and how often. It only counts and does not say what the words mean.
wortliste.beispiel: In the interviews "time" occurs more often than "money".
wortliste.vorsicht: The most frequent words are often filler words (stop words). Whether to hide them is a decision that has to be disclosed. Statable shows the switch and the list.

kwic.kurz: KWIC stands for "key word in context": all places where a search word occurs are shown one below the other, with the words before and after. This shows how the word is used.
kwic.beispiel: Search word "pressure": "... I feel pressure when ..." and "... pressure from the manager ...".
kwic.vorsicht: Only an excerpt is read. The meaning often becomes clear only in the whole text.

zweistufige-kleinste-quadrate.kurz: An estimation method for the case that a cause may itself be influenced by the outcome. Stage 1: the cause is predicted with the help of instruments. Stage 2: the outcome is explained by the predicted cause.
zweistufige-kleinste-quadrate.beispiel: Does the price of cigarettes affect sales? The price is first explained by the tax (instrument), then sales are explained by the price predicted in this way.
zweistufige-kleinste-quadrate.vorsicht: A weak instrument makes the estimate unreliable. A first-stage F statistic below about 10 is often regarded as a warning sign; Statable always shows it.

partialkorrelationsnetz.kurz: A picture in which each column is a node and each line a partial correlation: the relationship of two columns once all the others are taken out. If a line is missing, no direct relationship between the two can be seen.
partialkorrelationsnetz.beispiel: Sleep problems and tiredness are connected, and so are tiredness and concentration. Between sleep problems and concentration the line is missing: the relationship runs via tiredness.
partialkorrelationsnetz.vorsicht: The lines say nothing about direction or cause. Chance lines also occur; that is why Statable shows bootstrap intervals.
